After Task 5's `backfillOp`'s closing `}`, insert:

```js
/** A writer's refusal of an advance file it cannot read: the verb rewrites that file and will not overwrite one it
 *  cannot read. */
const refuseAdvance = (err, opName, id) => refuse(1, err[0], `${err[1]} ${opName} rewrites account "${id}"'s `
  + 'advance file and will not overwrite one it cannot read. Fix it by hand, or delete it (the next write re-creates '
  + 'it from the registry, with no holds and no history), then re-run. Nothing was written.');

/** `hold <class>` and `release <class>` (auto-advance spec §2.7, D3, D12): set or clear a class's hold, the one
 *  brake the automatic advance honours. They touch only the lane's advance file — the registry, its pins and the
 *  lane's settings stay as they are, so nothing re-materialises. A hold records WHEN (`now()`) and the ACT that set
 *  it, `hand` here (D-5190). A second hold, or a release of a class not held, changes nothing
 *  and says so (`changed: false`); a pending intent found on the way is still settled and written. */
function holdOp(opName, a, account, registry, catalogue, win) {
  const loaded = advanceForWrite(a.id, registry);
  if (loaded.err !== undefined) return refuseAdvance(loaded.err, opName, a.id);
  const c = loaded.advance.classes[a.class];
  let changed = false;
  if (opName === 'hold' && c.hold === null) {
    c.hold = { at: now(), by: 'hand' };
    changed = true;
  }
  if (opName === 'release' && c.hold !== null) {
    c.hold = null;
    changed = true;
  }
  if (changed || loaded.dirty) {
    const w = writeAdvance(a.id, loaded.advance);
    if (w !== null) return refuse(1, w[0], w[1]);
  }
  out({ ok: true, op: opName, class: a.class, changed, ...describe(account, registry, catalogue, win) });
  return 0;
}

/**
 * `revert <class>` (auto-advance spec §2.7): put back the model the class had before its last automatic advance
 * (`previous`, with its effort level — D-5189 — through `resolveEffort` when that model no
 * longer offers it), and hold the class there so the next hour cannot move it again. One act.
 *  - REFUSED, writing nothing: no advance on record (`no-previous`); a previous model the catalogue no longer lists
 *    (`previous-not-in-catalogue`); one another class pins now (`previous-taken`: a revert never empties another
 *    class); a registry the validator or the renderer refuses (`registry-invalid`, `unroutable-lane`).
 *  - THE BRAKE FIRST (D-5206): the hold reaches the advance file before the registry moves, so a
 *    revert stopped anywhere leaves the class held, never free to be advanced again. It is `{at: now(), by:
 *    'revert'}` whatever hold stood before, a hand one included: a hold records the act that set it last
 *    (D-5190), and the panel and doctor name that act.
 *  - COMMIT AFTER MATERIALISE, as an advance commits (D21): `previous` is cleared and the move recorded only once the
 *    lane's files are rendered. A materialise that fails puts the old registry back and renders it again, and the
 *    refusal says the class is held.
 */
function revertOp(a, account, registry, catalogue, win) {
  const loaded = advanceForWrite(a.id, registry);
  if (loaded.err !== undefined) return refuseAdvance(loaded.err, 'revert', a.id);
  const adv = loaded.advance;
  const c = adv.classes[a.class];
  const from = registry.classes[a.class];
  if (c.previous === null) {
    return refuse(1, 'no-previous',
      `account "${a.id}"'s ${a.class} class has no automatic advance on record, so there is nothing to revert to. `
      + `'ccrc models ${a.id} set-class ${a.class} <modelId|none>' sets it by hand. Nothing was written.`);
  }
  const to = c.previous.model;
  const rowOf = (id) => (id === null || catalogue === null ? undefined : catalogue.models.find((m) => m.id === id));
  if (to !== null && catalogue !== null && rowOf(to) === undefined) {
    return refuse(1, 'previous-not-in-catalogue',
      `${a.class}'s previous model "${to}" is no longer in account "${a.id}"'s catalogue, so it cannot be put back. `
      + `'ccrc models ${a.id} show' lists what the lane offers, and set-class picks one by hand. Nothing was written.`);
  }
  const taker = to === null ? undefined : CLASSES.find((o) => o !== a.class && registry.classes[o] === to);
  if (taker !== undefined) {
    return refuse(1, 'previous-taken',
      `${a.class}'s previous model "${to}" is the ${taker} class's model now, and a revert never empties another `
      + `class. Move ${taker} first, or set ${a.class} by hand. Nothing was written.`);
  }
  const next = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(registry));
  next.classes[a.class] = to;
  const effortFrom = isObj(registry.effort) && typeof registry.effort[a.class] === 'string'
    ? registry.effort[a.class] : null;
  let effortTo = c.previous.effort;
  const toRow = rowOf(to);
  if (effortTo !== null && toRow !== undefined && toRow.efforts.length > 0 && !toRow.efforts.includes(effortTo)) {
    effortTo = resolveEffort({ stored: effortTo, oldEfforts: rowOf(from)?.efforts ?? null, newEfforts: toRow.efforts })
      ?? null;
  }
  if (effortTo === null) {
    if (isObj(next.effort)) {
      delete next.effort[a.class];
      if (Object.keys(next.effort).length === 0) delete next.effort;
    }
  } else {
    next.effort = { ...(isObj(next.effort) ? next.effort : {}), [a.class]: effortTo };
  }
  // An explicit discovery list has to offer what a class routes to: set-class's own rule, and like it never on an
  // openrouter lane, whose list grows only through `discovery add`'s whitelist check.
  if (to !== null && registry.probe !== 'openrouter' && Array.isArray(next.discovery) && !next.discovery.includes(to)) {
    next.discovery = [...next.discovery, to];
  }
  let validated;
  try {
    validated = parseRegistry(next, catalogue);
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof RegistryInvalid) return refuseRegistry(e, a.id);
    throw e;
  }
  try {
    modelEnvBlock(validated, catalogue, windowsOf(win));
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof ModelEnvInvalid) return refuse(1, 'unroutable-lane', `${e.message} Nothing was written.`);
    throw e;
  }
  // THE BRAKE FIRST (D-5206), over any hold already standing: the act that set it last.
  c.hold = { at: now(), by: 'revert' };
  const w0 = writeAdvance(a.id, adv);
  if (w0 !== null) return refuse(1, w0[0], w0[1]);
  const w1 = writeRegistry(a.id, validated);
  if (w1 !== null) return refuse(1, w1[0], `${w1[1]} ${a.class} is held now, and stays on ${from ?? 'none'}.`);
  const mat = materialise(account, validated, catalogue, windowsOf(win));
  if (mat.err !== undefined) {
    const back = writeRegistry(a.id, registry);
    const again = back === null ? materialise(account, registry, catalogue, windowsOf(win)) : { err: back };
    const how = back !== null ? 'could NOT be put back'
      : again.err === undefined ? 'was put back, and the lane re-rendered on it'
        : `was put back, and rendering it failed too (${again.err[1]})`;
    return refuse(1, mat.err[0], `${mat.err[1]} The registry ${how}; ${a.class} is held, on ${from ?? 'none'}, and `
      + 'its previous model is still on record, so the revert can be run again.');
  }
  c.previous = null;
  const done = recordMove(adv, a.class, {
    at: now(), how: 'revert', from, to, ok: true, canary: 'not-run',
    ...(effortFrom !== effortTo ? { effort: { from: effortFrom, to: effortTo } } : {}),
  });
  const w2 = writeAdvance(a.id, done);
  const answer = { ok: true, op: 'revert', class: a.class, from, to, ...describe(account, validated, catalogue, win) };
  if (w2 !== null) {
    answer.advanceNote = `${w2[0]}: ${w2[1]} The class was reverted and is held; its previous model is still on `
      + 'record, so a second revert changes nothing.';
    process.stderr.write(`${SELF}: ${answer.advanceNote}\n`);
  }
  out(answer);
  return 0;
}
```

After Stage 0's paragraph that begins `**The context window.**`, add:

```markdown
**Holds, revert and the advance file.** Each lane may carry `~/.ccrc/models/<id>.advance.json`, a sibling of the
registry and never a key in it, so an older ccrc keeps reading the registry after a rollback. Per class it records
the family the class follows (the last part of a `<vendor>-<version>-<family>` model id), an optional hold, the
model the class had before its last automatic advance, and its last ten moves. `init codex` writes it, with a
family for every class, an empty one included. `set-class` records the move and takes the family from the new pin,
and clears it when you set `none` or a model id outside that shape, so a class you emptied by hand stays empty.
`hold <class>` keeps a class where it is, and `release <class>` lets it move again. `revert <class>` puts back the
model the class had before its last automatic advance, with its effort level, and holds it there; with no advance
on record it refuses `no-previous`. Holds arrive one build before the automatic advance itself, so a class that
must stay where it is can be held first. Every write to a lane's model files — every per-lane verb but `show`, and
the hourly refresh's re-materialise — runs under one per-lane lock, `~/.ccrc/locks/models-<id>.lock`. A verb that
finds it held waits up to 20 seconds and then refuses `lock-busy`, writing nothing; on a box without `flock`, or
before the first lock on a box whose PATH has no `mkdir`, the verbs run unserialised, as before. The catalogue is
the one lane model file written outside the lock: the probe replaces it whole, by a rename, so a writer under the
lock always reads one complete catalogue. `rm` reaps the advance file with the lane's other model files, and never
the lock.
```

  fixture lane, canary first (Task 11's first case), and every suite in "W2 whole-branch checks" is green.

  W1 this wave consumes: `shared/model-advance.mjs` (`familyOf`, `chooseCandidate`, `resolveEffort`, `canaryEffort`,
  `backfillAdvance`, `recordMove`, `recordFailure` (which writes `canary: 'failed'` on the entry it records; Task 9
  overwrites that word when the canary passed), `reconcilePending` (it settles a pending intent of EITHER shape, an
  automatic advance's, which carries no `how`, and a hand `set-class`'s, `how: 'hand'`, written before that verb's
  registry rename (D-5188), and it answers `recovered: true` for a landed intent of either
  shape, so Task 9 reads the intent's `how` first), `BLOCKED_CAUSES`, `REASON_MAX` (the one cap on a history reason,
  W1 Task 2: Tasks 9 and 10 import it, ruling RC4, and nothing in this wave assigns it), and the types `Advance`,
  `ClassAdvance` and `Pending` (`AdvancePending | HandPending`: TypeScript that reads `effortFrom` or `effortTo` off a
  pending intent narrows on `how` first; this wave's tests read neither)); in `deploy/models-op.mjs` `readAdvance`,
  `writeAdvance`, `now()`, `SEED_FAMILIES`, the `writes` flag on every `OPS` row, `advanceForWrite` (the one writer
  loader), `backfillOnce` and `backfillOp` (Task 9 extends the last); in `ccd/ccrc` `_models_lock` (Task 11 moves its
  wait clamp into `_models_lock_secs`), `_models_node_locked` (which runs node under `MODELS_NODE_BOUND_S`, 10 s, and
  answers rc 124 with no body when that bound expires), `MODELS_NODE_BOUND_S`, `_models_lock_path` and
  `MODELS_WRITE_OPS`; the verbs `ccrc models <id> hold|release|revert <class>`; `set-class`'s hand intent and family
  rule (its move recorded through `reconcilePending`'s hand branch, whether the verb finished or a crash cut it short;

```ts
// subcommands rather than lane ids — each DEFINED ONCE, in `shared/models.mjs`

// Neutral ids only: this repository is public.
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { MODELS_LANE_ID_RE, MODELS_RESERVED_IDS } from '../../shared/models.js';

const REPO = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
const read = (rel: string): string => readFileSync(path.join(REPO, rel), 'utf8');
/** The ONE capture of `re` in `src`: a second definition is a red here, not a quiet drift. */
const only = (src: string, re: RegExp, what: string): string => {
  const all = [...src.matchAll(re)];
  expect(all.length, `expected exactly one ${what}, found ${all.length}`).toBe(1);
  return all[0]![1]!;
};

    const src = read('shared/models.mjs');
    expect(only(src, /^export const MODELS_LANE_ID_RE = \/(.+)\/;$/gm, 'MODELS_LANE_ID_RE definition'))
      .toBe(MODELS_LANE_ID_RE.source);
  });

  it("shared/roster.ts's ID_RE has the same source", () => {
    expect(only(read('shared/roster.ts'), /^const ID_RE = \/(.+)\/;$/gm, 'ID_RE in shared/roster.ts'))
      .toBe(MODELS_LANE_ID_RE.source);
  });

  it("ccd/ccrc-wrapper-shape's WRAPPER_ID_RE has the same source", () => {
    expect(only(read('ccd/ccrc-wrapper-shape'), /^WRAPPER_ID_RE='([^']+)'$/gm, 'WRAPPER_ID_RE'))
      .toBe(MODELS_LANE_ID_RE.source);
  });

  it('deploy/models-op.mjs re-exports it as ACCOUNT_ID_RE and spells no literal of its own', () => {
    const src = read('deploy/models-op.mjs');
    expect(src).toContain('export const ACCOUNT_ID_RE = MODELS_LANE_ID_RE;');
    expect(src).not.toMatch(/ACCOUNT_ID_RE = \//);
    expect(src).not.toContain('[a-z0-9-]{0,31}');
  });

    for (const ok of ['lane-a', 'a', `a${'b'.repeat(31)}`]) expect(MODELS_LANE_ID_RE.test(ok), ok).toBe(true);
    for (const bad of ['..', 'lane/a', '-lane', 'Lane-a', `a${'b'.repeat(32)}`, '']) {
      expect(MODELS_LANE_ID_RE.test(bad), bad).toBe(false);
    }
  });
});
```

```ts
// ── auto-advance plan W2 Task 7: every runtime value reaches both twins ─────
// The describe above pins the .ts's OWN declarations against the .mjs. This
// one pins the other direction: every value the .mjs exports is reachable
// through the .ts (re-exported, or declared there for its `as const` type)
// and declared in the .d.mts, so a name added to the .mjs alone is red here
// rather than `undefined` in a bundle or invisible to tsc.
describe('shared/models: every value the .mjs exports reaches the .ts and the .d.mts', () => {
  const read = (f: string): string => readFileSync(path.join(REPO, 'shared', f), 'utf8');
  const valueExports = (src: string): string[] =>
    [...src.matchAll(/^export (?:const|function|class) ([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/gm)].map((m) => m[1]!).sort();
  const reExported = (src: string): string[] => {
    const m = /export \{([^}]*)\} from '\.\/models\.mjs';/.exec(src);
    expect(m, "shared/models.ts has no re-export block from './models.mjs'").not.toBeNull();
    return m![1]!.split(',').map((s) => s.trim()).filter((s) => s !== '');
  };
  const declaredIn = (src: string): string[] =>
    [...src.matchAll(/^export declare (?:const|function|class) ([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/gm)].map((m) => m[1]!);

  it('the .ts re-exports, or itself declares, every value export of the .mjs', () => {
    const ts = read('models.ts');
    const reachable = new Set([...reExported(ts), ...valueExports(ts)]);
    expect(valueExports(read('models.mjs')).filter((n) => !reachable.has(n))).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('the .d.mts declares every value export of the .mjs', () => {
    const declared = new Set(declaredIn(read('models.d.mts')));
    expect(valueExports(read('models.mjs')).filter((n) => !declared.has(n))).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('the lane-id pattern and the reserved words are among them, so the two checks above are not over nothing', () => {
    const mjs = valueExports(read('models.mjs'));
    expect(mjs).toContain('MODELS_LANE_ID_RE');
    expect(mjs).toContain('MODELS_RESERVED_IDS');
    expect(mjs.length).toBeGreaterThan(15);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 1: The fixtures**

Append to the end of `server/test/fixtures/advanceCases.ts`:

```ts
// ── The advance step's own fixtures (auto-advance plan W2, Tasks 8 to 12) ──
// Appended after W1's and importing nothing, so this block moves no line
// above it and adds nothing to the file's import list. Neutral ids only, in
// the `<vendor>-<version>-<family>` grammar: this repository is public. One
// lane is built from them everywhere, `lane-a` (codex-kind), and each case
// varies it by spreading. `CODEX` (modelCases.ts) is never extended.

/** Every effort level a row may list, lowest first: the catalogue's own order,
 *  which `resolveEffort` ranks by. */
export const STEP_EFFORTS: readonly string[] = ['low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', 'max'];

/** One catalogue row, in `parseCatalogue`'s normalised shape. */
export const stepRow = (id: string, efforts: readonly string[] = STEP_EFFORTS, hidden = false) => ({
  id, label: `Fixture ${id}`, context: 272000, maxContext: 272000, efforts: [...efforts], hidden,
  priceIn: null, priceOut: null,
});

/** A fresh codex catalogue with four families:
 *  - alpha: `model-6-alpha` is newest (`model-5.6-alpha` is older);
 *  - beta: one model;
 *  - gamma: `model-6.1-gamma` is newer than `model-5.6-gamma` and lists no
 *    `max`, so an opus at `max` resolves down to `xhigh`;
 *  - delta: one model, for an empty class whose family is stored. */
export const STEP_CATALOGUE = {
  probe: 'codex', fetchedAt: 1789000000, stale: false,
  models: [
    stepRow('model-5.6-alpha'), stepRow('model-6-alpha'),
    stepRow('model-6-beta'),
    stepRow('model-5.6-gamma'), stepRow('model-6.1-gamma', ['low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh']),
    stepRow('model-6-delta'),
  ],
};

/** lane-a's registry: haiku and sonnet on their family's newest model, opus one
 *  version behind (its one candidate is `model-6.1-gamma`), fable empty. Its key
 *  order is `parseRegistry`'s, so these bytes are what `writeRegistry` writes. */
export const STEP_REGISTRY = {
  probe: 'codex',
  classes: { haiku: 'model-6-alpha', sonnet: 'model-6-beta', opus: 'model-5.6-gamma', fable: null as string | null },
  subagent: 'sonnet',
  discovery: 'catalogue',
  effort: { haiku: 'high', sonnet: 'high', opus: 'max' } as Record<string, string>,
};

/** The family each class's advance-file entry stores. fable's is null: an empty
 *  class nobody seeded stays empty until a case gives it a family. */
export const STEP_FAMILIES: Readonly<Record<string, string | null>> = {
  haiku: 'alpha', sonnet: 'beta', opus: 'gamma', fable: null,
};

/** A v1 advance file (plan §3.1) for lane-a: every class at `STEP_FAMILIES`
 *  with no hold, no previous and no history, then `over[class]` spread over its
 *  entry, and `pending`. */
export const stepAdvance = (
  over: Readonly<Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>> = {},
  pending: Record<string, unknown> | null = null,
) => ({
  v: 1,
  classes: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(STEP_FAMILIES).map(([cls, family]) =>
    [cls, { family, hold: null, previous: null, history: [], ...(over[cls] ?? {}) }])),
  pending,
});

/** Where a codex-kind fixture lane listens, and where its OAuth would live. */
export interface StepLane { proxyPort: number; litellmPort: number; authDir: string }

/** The advance step's roster: one upstream row (a roster needs exactly one),
 *  `lane-a` (codex-kind, on `laneA`'s ports), `lane-b` and `lane-c` (an
 *  Anthropic lane). `lane-b` is external-kind (the live lanes' shape before their
 *  flip), or, given `laneB`, a second codex-kind lane on those ports. */
export const stepRoster = (laneA: StepLane, laneB?: StepLane) => ({
  version: 1,
  accounts: [
    { id: 'lane-up', label: 'lane-up', configDirSuffix: '.claude', exec: { kind: 'upstream' }, homeAble: true,
      telemetry: 'anthropic' },
    { id: 'lane-a', label: 'lane-a', configDirSuffix: '.claude-lane-a',
      exec: { kind: 'codex', provider: 'openai', proxyPort: laneA.proxyPort, litellmPort: laneA.litellmPort,
        authDir: laneA.authDir },
      homeAble: false, telemetry: 'codex' },
    { id: 'lane-b', label: 'lane-b', configDirSuffix: '.claude-lane-b',
      exec: laneB === undefined ? { kind: 'external', provider: 'openai' }
        : { kind: 'codex', provider: 'openai', proxyPort: laneB.proxyPort, litellmPort: laneB.litellmPort,
          authDir: laneB.authDir },
      homeAble: false, telemetry: 'codex' },
    { id: 'lane-c', label: 'lane-c', configDirSuffix: '.claude-lane-c', exec: { kind: 'generated' }, homeAble: true,
      telemetry: 'anthropic' },
  ],
});

/** `catalogue` in the RAW shape the Codex endpoint answers, the fields
 *  `ccrc-models-probe`'s `codex_models` reads, for `CCRC_MODELS_PROBE_FIXTURE`:
 *  a refresh then probes this same catalogue back. */
export const stepRaw = (catalogue: { models: ReadonlyArray<ReturnType<typeof stepRow>> }) => ({
  models: catalogue.models.map((m) => ({
    slug: m.id, display_name: m.label, description: '', context_window: m.context, max_context_window: m.maxContext,
    visibility: m.hidden ? 'hide' : 'show', default_reasoning_level: m.efforts[0] ?? null,
    supported_reasoning_levels: m.efforts.map((effort) => ({ effort })),
  })),
});
```

```ts
// ── auto-advance plan W2, Tasks 8 and 9: the advance step's two ops ──────────
// Their own lane (`stepRoster`, fixtures/advanceCases.ts): neutral ids only.
// The roster's ports are pure-parse: nothing in this file connects to either.
const STEP_PORTS = { proxyPort: 45020, litellmPort: 45021 };
const STEP_SETTINGS = '.claude-lane-a';
/** lane-a's advance file, through W1's `advanceOf`. */
const laneAdvance = (): Advance => advanceOf('lane-a');

/** A lane's registry, catalogue and advance file, then the op's own materialise.
 *  `catalogue: null` leaves the lane never probed; `advance: null` leaves the
 *  advance file absent. */
function plantStep(o: { id?: string; registry?: unknown; catalogue?: unknown; advance?: unknown } = {}): void {
  const id = o.id ?? 'lane-a';
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(home, '.ccrc', 'models'), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(regPath(id), `${JSON.stringify(o.registry ?? STEP_REGISTRY, null, 2)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
  if (o.catalogue !== null) writeCatalogue(id, o.catalogue ?? STEP_CATALOGUE);
  if (o.advance !== null) {
    fs.writeFileSync(advPath(id), `${JSON.stringify(o.advance ?? stepAdvance(), null, 2)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
  }
  const m = op('materialise', '--file', rosterPath(), '--id', id);
  expect(m.code, m.stdout + m.stderr).toBe(0);
}

/** Every file under ~/.ccrc and lane-a's settings.json, with its bytes and
 *  mtime: the "writes nothing" pins compare two of these. */
function snapshot(): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const walk = (d: string): void => {
    for (const e of fs.readdirSync(d, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      const p = path.join(d, e.name);
      if (e.isDirectory()) walk(p);
      else out.push(`${path.relative(home, p)} ${fs.statSync(p).mtimeMs} ${fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8')}`);
    }
  };
  walk(path.join(home, '.ccrc'));
  const settings = path.join(home, STEP_SETTINGS, 'settings.json');
  if (fs.existsSync(settings)) out.push(`${STEP_SETTINGS} ${fs.statSync(settings).mtimeMs} ${fs.readFileSync(settings, 'utf8')}`);
  return out.sort();
}

describe('advance-plan (auto-advance spec §2.2 to §2.3; plan W2 Task 8)', () => {
  const plan = (id = 'lane-a'): Result => op('advance-plan', '--file', rosterPath(), '--id', id);
  const none = { candidate: null, reason: null, blocked: null, effortTo: null, canaryEffort: null };

  beforeEach(() => { seed(stepRoster({ ...STEP_PORTS, authDir: codexAuthDir('lane-a') })); });

  it('a codex-kind lane on a fresh catalogue is eligible, and its candidate carries effortTo and canaryEffort', () => {
    plantStep();
    const r = plan();
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(r.body).toMatchObject({ ok: true, op: 'advance-plan', id: 'lane-a', eligible: true, why: null, file: 'ok' });
    expect(r.body['classes']).toEqual([
      { class: 'haiku', pin: 'model-6-alpha', family: 'alpha', held: false, ...none },
      { class: 'sonnet', pin: 'model-6-beta', family: 'beta', held: false, ...none },
      { class: 'opus', pin: 'model-5.6-gamma', family: 'gamma', held: false, candidate: 'model-6.1-gamma',
        reason: 'newer', blocked: null, effortTo: 'xhigh', canaryEffort: 'low' },
      { class: 'fable', pin: null, family: null, held: false, ...none },
    ]);
  });

  it('an empty class whose family is stored takes the newest of its family, with no effort of its own', () => {
    plantStep({ advance: stepAdvance({ fable: { family: 'delta' } }) });
    const fable = (plan().body['classes'] as Record<string, unknown>[])[3];
    expect(fable).toEqual({ class: 'fable', pin: null, family: 'delta', held: false, candidate: 'model-6-delta',
      reason: 'empty', blocked: null, effortTo: null, canaryEffort: 'low' });
  });

  it('a held class reports its candidate with held true', () => {
    plantStep({ advance: stepAdvance({ opus: { hold: { at: '2026-10-22T08:00:00Z', by: 'hand' } } }) });
    const opus = (plan().body['classes'] as Record<string, unknown>[])[2];
    expect(opus).toMatchObject({ class: 'opus', held: true, candidate: 'model-6.1-gamma' });
  });

  it('an unreadable windows file blocks each candidate with windows-unreadable and keeps the candidate', () => {
    // The commit would abandon `windows-unreadable` after a canary (Task 9), so
    // the plan says so first and the step spends no request on it.
    plantStep();
    plantWindows('lane-a', '{ not json');
    const rows = plan().body['classes'] as Record<string, unknown>[];
    expect(rows[2]).toMatchObject({ class: 'opus', candidate: 'model-6.1-gamma', blocked: 'windows-unreadable' });
    expect(rows[0]).toMatchObject({ class: 'haiku', candidate: null, blocked: null });
    expect(BLOCKED_CAUSES).toContain('windows-unreadable');
  });

  it('an absent advance file derives families from pins and seeds no empty class', () => {
    plantStep({ advance: null });
    const r = plan();
    expect(r.body).toMatchObject({ eligible: true, file: 'absent' });
    const rows = r.body['classes'] as Record<string, unknown>[];
    expect(rows[2]).toMatchObject({ class: 'opus', family: 'gamma', candidate: 'model-6.1-gamma' });
    // A seeded family here would be the backfill's job done by a read-only op.
    expect(rows[3]).toEqual({ class: 'fable', pin: null, family: null, held: false, ...none });
    expect(fs.existsSync(advPath('lane-a'))).toBe(false);
  });

  it.each([
    ['an external-kind lane', 'lane-not-codex-kind', (): void => plantStep({ id: 'lane-b' }), 'lane-b'],
    ['a codex-kind lane whose registry is not a codex probe', 'probe-not-codex', (): void => plantStep({
      registry: { probe: 'openrouter', classes: { haiku: null, sonnet: null, opus: null, fable: null },
        subagent: 'sonnet', discovery: [] } }), 'lane-a'],
    ['a lane never probed', 'never-probed', (): void => plantStep({ catalogue: null }), 'lane-a'],
    ['a stale catalogue', 'catalogue-stale', (): void => plantStep({ catalogue: { ...STEP_CATALOGUE, stale: true } }),
      'lane-a'],
  ] as [string, string, () => void, string][])('%s is ineligible, why %s, and no class has a candidate', (_w, why, plant, id) => {
    plant();
    const r = plan(id);
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(r.body).toMatchObject({ eligible: false, why });
    for (const row of r.body['classes'] as Record<string, unknown>[]) expect(row['candidate']).toBeNull();
  });

  it('an Anthropic lane is refused, as it refuses every op but show', () => {
    const r = plan('lane-c');
    expect(r.code).toBe(1);
    expect(r.body['error']).toBe('anthropic-lane');
  });

  it.each([
    ['an advance file that is a directory', 'advance-file-unreadable', (): void => {
      fs.rmSync(advPath('lane-a')); fs.mkdirSync(advPath('lane-a'));
    }],
    ['an advance file of another version', 'advance-file-invalid', (): void => {
      fs.writeFileSync(advPath('lane-a'), `${JSON.stringify({ ...stepAdvance(), v: 2 }, null, 2)}\n`);
    }],
    ['a registry that is not JSON', 'registry-invalid', (): void => { fs.writeFileSync(regPath('lane-a'), '{ not json'); }],
    ['a registry that is a directory', 'registry-unreadable', (): void => {
      fs.rmSync(regPath('lane-a')); fs.mkdirSync(regPath('lane-a'));
    }],
    ['a catalogue that is not a catalogue', 'catalogue-invalid', (): void => { writeCatalogue('lane-a', { probe: 'codex' }); }],
    ['a catalogue that is a directory', 'catalogue-unreadable', (): void => {
      const p = path.join(home, '.ccrc', 'models', 'lane-a.json');
      fs.rmSync(p); fs.mkdirSync(p);
    }],
  ] as [string, string, () => void][])('%s is a refusal naming %s, a BLOCKED_CAUSES word', (_w, word, spoil) => {
    plantStep();
    spoil();
    const r = plan();
    expect(r.code).toBe(1);
    expect(r.body).toMatchObject({ ok: false, error: word });
    expect(BLOCKED_CAUSES).toContain(word);
  });

  it('the plan writes nothing: every file under ~/.ccrc and the settings keep their bytes and mtimes', () => {
    plantStep({ advance: null });
    const before = snapshot();
    expect(plan().code).toBe(0);
    expect(plan('lane-a').body['eligible']).toBe(true);
    expect(snapshot()).toEqual(before);
  });
});
```

```js
/** `advance-plan` (auto-advance spec §2.2 to §2.3; plan W2 Task 8): READ-ONLY.
 *  Which classes of this lane the hourly refresh may advance, and to what — the
 *  question the refresh asks before it asks anything of the lane itself.
 *
 *  ELIGIBLE is three facts, and `why` names the first that fails:
 *    - `lane-not-codex-kind`: only an `exec.kind: "codex"` row advances
 *      (D-5198); an external row's tier, port and key are
 *      not ccrc's to know;
 *    - `probe-not-codex`: the family rule is the Codex lanes' (§2.2);
 *    - `never-probed` and `catalogue-stale`: no advance, and no retired-pin
 *      fallback, on a catalogue that is absent or marked stale
 *      (D-5199).
 *  On an ineligible lane every class is still listed, with its pin, family and
 *  hold, and no candidate.
 *
 *  THE FAMILY is the stored one when the advance file is present. With the
 *  file absent (a lane not yet backfilled) `chooseCandidate` derives it from
 *  the pin and an EMPTY class has none, so this op never seeds one (§2.1: the
 *  step "leaves an empty class unseeded until the backfill runs").
 *
 *  Per candidate, `effortTo` is the level the class would carry on the new
 *  model (`resolveEffort`, ranked by the old pin's row,
 *  D-5200; null: none) and `canaryEffort` the lowest
 *  level the new model lists (null: it lists none). A held or blocked class is
 *  reported with its candidate; the caller skips it. A candidate on a lane
 *  whose windows file cannot be read is blocked `windows-unreadable`
 *  (D-5193): the commit would abandon on it after the
 *  canary, so no request is spent on it.
 *
 *  A present advance file that cannot be read, or does not parse, is a REFUSAL
 *  carrying its own word, as an unreadable registry or catalogue already is
 *  before this op is reached (`main`'s reads): a pin never moves on data that
 *  cannot be read (§2.8). */
function advancePlanOp(a, account, registry, catalogue, win) {
  const rd = readAdvance(a.id);
  if (rd.err !== undefined) return refuse(1, rd.err[0], rd.err[1]);
  const adv = rd.advance;
  const why = !(isObj(account.exec) && account.exec.kind === 'codex') ? 'lane-not-codex-kind'
    : registry.probe !== 'codex' ? 'probe-not-codex'
      : catalogue === null ? 'never-probed'
        : catalogue.stale ? 'catalogue-stale'
          : null;
  const classes = CLASSES.map((cls) => {
    const pin = registry.classes[cls];
    const stored = adv === null ? null : adv.classes[cls].family;
    const row = {
      class: cls, pin, family: stored ?? familyOf(pin), held: adv !== null && adv.classes[cls].hold !== null,
      candidate: null, reason: null, blocked: null, effortTo: null, canaryEffort: null,
    };
    if (why !== null) return row;
    const choice = chooseCandidate({ registry, catalogue, cls, family: stored });
    row.candidate = choice.candidate;
    row.reason = choice.reason;
    row.blocked = choice.blocked;
    if (choice.candidate !== null) {
      const next = catalogue.models.find((m) => m.id === choice.candidate);
      const prev = pin === null ? undefined : catalogue.models.find((m) => m.id === pin);
      const newEfforts = next === undefined ? [] : next.efforts;
      row.effortTo = resolveEffort({
        stored: isObj(registry.effort) ? registry.effort[cls] : undefined,
        oldEfforts: prev === undefined ? null : prev.efforts,
        newEfforts,
      }) ?? null;
      row.canaryEffort = canaryEffort(newEfforts);
      if (row.blocked === null && win.state === 'unreadable') row.blocked = 'windows-unreadable';
    }
    return row;
  });
  out({ ok: true, op: 'advance-plan', id: a.id, eligible: why === null, why,
    file: adv === null ? 'absent' : 'ok', classes });
  return 0;
}
```

```js
import {
```

Insert immediately after `advancePlanOp`'s closing `}`:

```js
/** A history `reason` as the advance file's reader accepts it (plan §3.1):
 *  printable ASCII, at most `REASON_MAX` characters, the one number
 *  `shared/model-advance.mjs` defines and its `parseAdvance` holds every
 *  reason to. Every reason this file records passes through it, the canary's
 *  (`--reason`) and its own, because one the reader refused would make the
 *  whole advance file unreadable, and every later advance on the lane blocked
 *  behind it. */
const historyReason = (text) =>
  String(text).replace(/[^\x20-\x7e]+/g, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, REASON_MAX);

/** W1's `advanceForWrite` — the ONE writer loader: read, backfilled in memory
 *  when absent, its pending intent, of either shape, reconciled — plus what
 *  that intent recorded when it had LANDED (D-5216):
 *    `recoveredMove`  `{class, from, to, how}`, else null. `how` is the
 *                     intent's own: `advance` for an automatic advance's (its
 *                     intent carries no `how`), `hand` for a hand set-class's
 *                     (W1's `beginHandMove`, written before that verb's
 *                     registry rename). A landed hand move is reported as
 *                     hand, never as an advance: it records the
 *                     operator's own act, and owes no push.
 *    `recovered`      true only for a landed automatic advance, the one whose
 *                     history entry carries the `recovered: true` mark.
 *  W1's `reconcilePending` answers `recovered: true` for a landed intent of
 *  EITHER shape, and the settled file no longer says what the intent was, so
 *  it is read once more here, under the same lock, before `advanceForWrite`
 *  settles it. */
function settleForWrite(id, registry) {
  const cur = readAdvance(id);
  const intent = cur.err === undefined && cur.advance !== null ? cur.advance.pending : null;
  const loaded = advanceForWrite(id, registry);
  if (loaded.err !== undefined) return loaded;
  if (!loaded.recovered || intent === null) return { ...loaded, recovered: false, recoveredMove: null };
  const how = intent.how === 'hand' ? 'hand' : 'advance';
  return { ...loaded, recovered: how === 'advance',
    recoveredMove: { class: intent.class, from: intent.from, to: intent.to, how } };
}

/** `advance-commit` (auto-advance spec §2.1 D21 and §2.3 steps 4 to 6; plan W2
 *  Task 9): one class's move, or one failed canary's record, under the
 *  lane-files lock THE CALLER holds (`ccd/ccrc`'s `_models_node_locked`; this
 *  file takes no lock). `outcome` is `moved`, `failed` or `abandoned` (with
 *  `why`); `push` is true for a move and for a failure not already on record
 *  (D-5192).
 *
 *  THE ORDER of skeleton §3.3. A lane the advance step never touches (not
 *  codex-kind, or its probe not codex) abandons `not-eligible` before anything
 *  is read (D-5198). Otherwise the advance file is loaded
 *  through the one writer loader and any pending intent SETTLED FIRST
 *  (`settleForWrite`), so a crash gap heals even when this commit then
 *  abandons; an abandon writes the file only when that load changed it
 *  (`dirty`: created, or an intent settled), as W1's verbs do. `recoveredMove`
 *  names an intent that had landed, with its `how`, so a hand set-class's is
 *  reported as hand and never as an advance; `recovered` is true for a landed
 *  automatic advance only (D-5216).
 *
 *  THE RE-CHECK (D21). The canary ran OUTSIDE the lock, so what it was planned
 *  on is read again here, under it, and the move is ABANDONED when any of it
 *  changed:
 *    `catalogue-stale`     the catalogue is absent or stale (a passed canary);
 *    `windows-unreadable`  the measured windows cannot be read, so the env block
 *                          the move would write cannot be decided (a passed
 *                          canary; D-5193);
 *    `held`                a Hold landed during the canary: the Hold wins;
 *    `pin-moved`           the class no longer pins `--from` (a hand set-class,
 *                          or an overlapping refresh that moved it first);
 *    `candidate-changed`   the family rule no longer answers `--to`.
 *
 *  THE MOVE: validate the moved registry and its env block; write the INTENT
 *  (`pending`) to the advance file; rename the registry; materialise; and only
 *  then write `previous`, the history entry and clear `pending`. A SIGTERM
 *  between the rename and the materialise (the refresh unit's 300 s bound)
 *  leaves the intent on disk, and the next locked writer reconciles it
 *  (D-5188; the hourly step's backfill is the first,
 *  D-5215). A materialise that fails restores the
 *  previous registry under the same lock and materialises it again, and
 *  records a failed advance whose reason names both outcomes; `restored` says
 *  whether the previous registry AND its files are back
 *  (D-5208). When even the previous registry cannot
 *  be written back, the failure is recorded and the intent KEPT
 *  (D-5217): the registry does pin `--to`, so
 *  the next locked writer records the move as landed once the next refresh's
 *  own materialise has rewritten the lane's files from it. `previous` carries
 *  the effort the class had (D-5189), so a Revert
 *  restores it.
 *
 *  A failed advance's history entry records what the canary answered:
 *  `failed` for a refused canary, `passed` for a move that failed after it
 *  (`fail` sets it on the entry `recordFailure` returns). A moved registry that
 *  does not validate is a failed advance too, so doctor names it
 *  (D-5207). */
function advanceCommitOp(a, account, registry, catalogue, win) {
  if (!CLASSES.includes(a.class)) {
    return refuse(1, 'unknown-class', `"${a.class}" is not a class: the four are ${CLASSES.join(', ')}.`, 'class');
  }
  if (a.canary !== 'passed' && a.canary !== 'failed') {
    return refuse(2, 'bad-argv', `--canary takes passed or failed (got ${JSON.stringify(a.canary)}).`);
  }
  if (a.from !== 'none' && !MODEL_ID_RE.test(a.from)) {
    return refuse(1, 'bad-model-id', `--from "${a.from}" is neither a model id nor "none".`, 'from');
  }
  if (!MODEL_ID_RE.test(a.to)) return refuse(1, 'bad-model-id', `--to "${a.to}" is not a model id.`, 'to');
  const cls = a.class;
  const from = a.from === 'none' ? null : a.from;
  const effortFrom = isObj(registry.effort) && typeof registry.effort[cls] === 'string' ? registry.effort[cls] : null;
  let effortTo = null;
  let recovered = false;
  let recoveredMove = null;
  const answer = (outcome, extra = {}) => {
    out({ ok: true, op: 'advance-commit', id: a.id, class: cls, outcome, from, to: a.to,
      effort: { from: effortFrom, to: effortTo }, push: false, recovered,
      ...(recoveredMove === null ? {} : { recoveredMove }), ...extra });
    return 0;
  };

  // 1. A lane the advance step never touches: nothing is read or written.
  if (!(isObj(account.exec) && account.exec.kind === 'codex') || registry.probe !== 'codex') {
    return answer('abandoned', { why: 'not-eligible' });
  }
  // 2. The advance file, through the one writer loader: a pending intent a
  //    SIGTERM left behind is settled before anything is re-checked.
  const loaded = settleForWrite(a.id, registry);
  if (loaded.err !== undefined) return refuse(1, loaded.err[0], loaded.err[1]);
  let adv = loaded.advance;
  recovered = loaded.recovered;
  recoveredMove = loaded.recoveredMove;
  const abandon = (why) => {
    if (loaded.dirty) {
      const w = writeAdvance(a.id, adv);
      if (w !== null) return refuse(1, w[0], w[1]);
    }
    return answer('abandoned', { why });
  };

  // 3. The re-check: what the move needs, then the Hold, the pin and (passed
  //    only) the candidate.
  if (a.canary === 'passed') {
    if (catalogue === null || catalogue.stale) return abandon('catalogue-stale');
    if (win.state === 'unreadable') return abandon('windows-unreadable');
  }
  if (adv.classes[cls].hold !== null) return abandon('held');
  if (registry.classes[cls] !== from) return abandon('pin-moved');
  /** One failed advance on record (D-5192), with what the
   *  canary answered, and `pending` as given (null: cleared). W1's
   *  `recordFailure` writes `canary: 'failed'` on the entry it records — always
   *  the class's NEWEST, updated or appended — so a move that failed after a
   *  PASSED canary says so on that entry. */
  const fail = (reason, canary, extra = {}, pending = null) => {
    const f = recordFailure(adv, cls, { at: now(), from, to: a.to, reason });
    const history = f.advance.classes[cls].history;
    history[history.length - 1].canary = canary;
    const w = writeAdvance(a.id, { ...f.advance, pending });
    if (w !== null) return refuse(1, w[0], w[1]);
    return answer('failed', { reason, push: f.isNew, ...extra });
  };
  if (a.canary === 'failed') return fail(historyReason(a.reason ?? '') || 'the canary failed', 'failed');
  const choice = chooseCandidate({ registry, catalogue, cls, family: adv.classes[cls].family });
  if (choice.blocked !== null || choice.candidate !== a.to) return abandon('candidate-changed');

  // 4. The moved registry, its effort resolved against the old pin's row.
  const newRow = catalogue.models.find((m) => m.id === a.to);
  const oldRow = from === null ? undefined : catalogue.models.find((m) => m.id === from);
  effortTo = resolveEffort({
    stored: effortFrom ?? undefined,
    oldEfforts: oldRow === undefined ? null : oldRow.efforts,
    newEfforts: newRow === undefined ? [] : newRow.efforts,
  }) ?? null;
  const next = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(registry));
  next.classes[cls] = a.to;
  if (effortTo === null) {
    if (isObj(next.effort)) {
      delete next.effort[cls];
      if (Object.keys(next.effort).length === 0) delete next.effort;
    }
  } else {
    next.effort = { ...(isObj(next.effort) ? next.effort : {}), [cls]: effortTo };
  }

  // 5. Validate before anything is written (rule 2).
  const windows = windowsOf(win);
  let validated;
  try {
    validated = parseRegistry(next, catalogue);
    modelEnvBlock(validated, catalogue, windows);
  } catch (e) {
    if (!(e instanceof RegistryInvalid) && !(e instanceof ModelEnvInvalid)) throw e;
    return fail(historyReason(`the moved registry does not validate: ${e.message}`), 'passed', { restored: true });
  }

  // 6. The intent, BEFORE the rename (D-5188).
  const at = now();
  const intent = { class: cls, from, to: a.to, effortFrom, effortTo, at };
  let w = writeAdvance(a.id, { ...adv, pending: intent });
  if (w !== null) return refuse(1, w[0], w[1]);

  // 7. The rename, then 8. materialise, or 9. the restore.
  w = writeRegistry(a.id, validated);
  if (w !== null) {
    return fail(historyReason(`the moved registry could not be written (${w[0]}): ${w[1]}`), 'passed', { restored: true });
  }
  const mat = materialise(account, validated, catalogue, windows);
  if (mat.err !== undefined) {
    const back = writeRegistry(a.id, registry);
    if (back !== null) {
      // The registry still pins `--to`: the failure is recorded (doctor's
      // held-back reads it) and the intent is KEPT, so the next locked writer
      // records the move as landed (D-5217).
      return fail(historyReason(`materialise failed (${mat.err[0]}) and the previous registry could not be written `
        + `back (${back[0]}): ${mat.err[1]}`), 'passed', { restored: false }, intent);
    }
    const again = materialise(account, registry, catalogue, windows);
    if (again.err !== undefined) {
      return fail(historyReason(`materialise failed (${mat.err[0]}) and re-materialising the previous registry failed `
        + `too (${again.err[0]}): ${mat.err[1]}`), 'passed', { restored: false });
    }
    return fail(historyReason(`materialise failed (${mat.err[0]}), so the previous registry was restored: ${mat.err[1]}`),
      'passed', { restored: true });
  }

  // 10. The commit: previous with its effort, the ok entry, no intent.
  adv = recordMove({ ...adv, pending: null,
    classes: { ...adv.classes, [cls]: { ...adv.classes[cls], previous: { model: from, effort: effortFrom } } } },
  cls, { at, how: 'advance', from, to: a.to, ok: true, canary: 'passed',
    ...(effortFrom === effortTo ? {} : { effort: { from: effortFrom, to: effortTo } }) });
  w = writeAdvance(a.id, adv);
  // A history that could not be written leaves the intent on disk: the next
  // locked writer records the move as landed. The class DID move.
  return answer('moved', { push: true,
    ...(w === null ? {} : { reason: historyReason(`moved, but its history could not be written (${w[0]})`) }) });
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: `advance-backfill` settles a pending intent (D-5215)**

Why here: W1's `backfillOnce` creates the file only when it is absent and never reconciles. After a SIGTERM between
a move's registry rename and its materialise, the moved class already pins its family's newest model, so the plan
gives it no candidate, and with every class current (ruling RB6) no commit runs either: the intent would stay on disk
for good, with no history entry and no `previous`, so Revert could not undo that move. The backfill is the hourly
step's first locked writer (Task 11, step 1), so it settles the intent every hour.

In `deploy/models-op.mjs`, replace W1's `backfillOp` docstring and body, from

```js
/** `advance-backfill` (auto-advance spec §2.1): give a codex-kind lane whose registry probe is `codex` its advance
```

to its closing `}`, with:

```js
/** `advance-backfill` (auto-advance spec §2.1): give a codex-kind lane whose registry probe is `codex` its advance
 *  file when it has none (`backfillOnce`). In a file that EXISTS it settles a pending intent under the same lock and
 *  rewrites nothing else (plan W2 Task 9, D-5215): the hourly advance step calls this first,
 *  so a move a SIGTERM cut short after its registry rename is recorded within the hour even when its class then has
 *  no candidate, and so is a hand set-class cut short after its rename (W1's hand intent). `recoveredMove` appears
 *  only when that intent had landed, with the intent's `how`: `advance`, or `hand` for a hand set-class's, which is
 *  reported as hand and never as an advance (D-5216). Any other lane answers `created:
 *  false` with why, never a refusal, because the hourly refresh asks every lane (D-5198). */
function backfillOp(a, account, registry) {
  let why = null;
  if (!(isObj(account.exec) && account.exec.kind === 'codex')) why = 'lane-not-codex-kind';
  else if (registry.probe !== 'codex') why = 'probe-not-codex';
  const b = why === null ? backfillOnce(a.id, registry) : { created: false, why };
  if (b.err !== undefined) return refuse(1, b.err[0], b.err[1]);
  let recoveredMove = null;
  if (b.created === false && b.why === 'present') {
    const s = settleForWrite(a.id, registry);
    if (s.err !== undefined) return refuse(1, s.err[0], s.err[1]);
    if (s.dirty) {
      const w = writeAdvance(a.id, s.advance);
      if (w !== null) return refuse(1, w[0], w[1]);
    }
    recoveredMove = s.recoveredMove;
  }
  out({ ok: true, op: 'advance-backfill', id: a.id, created: b.created, ...(b.created ? {} : { why: b.why }),
    ...(recoveredMove === null ? {} : { recoveredMove }) });
  return 0;
}
```

```ts
// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Auto-advance plan W2 Task 10 — a fake lane PROXY, for the canary.
// A python child like every listener in this file, bound to 127.0.0.1 on a
// port the kernel chose. It answers the shim's lane probe, `GET /ccgpt/lane`,
// as the lane it was started for (or as another lane, or 404, by a `lane` file
// in its record directory), and `POST /v1/messages` the way the lane's shim and
// LiteLLM can, by a MODE FILE there (`mode.<model>` first, then `mode`, default
// `ok`). It records every POST (its path, its header NAMES, its Authorization
// VALUE and its body) to `req.<n>.json`, and every GET to `get.<n>.json`. The
// key it records is the fixture's own, minted per case.
// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

/** One mode per row of the canary's classification table (plan §3.6), and the
 *  caps it reads under. */
export type LaneProxyMode = 'ok' | `slow-ok:${number}` | 'park' | 'hang' | 'trickle' | 'flood' | '500' | '500-huge'
  | '500-risk' | '502-refused' | '502-reset' | '401-echo' | 'thinking-only' | 'blank-text' | 'stream-error' | 'json-200';

/** The shim's 502 text for a refused gateway connection it waited out
 *  (D-4933), up to its first interpolation, read out of `ccd/ccgpt-proxy.py`:
 *  the ONE reader, for the fake's `502-refused` answer and the canary's parity
 *  pin. Throws when that line moved. */
export function shimRefusedPrefix(): string {
  const src = readFileSync(join(REPO, 'ccd', 'ccgpt-proxy.py'), 'utf8');
  const m = /f"(ccgpt-proxy: upstream unreachable: connection refused for )\{UPSTREAM_WAIT_S\}s: \{e\.last\}"/.exec(src);
  if (m === null) throw new Error('ccd/ccgpt-proxy.py no longer carries the D-4933 refused-connect 502 text');
  return m[1]!.trimEnd();
}

export const FAKE_LANE_PROXY_PY = `import json, os, socketserver, sys, threading, time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
ARGS = sys.argv[1:]
def opt(name, default):
    return ARGS[ARGS.index(name) + 1] if name in ARGS and ARGS.index(name) + 1 < len(ARGS) else default
REC = opt("--rec", "")
D4933 = opt("--d4933", "")
LANE = opt("--lane", "")
LOCK = threading.Lock()
COUNT = [0]
GETS = [0]
def mode_for(model):
    for name in (["mode." + model] if model else []) + ["mode"]:
        p = os.path.join(REC, name)
        if os.path.isfile(p):
            with open(p) as f:
                return f.read().strip()
    return "ok"
def lane_answer():
    p = os.path.join(REC, "lane")
    if os.path.isfile(p):
        with open(p) as f:
            v = f.read().strip()
        return None if v == "-" else v
    return LANE
def start():
    return ("message_start", {"type": "message_start", "message": {"id": "msg_fixture", "type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": []}})
def thinking(t):
    return ("content_block_delta", {"type": "content_block_delta", "index": 0, "delta": {"type": "thinking_delta", "thinking": t}})
def text(t):
    return [start(),
            ("content_block_start", {"type": "content_block_start", "index": 0, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}}),
            ("content_block_delta", {"type": "content_block_delta", "index": 0, "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": t}}),
            ("content_block_stop", {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": 0}),
            ("message_delta", {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "end_turn"}}),
            ("message_stop", {"type": "message_stop"})]
THINKING = [start(),
            ("content_block_start", {"type": "content_block_start", "index": 0, "content_block": {"type": "thinking", "thinking": ""}}),
            thinking("Considering the reply."),
            ("content_block_stop", {"type": "content_block_stop", "index": 0}),
            ("message_delta", {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "max_tokens"}}),
            ("message_stop", {"type": "message_stop"})]
FLOOD = [start()] + [thinking("x" * 4096) for _ in range(80)] + [
            ("message_delta", {"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "max_tokens"}}),
            ("message_stop", {"type": "message_stop"})]
STREAM_ERROR = [start(), ("error", {"type": "error", "error": {"type": "overloaded_error", "message": "fixture overload"}})]
class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass
    def _json(self, code, obj):
        body = json.dumps(obj).encode()
        self.send_response(code)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.send_header("Connection", "close")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)
    def _sse_head(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
        self.send_header("Connection", "close")
        self.end_headers()
    def _event(self, name, data):
        self.wfile.write(("event: %s\\ndata: %s\\n\\n" % (name, json.dumps(data))).encode())
        self.wfile.flush()
    def _sse(self, events):
        self._sse_head()
        for name, data in events:
            self._event(name, data)
    def do_GET(self):
        with LOCK:
            GETS[0] += 1
            n = GETS[0]
        with open(os.path.join(REC, "get.%d.json" % n), "w") as f:
            json.dump({"n": n, "path": self.path,
                       "headerNames": sorted(k.lower() for k in self.headers.keys()),
                       "authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization")}, f)
        lane = lane_answer() if self.path == "/ccgpt/lane" else None
        if lane is None:
            return self._json(404, {"error": "not found"})
        return self._json(200, {"lane": lane})
    def do_POST(self):
        raw = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0))
        try:
            body = json.loads(raw)
        except Exception:
            body = None
        model = body.get("model") if isinstance(body, dict) else None
        with LOCK:
            COUNT[0] += 1
            n = COUNT[0]
        with open(os.path.join(REC, "req.%d.json" % n), "w") as f:
            json.dump({"n": n, "path": self.path, "model": model,
                       "headerNames": sorted(k.lower() for k in self.headers.keys()),
                       "authorization": self.headers.get("Authorization"), "body": body}, f)
        mode = mode_for(model or "")
        if mode == "ok":
            return self._sse(text("OK"))
        if mode.startswith("slow-ok:"):
            time.sleep(float(mode.split(":", 1)[1]))
            return self._sse(text("OK"))
        if mode == "park":
            open(os.path.join(REC, "parked.%d" % n), "w").close()
            deadline = time.time() + 60
            while not os.path.exists(os.path.join(REC, "release")) and time.time() < deadline:
                time.sleep(0.05)
            return self._sse(text("OK"))
        if mode == "hang":
            time.sleep(60)
            return
        if mode == "trickle":
            self._sse_head()
            self._event(*start())
            deadline = time.time() + 60
            while time.time() < deadline:
                self._event(*thinking("still thinking"))
                time.sleep(0.2)
            return
        if mode == "flood":
            return self._sse(FLOOD)
        if mode == "500":
            return self._json(500, {"error": {"type": "api_error", "message": "upstream error"}})
        if mode == "500-huge":
            return self._json(500, {"pad": "x" * 70000, "error": {"type": "api_error", "message": "upstream error"}})
        if mode == "500-risk":
            return self._json(500, {"error": {"type": "api_error", "message": "risk-averse upstream refused the task-queue"}})
        if mode == "502-refused":
            return self._json(502, {"error": D4933 + " 60s: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>"})
        if mode == "502-reset":
            return self._json(502, {"error": "ccgpt-proxy: upstream unreachable: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer"})
        if mode == "401-echo":
            return self._json(401, {"error": {"type": "auth_error", "message": "Authentication Error, Invalid proxy server token passed. Received API Key = %s" % (self.headers.get("Authorization") or "")}})
        if mode == "thinking-only":
            return self._sse(THINKING)
        if mode == "blank-text":
            return self._sse(text(" "))
        if mode == "stream-error":
            return self._sse(STREAM_ERROR)
        if mode == "json-200":
            return self._json(200, {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "OK"}]})
        return self._json(500, {"error": "fixture: unknown mode " + mode})
class Server(ThreadingHTTPServer):
    daemon_threads = True
    def server_bind(self):
        socketserver.TCPServer.server_bind(self)
        self.server_name, self.server_port = self.server_address[:2]
server = Server(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
print("READY %d" % server.server_address[1], flush=True)
server.serve_forever()
`;

export interface FakeLaneProxy { port: number; rec: string; child: ChildProcess }
export interface LaneProxyRequest {
  n: number; path: string; model: string | null; headerNames: string[]; authorization: string | null; body: unknown;
}
export interface LaneProxyGet { n: number; path: string; headerNames: string[]; authorization: string | null }

/** The fake lane proxy, a tracked python child of this process on a port the
 *  kernel chose (held from the moment this resolves), answering the lane probe
 *  as `lane`. Its record directory is `<home>/fake-lane-proxy`. Ended by
 *  `killLaneProcesses(home)`, through its handle. */
export async function spawnFakeLaneProxy(home: string, lane = 'lane-a'): Promise<FakeLaneProxy> {
  const py = pythonOrSkip();
  if (py === null) throw new Error('spawnFakeLaneProxy needs python3 — gate the describe with pythonOrSkip()');
  const dir = path.join(home, 'fake-procs');
  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  const script = path.join(dir, 'lane-proxy.py');
  if (!fs.existsSync(script)) fs.writeFileSync(script, FAKE_LANE_PROXY_PY);
  const rec = path.join(home, 'fake-lane-proxy');
  fs.mkdirSync(rec, { recursive: true });
  const child = spawn(py, [script, '--rec', rec, '--d4933', shimRefusedPrefix(), '--lane', lane], {
    cwd: home,
    env: { PATH: process.env['PATH'] ?? '/usr/bin:/bin', HOME: home, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE: '1' },
    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  });
  trackChild(home, child);
  const port = await new Promise<number>((resolve, reject) => {
    let out = '';
    let err = '';
    const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`the fake lane proxy reported no READY within 10s: ${err}`)), 10_000);
    child.stdout?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => {
      out += c.toString();
      const m = /^READY (\d+)$/m.exec(out);
      if (m) { clearTimeout(timer); resolve(Number(m[1])); }
    });
    child.stderr?.on('data', (c: Buffer) => { err += c.toString(); });
    child.once('exit', (code, sig) => {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      reject(new Error(`the fake lane proxy exited (${code ?? sig}) before READY: ${err}`));
    });
  });
  return { port, rec, child };
}

/** What the fake answers a POST with: for every model, or for `model` only. */
export function laneProxyMode(p: FakeLaneProxy, mode: LaneProxyMode, model?: string): void {
  writeFileSync(join(p.rec, model === undefined ? 'mode' : `mode.${model}`), `${mode}\n`);
}

/** Which lane the fake's lane probe answers as from now on; null: a 404. */
export function laneProxyAnswersAs(p: FakeLaneProxy, lane: string | null): void {
  writeFileSync(join(p.rec, 'lane'), `${lane ?? '-'}\n`);
}

const recorded = <T extends { n: number }>(p: FakeLaneProxy, re: RegExp): T[] =>
  fs.readdirSync(p.rec).filter((f) => re.test(f))
    .map((f) => JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(p.rec, f), 'utf8')) as T)
    .sort((x, y) => x.n - y.n);

/** Every POST the fake received, in arrival order. */
export function laneProxyRequests(p: FakeLaneProxy): LaneProxyRequest[] {
  return recorded<LaneProxyRequest>(p, /^req\.\d+\.json$/);
}

/** Every GET (the lane probe) the fake received, in arrival order. */
export function laneProxyGets(p: FakeLaneProxy): LaneProxyGet[] {
  return recorded<LaneProxyGet>(p, /^get\.\d+\.json$/);
}

/** How many requests are parked (`park` mode) right now, or were. */
export function laneProxyParked(p: FakeLaneProxy): number {
  return fs.readdirSync(p.rec).filter((f) => /^parked\.\d+$/.test(f)).length;
}

/** Lets every parked request answer, with a 200 and text. */
export function laneProxyRelease(p: FakeLaneProxy): void {
  writeFileSync(join(p.rec, 'release'), '');
}
```

```ts
function canary(args: string[] = [], extraEnv: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {}): Canary {
  const t0 = Date.now();
  const r = spawnSync(process.execPath,
    [CANARY, '--id', 'lane-a', '--model', 'model-6.1-gamma', '--effort', 'low', '--timeout-s', '2', ...args],

  return { code: r.status, body: JSON.parse(lines[0]!) as Record<string, unknown>, out: stdout, ms: Date.now() - t0 };
}

  it('a FIFO at runtime.env is unavailable at once, never a block', () => {
    fs.rmSync(envPath());
    expect(spawnSync('mkfifo', [envPath()]).status, 'mkfifo is needed for this case').toBe(0);
    const c = canary();
    expect(c.body).toMatchObject({ result: 'unavailable', reason: 'runtime.env could not be read (ENOTREG)' });
    expect(c.ms).toBeLessThan(10_000);
    expect(laneProxyRequests(proxy)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it.each([
    ['an id that is not a lane id', ['--id', '../x']],
    ['a model that is not a model id', ['--model', 'not an id']],
    ['an effort longer than 64 characters', ['--effort', 'x'.repeat(65)]],
    ['an effort with a control character', ['--effort', 'lo\tw']],
    ['a deadline of 0', ['--timeout-s', '0']],
    ['an unknown key', ['--key', 'x']],
  ] as [string, string[]][])('%s is a usage error at exit 2, and nothing is sent', (_w, args) => {
    const c = canary(args);
    expect(c.code).toBe(2);
    expect(c.body).toMatchObject({ ok: false, error: 'bad-argv' });
    expect(laneProxyGets(proxy)).toEqual([]);
    expect(laneProxyRequests(proxy)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('the key never leaves the process: no answer carries it, whatever the lane says', () => {
    const modes: LaneProxyMode[] = ['ok', '500', '401-echo', '502-reset', 'stream-error', 'thinking-only', 'json-200'];
    for (const mode of modes) {
      laneProxyMode(proxy, mode);
      expect(canary().out, mode).not.toContain(key.slice(3));
    }
    expect(laneProxyRequests(proxy).map((q) => q.authorization)).toEqual(modes.map(() => `Bearer ${key}`));
  });
});

describe('deploy/models-canary.mjs in source (plan W2 Task 10)', () => {

    expect(s).not.toMatch(/process\.env(?:\.[A-Za-z_]\w*|\[[^\]]+\])\s*=(?!=)/);
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the canary**

Create `deploy/models-canary.mjs`:

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// models-canary — ONE request through a Codex lane's own proxy, for one
// candidate model, before the hourly refresh moves a class to it (auto-advance
// spec §2.3 step 3, D2 and D22; plan W2 Task 10). `ccd/ccrc`'s `_models_canary`
// is its one caller.
//
// FIRST, THE LANE PROBE (D-5210). A port is only a
// number (`ccd/ccgpt-proxy.py`'s own rule): before the key goes anywhere, this
// program asks `GET /ccgpt/lane` on the lane's proxy port, with no key, and
// sends the keyed request only when the listener answers as THIS lane. Another
// lane's leftover shim, a stray listener or a foreign process on that port gets
// nothing: the answer is `unavailable`, and no request carrying the key is made.
//
// WHAT IT SENDS. `POST http://127.0.0.1:<proxyPort>/v1/messages`, the path a
// session's requests take: a "reply OK" prompt, `max_tokens` 512, streamed, and
// the lowest effort the model lists (`output_config.effort`, omitted when it
// lists none, or when that level is literally named `none`: the sentinel and a
// level of that name both send the provider's own default, which still tests
// the model). Streamed, because every lane LiteLLM entry is `mode: responses`,
// which parses only streamed answers (`deploy/litellm-config.template.yaml`).
// 512 tokens, so a low-effort reasoning pass still has room before its text.
// Reading stops at the first non-empty text delta, or at READ_CAP bytes.
//
// WHAT IT ANSWERS. Exactly one JSON object on stdout, and nothing on stderr:
// `{"ok":true,"op":"canary","result":R,"status":S,"reason":T}` at exit 0, R one of
//   passed       a 200 whose stream carried a non-empty text delta in time;
//   failed       a real refusal: any other status, a 200 with no text or with
//                an error event, a socket error on the keyed request other
//                than a refused connect;
//   not-ready    the lane is not up yet: the shim's D-4933 502 (a refused
//                gateway connection it waited out), a refused connect on the
//                shim's own port, or this program's own deadline (D22) — a
//                deadline that passes after a 200 still answers not-ready, and
//                its reason says the lane answered;
//   unavailable  the lane's files are absent, unreadable or malformed, or the
//                port does not answer as this lane; no keyed request was sent.
// A usage error is `{"ok":false,"error":"bad-argv",…}` at exit 2.
//
// THE KEY. The lane's gateway key is read from `runtime.env` in THIS process and
// lives in one local variable and one request header. It never reaches argv,
// the environment, stdout, stderr or a `reason`: every reason is scrubbed of it
// (`scrub`), because an upstream refusal may echo the key back (a LiteLLM 401
// names the key it received). This program spawns no process.
//
// NO PROXY. `node:http` with a FRESH `Agent` to the literal `127.0.0.1`: no proxy
// variable in the environment applies, and no name is resolved.

import { Agent, request } from 'node:http';
import { statSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
// REASON_MAX: the advance file's one cap on a history reason (W1's
// `shared/model-advance.mjs`, a pure module). A failed canary's reason becomes
// `advance-commit`'s `--reason`, so it is cut to the number the file's reader
// holds it to, imported and never spelled again here.
import { REASON_MAX } from '../shared/model-advance.mjs';
import { MODEL_ID_RE, MODELS_LANE_ID_RE } from '../shared/models.mjs';
import { readRegular } from '../shared/modelenv.mjs';

/** This program's own deadline in seconds when `--timeout-s` is absent. LONGER
 *  than the shim's 60 s refused-connect wait (`UPSTREAM_WAIT_DEFAULT_S`,
 *  `ccd/ccgpt-proxy.py`, D-4933), so a restarting gateway answers the shim's own
 *  502 (not ready) before this deadline does. `ccd/ccrc`'s
 *  `_models_canary_secs` defaults to the same number. */
const CANARY_TIMEOUT_S = 90;
const TIMEOUT_MAX_S = 600;
/** The shim's 502 text for a refused gateway connection it waited out
 *  (`ccd/ccgpt-proxy.py`, D-4933); `models-canary.test.ts` reads it out of
 *  that file and compares. */
const D4933_PREFIX = 'ccgpt-proxy: upstream unreachable: connection refused for';
const READ_CAP = 256 * 1024;
const ERROR_BODY_CAP = 64 * 1024;
const LANE_PROBE_CAP = 4 * 1024;
const RUNTIME_ENV_MAX = 256;
const LANE_JSON_MAX = 64 * 1024;
/** `runtime.env`'s one line (`_codex_runtime_env_ensure`, `ccd/ccrc`). */
const KEY_LINE = /^LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=(sk-[0-9a-f]{48})\n?$/;
/** An effort level as a catalogue may carry it (`parseCatalogue` keeps any
 *  non-empty string): printable ASCII, 1 to 64 characters, no space at either
 *  end. It only ever enters a JSON-encoded body, so this bounds it and no more. */
const EFFORT_RE = /^[\x21-\x7e](?:[\x20-\x7e]{0,62}[\x21-\x7e])?$/;
const KEYS = ['id', 'model', 'effort', 'timeout-s'];
const HOME = process.env['HOME'] ?? '';

let answered = false;
/** The one answer. Exits once stdout has taken it. */
function answer(o, code) {
  if (answered) return;
  answered = true;
  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify(o)}\n`, () => process.exit(code));
}
const usage = (detail) => answer({ ok: false, error: 'bad-argv', detail }, 2);

/** A reason as it may leave this process: the key and its hex, and anything
 *  shaped like a gateway key (an `sk-` that starts a word), replaced; printable
 *  ASCII; at most REASON_MAX. An ordinary word that merely contains `sk-`
 *  ("risk-free", "task-queue") is left as it is. */
function scrub(text, key) {
  let s = String(text);
  if (key !== null) s = s.split(key).join('sk-<redacted>').split(key.slice(3)).join('<redacted>');
  s = s.replace(/(?<![A-Za-z0-9])sk-[A-Za-z0-9._-]{4,}/g, 'sk-<redacted>');
  return s.replace(/[^\x20-\x7e]+/g, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, REASON_MAX);
}

/** A lane file, size-bounded before it is read, then read by `readRegular`,
 *  which refuses a FIFO or a directory at once (`ENOTREG`), never opening it. */
function readSmall(p, max) {
  if (statSync(p).size > max) throw Object.assign(new Error(`larger than ${max} bytes`), { code: 'ETOOBIG' });
  return readRegular(p);
}

/** The lane's proxy port and key, or `{why}`. A `why` never quotes a file. */
function laneInputs(id) {
  const dir = path.join(HOME, '.ccrc', 'codex', id);
  let port;
  try {
    const j = JSON.parse(readSmall(path.join(dir, 'lane.json'), LANE_JSON_MAX));
    port = j !== null && typeof j === 'object' ? j.proxyPort : undefined;
  } catch (e) {
    return { why: `lane.json could not be read (${typeof e.code === 'string' ? e.code : 'not JSON'})` };
  }
  if (!Number.isInteger(port) || port < 1 || port > 65535) return { why: 'lane.json names no proxyPort from 1 to 65535' };
  let text;
  try {
    text = readSmall(path.join(dir, 'runtime.env'), RUNTIME_ENV_MAX);
  } catch (e) {
    return { why: `runtime.env could not be read (${typeof e.code === 'string' ? e.code : 'unreadable'})` };
  }
  const m = KEY_LINE.exec(text);
  if (m === null) return { why: 'runtime.env is not one LITELLM_MASTER_KEY line' };
  return { port, key: m[1] };
}

/** `{error: "…"}` (the shim's one refusal shape) or `{error: {message}}`
 *  (LiteLLM's and the Anthropic API's), or null. */
function errorText(text) {
  try {
    const j = JSON.parse(text);
    if (j !== null && typeof j === 'object') {
      if (typeof j.error === 'string') return j.error;
      if (j.error !== null && typeof j.error === 'object' && typeof j.error.message === 'string') return j.error.message;
    }
  } catch { /* not JSON: the body itself is the reason */ }
  return null;
}

/** The lane a `GET /ccgpt/lane` answer names, or null: a 200, `application/json`,
 *  and an object whose only key is a string `lane` (`ccd/ccrc`'s
 *  `_codex_lane_answer` reads the same shape). */
function laneOf(status, type, text) {
  if (status !== 200 || !/^\s*application\/json\s*(;.*)?$/i.test(type)) return null;
  try {
    const j = JSON.parse(text);
    if (j === null || typeof j !== 'object' || Array.isArray(j)) return null;
    const keys = Object.keys(j);
    return keys.length === 1 && keys[0] === 'lane' && typeof j.lane === 'string' ? j.lane : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function send(port, key, id, model, effort, timeoutS) {
  const agent = new Agent({ keepAlive: false, maxSockets: 1 });
  const body = JSON.stringify({
    model, max_tokens: 512, stream: true,
    messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Reply with the single word OK.' }],
    ...(effort === null ? {} : { output_config: { effort } }),
  });
  let req = null;
  let timer = null;
  let got200 = false;
  const finish = (result, status, reason) => {
    if (timer !== null) clearTimeout(timer);
    answer({ ok: true, op: 'canary', result, status, reason: reason === null ? null : scrub(reason, key) }, 0);
    if (req !== null) req.destroy();
    agent.destroy();
  };
  const refusedOr = (e, otherwise) => {
    if (e.code === 'ECONNREFUSED') finish('not-ready', null, `the lane's proxy on 127.0.0.1:${port} refused the connection`);
    else otherwise(e);
  };
  timer = setTimeout(() => finish('not-ready', got200 ? 200 : null, got200
    ? `the lane answered 200 but sent no text within ${timeoutS}s`
    : `no text from the lane within ${timeoutS}s`), timeoutS * 1000);

  // 1. THE LANE PROBE: no key, and nothing keyed unless it answers as `id`.
  req = request({
    host: '127.0.0.1', port, method: 'GET', path: '/ccgpt/lane', agent, headers: { accept: 'application/json' },
  });
  req.on('error', (e) => refusedOr(e, (x) => finish('unavailable', null,
    `the lane probe on 127.0.0.1:${port} failed (socket: ${x.code ?? x.message}), so the key was not sent`)));
  req.on('response', (res) => {
    const status = res.statusCode ?? 0;
    const type = String(res.headers['content-type'] ?? '');
    let text = '';
    res.setEncoding('utf8');
    res.on('error', (e) => finish('unavailable', null,
      `the lane probe on 127.0.0.1:${port} failed (socket: ${e.code ?? e.message}), so the key was not sent`));
    res.on('data', (c) => { if (text.length < LANE_PROBE_CAP) text += c.slice(0, LANE_PROBE_CAP - text.length); });
    res.on('end', () => {
      if (laneOf(status, type, text) !== id) {
        finish('unavailable', null, `127.0.0.1:${port} does not answer as ${id}'s shim, so the key was not sent`);
        return;
      }
      post();
    });
  });
  req.end();

  // 2. THE KEYED REQUEST, to a listener that just answered as this lane.
  function post() {
    req = request({
      host: '127.0.0.1', port, method: 'POST', path: '/v1/messages', agent,
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${key}`, 'content-type': 'application/json', 'anthropic-version': '2023-06-01',
        accept: 'text/event-stream', 'content-length': Buffer.byteLength(body),
      },
    });
    req.on('error', (e) => refusedOr(e, (x) => finish('failed', null, `socket: ${x.code ?? x.message}`)));
    req.on('response', (res) => {
      const status = res.statusCode ?? 0;
      res.setEncoding('utf8');
      res.on('error', (e) => finish('failed', status, `socket: ${e.code ?? e.message}`));
      if (status !== 200) {
        let text = '';
        res.on('data', (c) => { if (text.length < ERROR_BODY_CAP) text += c.slice(0, ERROR_BODY_CAP - text.length); });
        res.on('end', () => {
          const err = errorText(text);
          if (status === 502 && err !== null && err.startsWith(D4933_PREFIX)) finish('not-ready', 502, err);
          else finish('failed', status, `http ${status}: ${err ?? text}`);
        });
        return;
      }
      got200 = true;
      const type = String(res.headers['content-type'] ?? '');
      let buf = '';
      let seen = 0;
      let stop = null;
      res.on('data', (chunk) => {
        seen += chunk.length;
        buf += chunk;
        let nl = buf.indexOf('\n');
        while (nl !== -1) {
          const line = buf.slice(0, nl).replace(/\r$/, '');
          buf = buf.slice(nl + 1);
          nl = buf.indexOf('\n');
          if (!line.startsWith('data:')) continue;
          let ev;
          try { ev = JSON.parse(line.slice(5)); } catch { continue; }
          if (ev === null || typeof ev !== 'object') continue;
          if (ev.type === 'content_block_delta' && ev.delta?.type === 'text_delta'
              && typeof ev.delta.text === 'string' && ev.delta.text.trim() !== '') {
            finish('passed', 200, null);
            return;
          }
          if (ev.type === 'error') {
            finish('failed', 200, `stream-error: ${typeof ev.error?.type === 'string' ? ev.error.type : 'unknown'}`);
            return;
          }
          if (ev.type === 'message_delta' && typeof ev.delta?.stop_reason === 'string') stop = ev.delta.stop_reason;
        }
        if (seen > READ_CAP) finish('failed', 200, `no-text: no text in the first ${READ_CAP} bytes`);
      });
      res.on('end', () => finish('failed', 200, /text\/event-stream/.test(type)
        ? `no-text: the stream ended${stop === null ? '' : ` (stop_reason ${stop})`} before any text`
        : `no-text: the answer was not a stream (${type === '' ? 'no content-type' : type})`));
    });
    req.end(body);
  }
}

function main(argv) {
  const got = {};
  for (let i = 2; i < argv.length; i += 2) {
    const k = argv[i];
    if (typeof k !== 'string' || !k.startsWith('--') || !KEYS.includes(k.slice(2))) {
      return usage(`${JSON.stringify(k ?? '')} is not one of --${KEYS.join(', --')}`);
    }
    const v = argv[i + 1];
    if (typeof v !== 'string' || v.startsWith('--')) return usage(`${k} needs a value`);
    got[k.slice(2)] = v;
  }
  const { id, model } = got;
  const effort = got.effort ?? 'none';
  if (typeof id !== 'string' || !MODELS_LANE_ID_RE.test(id)) return usage('--id must be a lane id');
  if (typeof model !== 'string' || !MODEL_ID_RE.test(model)) return usage('--model must be a model id');
  if (!EFFORT_RE.test(effort)) return usage('--effort must be 1 to 64 printable characters, or none');
  let timeoutS = CANARY_TIMEOUT_S;
  if (got['timeout-s'] !== undefined) {
    const t = got['timeout-s'];
    if (!/^[0-9]{1,3}$/.test(t) || Number(t) < 1 || Number(t) > TIMEOUT_MAX_S) {
      return usage(`--timeout-s must be a whole number from 1 to ${TIMEOUT_MAX_S}`);
    }
    timeoutS = Number(t);
  }
  const lane = laneInputs(id);
  if (lane.why !== undefined) {
    return answer({ ok: true, op: 'canary', result: 'unavailable', status: null, reason: lane.why }, 0);
  }
  return send(lane.port, lane.key, id, model, effort === 'none' ? null : effort, timeoutS);
}

main(process.argv);
```

```ts
// through `ccd/ccrc` SOURCED with the lane library's tier question redefined by

/** `ccrc-models.test.ts`'s box: the tree `ccrc` resolves against, `deploy` and
```
