```ts
  });

  describe('the op reaches no exec path — read from the source', () => {
    const src = readFileSync(SERVER_TS, 'utf8');
    const port = readFileSync(MODELSOP_TS, 'utf8');

    it("handleReq's models case names no exec-surface call, builds its argv from the one builder, and spawns only through the port", () => {
      const handle = slice(src, 'async function handleReq(', /\n\}\n/);
      const body = slice(handle, "case 'models': {", CASE_END);
      expect(body).not.toMatch(EXEC_PATH);
      expect(body).toMatch(/const file = updateLauncherPath\(ctx\.cfg\.home\);/);
      expect(body).toMatch(/const argv = modelsSpawnArgv\(req\.lane, req\.action, /);
      expect(body).toMatch(/ctx\.spawnModels\(file, argv, MODELS_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS\)/);
      expect(body.match(/\bspawnModels\s*\(/g), 'one call site').toHaveLength(1);
    });

    it("validateReq's models case calls the three guards and restates no pattern or word list", () => {
      const validate = slice(src, 'function validateReq(', /\n\}\n/);
      const body = slice(validate, "case 'models': {", CASE_END);
      expect(body).toMatch(/isModelsLaneId\(lane\)/);
      expect(body).toMatch(/isModelsAction\(action\)/);
      expect(body).toMatch(/isModelsClass\(cls\)/);
      expect(body).toMatch(/refuse: 'bad-lane'/);
      expect(body).toMatch(/refuse: 'bad-action'/);
      expect(body).toMatch(/refuse: 'bad-class'/);
      expect(body, 'the lane pattern is restated here').not.toMatch(/MODELS_LANE_ID_RE|\[a-z\]|\{0,31\}|'refresh'|'litellm'/);
    });

    it('the port names no exec path, closes stdin, caps stdout, and hands the child only its explicit env', () => {
      expect(port).not.toMatch(EXEC_PATH);
      expect(port).toMatch(/spawn\(file, \[\.\.\.args\], \{ detached: true, stdio: \['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'\], env: childEnv \}\)/);
      expect(port, 'the port reads the agent environment itself').not.toMatch(/env:\s*process\.env|\.\.\.process\.env/);
      expect(port).toMatch(/max: MODELS_ANSWER_MAX_BYTES/);
      const factory = slice(port, 'export function makeModelsSpawn(', /\n\}\n/);
      expect(factory, 'the factory reads process.env').not.toMatch(/process\.env/);
    });

    it('ccrc stays off the exec surface: the exec op refuses both shapes', () => {
      expect([...EXEC_COMMANDS]).toEqual(['tmux', 'ccd']);
      for (const argv of [modelsSpawnArgv('lane-a', 'show'), modelsSpawnArgv('lane-a', 'hold', CLASSES[0])]) {
        expect(isExecAllowed('ccrc', [...argv])).toBe(false);
        expect(isExecAllowed(updateLauncherPath('/h'), [...argv])).toBe(false);
      }
    });

    it('agent/CLAUDE.md and server.ts count THREE wire-triggered spawns, and CLAUDE.md names the models op and its guards', () => {
      const md = readFileSync(AGENT_CLAUDE_MD, 'utf8').replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
      expect(md).toContain('is one of the THREE wire-triggered spawns outside the exec whitelist');
      expect(md).not.toContain('one of the TWO wire-triggered spawns');
      for (const needle of ['The **`models` op**', '`isModelsLaneId`', '`modelsSpawnArgv`', '`{HOME, PATH, LANG}`']) {
        expect(md, needle).toContain(needle);
      }
      // The source's own comments read as history in this repository, so a count they state must be the tree's.
      const flat = src.replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
      expect(flat, 'a comment in server.ts still counts two').not.toMatch(/\b(?:One|one) of the TWO\b/);
      expect(flat).toContain('One of the THREE wire-triggered spawns outside the');
    });
  });

  it("modelsEnv is exactly HOME, PATH and LANG, the agent's node directory first on PATH", () => {
    expect(modelsEnv('/h', { PATH: '/p', LANG: 'en_US.UTF-8', CCRC_AGENT_TOKEN: 'x', CCRC_MODELS_LOCK_S: '1', HOME: '/e' }, '/n'))
      .toEqual({ HOME: '/h', PATH: '/n:/p', LANG: 'en_US.UTF-8' });
    expect(modelsEnv('/h', {}, '/n')).toEqual({ HOME: '/h', PATH: '/n:/usr/bin:/bin', LANG: 'C' });
    expect(modelsEnv('/h', {}).PATH.split(':')[0]).toBe(path.dirname(process.execPath));
  });

  describe('the real port — one real child, under the fixture HOME', () => {
    // CONTAINMENT: every launcher is the fixture's absolute path, and PATH and HOME are cut to the fixture and the
    // system directories for these cases, restored whether the case passed or threw.
    const saved = { PATH: process.env.PATH, HOME: process.env.HOME, CCRC_AGENT_TOKEN: process.env.CCRC_AGENT_TOKEN };
    function contain(home: string, pathValue = '/usr/bin:/bin'): void {
      process.env.PATH = pathValue;
      process.env.HOME = home;
      // Planted in the agent's own environment, built from pieces: the child must never see it.
      process.env.CCRC_AGENT_TOKEN = ['planted', 'agent', 'bearer'].join('-');
    }
    afterEach(() => {
      for (const k of ['PATH', 'HOME', 'CCRC_AGENT_TOKEN'] as const) {
        if (saved[k] === undefined) delete process.env[k]; else process.env[k] = saved[k];
      }
    });
    function plantLauncher(home: string, body: string): string {
      const bin = path.join(home, '.local', 'bin');
      mkdirSync(bin, { recursive: true });
      const file = path.join(bin, 'ccrc');
      writeFileSync(file, `#!/bin/sh\n${body}\n`);
      chmodSync(file, 0o755);
      return file;
    }
    /** A launcher line that prints one SMALL object through whatever `node` the child's PATH finds. The object rides
     *  one argv string, and Linux refuses a single argument past 128 KiB (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`, E2BIG), so a large answer
     *  is built inside the child instead (the under-the-cap case below). */
    const printViaNode = (obj: unknown): string =>
      `exec node -e 'process.stdout.write(process.argv[1] + "\\n")' '${JSON.stringify(obj)}'`;

    it("is the agent's default: exact argv, and an environment of exactly three names with the agent's node first", async () => {
      fixture = makeFixture();
      contain(fixture.home);
      const h = fixture.home;
      plantLauncher(h, [
        `printf '%s\\n' "$0" "$@" > '${h}/argv'`,
        `/usr/bin/env > '${h}/env'`,
        `echo '${JSON.stringify(SHOWN)}'`,
      ].join('\n'));
      agent = await boot(fixture);   // NO spawnModels: startAgent's default is the thing under test
      const c = await open(agent.port);
      expect(await c.req<Res>(1, { op: 'models', lane: 'lane-a', action: 'hold', class: CLASSES[1] }))
        .toEqual({ t: 'res', id: 1, ok: true, exit: 0, answer: SHOWN });
      expect(readFileSync(path.join(h, 'argv'), 'utf8'))
        .toBe([path.join(h, '.local', 'bin', 'ccrc'), 'models', 'lane-a', 'hold', CLASSES[1], ''].join('\n'));
      const env = readFileSync(path.join(h, 'env'), 'utf8');
      expect(env, 'the agent bearer reached the child').not.toContain('CCRC_AGENT_TOKEN');
      expect(env).not.toContain(['planted', 'agent', 'bearer'].join('-'));
      const names = env.split('\n').filter((l) => l.includes('=')).map((l) => l.slice(0, l.indexOf('=')));
      // The shell may add its own bookkeeping names (PWD, OLDPWD, SHLVL, _); nothing else of the agent's.
      expect(names.filter((n) => !['PWD', 'OLDPWD', 'SHLVL', '_'].includes(n)).sort()).toEqual(['HOME', 'LANG', 'PATH']);
      expect(env).toContain(`HOME=${h}\n`);
      expect(env).toContain(`PATH=${path.dirname(process.execPath)}:/usr/bin:/bin\n`);
    });

    it("a child PATH without node still finds the agent's own (Review Focus line 5, D-5227)", async () => {
      fixture = makeFixture();
      const h = fixture.home;
      const empty = path.join(h, 'no-node-bin');
      mkdirSync(empty, { recursive: true });
      contain(h, empty);   // the agent's own PATH names one empty directory and nothing else
      plantLauncher(h, printViaNode(SHOWN));
      agent = await boot(fixture);
      const c = await open(agent.port);
      expect(await c.req<Res>(1, { op: 'models', lane: 'lane-a', action: 'show' }))
        .toEqual({ t: 'res', id: 1, ok: true, exit: 0, answer: SHOWN });
      // The control: the same launcher under the same PATH with no node directory in front is a named no-answer, the
      // shell's own sentence about `node` as its detail — never spawn-failed, which would say the launcher is missing.
      const r = await makeModelsSpawn({ HOME: h, PATH: empty, LANG: 'C' })(path.join(h, '.local', 'bin', 'ccrc'),
        modelsSpawnArgv('lane-a', 'show'), 10_000);
      const a = modelsAnswer(r);
      expect(a).toMatchObject({ ok: false, err: 'no-answer' });
      expect(a.ok ? '' : a.detail).toMatch(/node/);
    });

    it('a launcher that is not there is spawn-failed naming why', async () => {
      fixture = makeFixture();
      contain(fixture.home);
      agent = await boot(fixture);
      const c = await open(agent.port);
      expect(await c.req<Res>(1, { op: 'models', lane: 'lane-a', action: 'show' }))
        .toEqual({ t: 'res', id: 1, ok: false, err: 'spawn-failed', detail: 'could not start the launcher (ENOENT)' });
    });

    it('stdout past the cap is no-answer, never a cut object (Review Focus line 5)', async () => {
      fixture = makeFixture();
      contain(fixture.home);
      const h = fixture.home;
      plantLauncher(h, `exec node -e 'process.stdout.write("x".repeat(${MODELS_ANSWER_MAX_BYTES + 1}))'`);
      const r = await makeModelsSpawn(modelsEnv(h))(path.join(h, '.local', 'bin', 'ccrc'), modelsSpawnArgv('lane-a', 'show'), 10_000);
      expect([r.capped, r.stdout]).toEqual([true, null]);
      expect(modelsAnswer(r)).toEqual({ ok: false, err: 'no-answer',
        detail: `the child's answer passed the ${MODELS_ANSWER_MAX_BYTES}-byte cap` });
    });

    it('an answer under the cap is read whole', async () => {
      fixture = makeFixture();
      contain(fixture.home);
      const h = fixture.home;
      // Built INSIDE the child: as one argv string this object (about 256 KiB) would fail the exec with E2BIG.
      const PAD = MODELS_ANSWER_MAX_BYTES - 64;
      plantLauncher(h, `exec node -e 'process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ok:true,pad:"p".repeat(${PAD})})+"\\n")'`);
      const r = await makeModelsSpawn(modelsEnv(h))(path.join(h, '.local', 'bin', 'ccrc'), modelsSpawnArgv('lane-a', 'show'), 10_000);
      expect([r.capped, (r.stdout ?? '').length < MODELS_ANSWER_MAX_BYTES]).toEqual([false, true]);
      expect(modelsAnswer(r)).toEqual({ ok: true, exit: 0, answer: { ok: true, pad: 'p'.repeat(PAD) } });
    });

    it('stderr past its cap keeps its HEAD: an older ccrc is still named by its first line, and the capture stays bounded (Review Focus line 5)', async () => {
      fixture = makeFixture();
      contain(fixture.home);
      const h = fixture.home;
      // The missing-verb line, then far more than the cap: a usage text that grew, or a child that will not stop.
      const tail = MODELS_STDERR_MAX_BYTES + 6 * 1024;
      plantLauncher(h, `exec node -e 'process.stderr.write(${JSON.stringify(`${MODELS_VERB_MISSING_LINE}\n`)} + "x".repeat(${tail})); process.exitCode = 2'`);
      const r = await makeModelsSpawn(modelsEnv(h))(path.join(h, '.local', 'bin', 'ccrc'), modelsSpawnArgv('lane-a', 'show'), 10_000);
      expect(Buffer.byteLength(r.stderr), 'the stderr capture is not bounded').toBeLessThanOrEqual(MODELS_STDERR_MAX_BYTES);
      expect(r.stderr.startsWith(`${MODELS_VERB_MISSING_LINE}\n`), 'the head was thrown away at the cap').toBe(true);
      expect(modelsAnswer(r)).toEqual({ ok: false, err: 'no-answer', detail: MODELS_VERB_MISSING_LINE });
    });

    it('at the bound the group gets SIGTERM first (the trap runs), then SIGKILL after the grace, and the answer is timeout', async () => {
      fixture = makeFixture();
      contain(fixture.home);
      const h = fixture.home;
      // Traps TERM and keeps running, so only the SIGKILL ends it: the trap's record proves TERM came first.
      const file = plantLauncher(h, [
        `trap "echo TERM >> '${h}/sig'" TERM`,
        'while :; do sleep 0.05; done',
      ].join('\n'));
      const t0 = Date.now();
      const r = await makeModelsSpawn(modelsEnv(h))(file, modelsSpawnArgv('lane-a', 'show'), 300);
      const took = Date.now() - t0;
      expect(r.killed).toBe(true);
      expect(readFileSync(path.join(h, 'sig'), 'utf8')).toBe('TERM\n');
      expect(took, 'SIGKILL came before the grace').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(300 + MODELS_KILL_GRACE_MS - 100);
      expect(took).toBeLessThan(300 + MODELS_KILL_GRACE_MS + 2_500);
      expect(modelsAnswer(r)).toEqual({ ok: false, err: 'timeout',
        detail: `the ccrc child was stopped at the ${MODELS_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS} ms bound` });
      expect(existsSync(path.join(h, 'sig'))).toBe(true);
    });
  });
});
```

```ts
// Layer 4c (auto-advance plan W4 Task 17): the `models` op is the THIRD wire-triggered spawn outside the exec
// whitelist. The same two properties as layers 4 and 4b, for its own port: its case and its port name no exec-surface
// symbol, `spawnModels(` has exactly one call site, inside `case 'models'` of handleReq, and every line that NAMES the
// port is pinned, so an alias of it is a new line here.
describe('layer 4c — the models op is not an exec path, and its spawn port has one caller', () => {
  let readFileSync: typeof import('node:fs').readFileSync;
  let readdirSync: typeof import('node:fs').readdirSync;
  let path: typeof import('node:path');
  let SRC_DIR = '';
  let serverSrc = '';
  let handleReq = '';
  const EXEC_PATH = /\b(?:isExecAllowed|runExec|resolveSpawnCmd|checkPath)\s*\(|\bEXEC_WHITELIST\b/;
  const code = (src: string): string => src.split('\n').filter((l) => !/^\s*(?:\/\/|\/\*|\*)/.test(l)).map((l) => l.replace(/\s\/\/.*$/, '')).join('\n');
  const CASE_END = /\n    (?:case '|default:)/;
  function caseBody(src: string, word: string): string {
    const open = `case '${word}': {`;
    const at = src.indexOf(open);
    expect(at, `${open} not found`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
    const rest = src.slice(at + open.length);
    const end = CASE_END.exec(rest);
    expect(end, `no end after ${open}`).not.toBeNull();
    return rest.slice(0, end!.index);
  }
  beforeAll(async () => {
    ({ readFileSync, readdirSync } = await import('node:fs'));
    path = await import('node:path');
    const { fileURLToPath } = await import('node:url');
    SRC_DIR = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..', 'agent', 'src');
    serverSrc = readFileSync(path.join(SRC_DIR, 'server.ts'), 'utf8');
    const at = serverSrc.indexOf('async function handleReq(');
    expect(at, 'handleReq not found').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
    const rest = serverSrc.slice(at);
    const end = /\n\}\n/.exec(rest);
    expect(end, 'no end after handleReq').not.toBeNull();
    handleReq = rest.slice(0, end!.index);
  });

  it("(a) `case 'models'` and agent/src/modelsop.ts name no exec-surface symbol", () => {
    const body = caseBody(handleReq, 'models');
    expect(code(body)).not.toMatch(EXEC_PATH);
    expect(code(body), 'the cut is the models op, not an empty slice').toMatch(/\bspawnModels\s*\(/);
    expect(code(readFileSync(path.join(SRC_DIR, 'modelsop.ts'), 'utf8'))).not.toMatch(EXEC_PATH);
  });

  it("(b) `spawnModels(` is called exactly once in agent/src, inside `case 'models'`, and nowhere outside it", () => {
    const body = caseBody(handleReq, 'models');
    const call = /\bspawnModels\s*\(/g;
    expect(code(body).match(call)?.length ?? 0, "one call inside case 'models'").toBe(1);
    const outside = serverSrc.replace(body, '');
    expect(outside.length, 'the case was cut out of the scan').toBeLessThan(serverSrc.length);
    expect(code(outside).match(call)?.length ?? 0, "call sites outside case 'models' in server.ts").toBe(0);
    for (const f of readdirSync(SRC_DIR).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.ts') && n !== 'server.ts')) {
      expect(code(readFileSync(path.join(SRC_DIR, f), 'utf8')).match(call)?.length ?? 0, `${f} calls spawnModels(`).toBe(0);
    }
  });

  it('(b) `spawnModels` is named only where the port is declared, carried and called, and its factory only where it is defined and defaulted', () => {
    const lines = (word: RegExp): string[] => code(serverSrc).split('\n').filter((l) => word.test(l)).map((l) => l.trim());
    expect(lines(/\bspawnModels\b/)).toEqual([
      'spawnModels?: ModelsSpawn;',
      'spawnModels: ModelsSpawn;',
      'spawned = await ctx.spawnModels(file, argv, MODELS_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS);',
      'spawnModels: opts.spawnModels,',
      'spawnModels: rawOpts.spawnModels ?? makeModelsSpawn(modelsEnv(rawOpts.home ?? os.homedir())),',
    ]);
    expect(lines(/\bmakeModelsSpawn\b/).filter((l) => !l.startsWith('import'))).toEqual([
      'spawnModels: rawOpts.spawnModels ?? makeModelsSpawn(modelsEnv(rawOpts.home ?? os.homedir())),',
    ]);
    for (const f of readdirSync(SRC_DIR).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.ts') && n !== 'server.ts' && n !== 'modelsop.ts')) {
      expect(code(readFileSync(path.join(SRC_DIR, f), 'utf8')), `${f} names the models spawn port`)
        .not.toMatch(/\b(?:spawnModels|makeModelsSpawn)\b/);
    }
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: The port, `agent/src/modelsop.ts`**

```ts
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import {
  MODELS_ANSWER_MAX_BYTES, MODELS_DRAIN_MS, MODELS_KILL_GRACE_MS, MODELS_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS, firstStderrLine,
  type ModelsOpError,
} from '../../shared/agent-protocol.js';
import { tokenSyncEnv, type TokenSyncEnv } from './tokensync.js';

/**
 * The `models` op's spawn port (auto-advance spec 2026-10-13 §2.7, D14; plan W4 Task 17). The THIRD wire-triggered
 * spawn outside the exec whitelist, after the `update` op's and the `token-sync` op's, and like both it is NOT
 * `runExec`: `ccrc` is on neither exec list, and the argv is one of two frozen shapes (`modelsSpawnArgv`).
 *
 * Its OWN bounded body, for D-4390's reason (`tokensync.ts`): not a third copy of the update op's pinned twin and not
 * the token-sync body with options. What differs from token-sync's, each on purpose:
 *  - stdin is closed (`'ignore'`): the verb reads nothing, and an open pipe would only be a way for it to wait.
 *  - stdout is the ANSWER here, one JSON object that a `show` makes a few KiB long, so its cap is
 *    `MODELS_ANSWER_MAX_BYTES` and a cap hit is its own flag, `capped`, never folded into "no EOF".
 *  - the child's PATH begins with the directory of the `node` running this agent
 *    (D-5227, `modelsEnv`): `ccrc models` runs `deploy/models-op.mjs` under
 *    `node`, and a user unit's PATH may name none.
 * Shared with it: the explicit three-name environment, never `process.env` (which carries `CCRC_AGENT_TOKEN`); the
 * child as its own process group, so the bound reaches the `node` it runs; SIGTERM at the bound, so the verb's traps
 * run, and SIGKILL `MODELS_KILL_GRACE_MS` later; one drain deadline. `server/test/update-spawn-twin-bodies.test.ts`
 * holds that this file carries no twin sentinel.
 *
 * Production is the port `startAgent` builds from `makeModelsSpawn(modelsEnv(home))`; tests inject a recorder through
 * `AgentOpts.spawnModels`.
 */
export type ModelsSpawn = (file: string, args: readonly string[], timeoutMs: number) => Promise<ModelsSpawnResult>;

/** What the bounded models spawner answers. `stdout` is the child's whole stdout read to EOF, or `null` when EOF was
 *  not reached within the drain, a read failed, or the cap was hit: `null` is "not measured", never "empty", and
 *  `capped` says when it was the cap. `stderr` is at most `MODELS_STDERR_MAX_BYTES`, its head kept. `killed` is true
 *  when the bound fired. `pid` is null only when the spawn itself failed. */
export interface ModelsSpawnResult {
  code: number; stdout: string | null; stderr: string; killed: boolean; capped: boolean; pid: number | null;
}

/** The child's whole environment: `tokenSyncEnv`'s three names, with the agent's own node directory first on PATH
 *  (D-5227). Still exactly HOME, PATH and LANG: none of the agent's own
 *  variables, and no models knob (the lock wait, the clock), reaches the verb. Named here by none of their names:
 *  `single-definition.test.ts` holds each of those knobs to the one file that reads it. */
export function modelsEnv(
  home: string, from: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env, nodeDir: string = path.dirname(process.execPath),
): TokenSyncEnv {
  const base = tokenSyncEnv(home, from);
  return { HOME: base.HOME, PATH: `${nodeDir}:${base.PATH}`, LANG: base.LANG };
}

/** The verb's stderr is one sentence on a refusal and a short summary on `show`; past this the capture stops
 *  GROWING, and what it already holds is KEPT: the head is where `ccrc` says why it printed no answer (an older ccrc's
 *  usage refusal is its first line, its usage text after it), and `modelsAnswer` reads the first line. Exported for
 *  the test that holds the capture to it. */
export const MODELS_STDERR_MAX_BYTES = 65_536;

/**
 * The verb under a bound. The child is its own PROCESS GROUP (`detached`, pgid = pid). Answers, kept apart:
 *  - `killed` — the child was still running at `timeoutMs`: the group got SIGTERM, and SIGKILL
 *    `MODELS_KILL_GRACE_MS` later unless the child had exited by then.
 *  - A spawn error (`ENOENT`/`EACCES`): code 1, `pid: null`, and the sentence `could not start the launcher (<code>)`,
 *    the other two ports' own words.
 *  - Every other exit — the child's code (`128 + signo` for a signal that was not ours), its stdout and stderr.
 * The answer comes once the child has exited and both pipes reached EOF, or at ONE drain deadline armed by the exit or
 * by the SIGKILL, whichever comes first, never restarted: within `timeoutMs + MODELS_KILL_GRACE_MS + MODELS_DRAIN_MS`
 * of the spawn. Nothing resolves twice.
 */
export function makeModelsSpawn(env: TokenSyncEnv): ModelsSpawn {
  // Copied name by name, so a caller's object with more fields still hands the child exactly three.
  const childEnv: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = { HOME: env.HOME, PATH: env.PATH, LANG: env.LANG };
  return (file, args, timeoutMs) => new Promise((resolve) => {
    let settled = false;
    let exited: { code: number } | null = null;
    let killed = false;
    let termTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
    let killTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
    let drainTimer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
    // Two caps, two policies: stdout past its cap is NO answer, so nothing of it is kept (`keepHead: false`); stderr
    // past its cap keeps its head (`keepHead: true`), the line that says why.
    const out = { chunks: [] as Buffer[], bytes: 0, max: MODELS_ANSWER_MAX_BYTES, keepHead: false, capped: false, broken: false, eof: false };
    const err = { chunks: [] as Buffer[], bytes: 0, max: MODELS_STDERR_MAX_BYTES, keepHead: true, capped: false, broken: false, eof: false };
    const child = spawn(file, [...args], { detached: true, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'], env: childEnv });
    const clear = (): void => {
      for (const t of [termTimer, killTimer, drainTimer]) if (t !== null) clearTimeout(t);
      termTimer = killTimer = drainTimer = null;
    };
    const finish = (r: ModelsSpawnResult): void => {
      if (settled) return;
      settled = true;
      clear();
      child.stdout?.destroy();
      child.stderr?.destroy();
      resolve(r);
    };
    const answer = (): void => {
      if (exited === null) return;
      finish({
        code: exited.code,
        stdout: out.eof && !out.capped && !out.broken ? Buffer.concat(out.chunks).toString('utf8') : null,
        stderr: Buffer.concat(err.chunks).toString('utf8'),
        killed,
        capped: out.capped,
        pid: child.pid ?? null,
      });
    };
    const armDrain = (): void => {
      if (drainTimer !== null) return;
      drainTimer = setTimeout(() => { exited ??= { code: 1 }; answer(); }, MODELS_DRAIN_MS);
    };
    const signalGroup = (signal: 'SIGTERM' | 'SIGKILL'): void => {
      if (child.pid === undefined) return;
      try { process.kill(-child.pid, signal); } catch (e) {
        // ESRCH: the group is already gone. Anything else: fall back to the child alone rather than to nothing.
        if ((e as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'ESRCH') child.kill(signal);
      }
    };
    const take = (buf: typeof out) => (chunk: Buffer): void => {
      if (buf.capped) return;
      if (buf.bytes + chunk.length > buf.max) {
        buf.capped = true;
        if (buf.keepHead) {
          buf.chunks.push(chunk.subarray(0, buf.max - buf.bytes));
          buf.bytes = buf.max;
        } else {
          buf.chunks = [];
        }
        return;
      }
      buf.chunks.push(chunk);
      buf.bytes += chunk.length;
    };
    const broke = (buf: typeof out, other: typeof out) => (): void => {
      buf.broken = true;
      buf.eof = true;
      if (other.eof) answer();
    };
    child.stdout?.on('data', take(out));
    child.stderr?.on('data', take(err));
    child.stdout?.on('end', () => { out.eof = true; if (err.eof) answer(); });
    child.stderr?.on('end', () => { err.eof = true; if (out.eof) answer(); });
    child.stdout?.on('error', broke(out, err));
    child.stderr?.on('error', broke(err, out));
    child.on('error', (e: NodeJS.ErrnoException) => {
      if (child.pid !== undefined) return;
      finish({
        code: 1, stdout: '', killed: false, capped: false, pid: null,
        stderr: `could not start the launcher (${typeof e.code === 'string' ? e.code : 'unknown'})`,
      });
    });
    child.once('exit', (exitCode, signal) => {
      if (termTimer !== null) { clearTimeout(termTimer); termTimer = null; }
      if (killTimer !== null) { clearTimeout(killTimer); killTimer = null; }
      const signo = signal === null ? undefined : os.constants.signals[signal];
      exited = { code: typeof exitCode === 'number' ? exitCode : signo !== undefined ? 128 + signo : 1 };
      if (out.eof && err.eof) { answer(); return; }
      armDrain();
    });
    termTimer = setTimeout(() => {
      termTimer = null;
      if (exited !== null || child.pid === undefined) return;
      killed = true;
      signalGroup('SIGTERM');
      killTimer = setTimeout(() => {
        killTimer = null;
        if (exited !== null) return;
        signalGroup('SIGKILL');
        // A child that will not die (an uninterruptible wait) must not stop the answer past the drain bound.
        armDrain();
      }, MODELS_KILL_GRACE_MS);
    }, timeoutMs);
  });
}

/** The op's answer, mapped from the child. ONE OBJECT IS AN ANSWER, whatever it says: a verb's own refusal
 *  (`lock-busy`, `no-previous`, an older ccrc's `unknown-subcommand`) travels as `ok` with its exit code, and the
 *  server reads it. Only a child that never printed exactly one object is a refusal of the op. */
export type ModelsAnswer =
  | { ok: true; exit: 0 | 1 | 2; answer: Record<string, unknown> }
  | { ok: false; err: Extract<ModelsOpError, 'spawn-failed' | 'timeout' | 'no-answer'>; detail: string };

/** The ONE mapping. Killed at the bound → `timeout`, naming the bound. The child may have written before it was
 *  stopped, and what covers each verb this op spawns differs: a hold or a release is one atomic write; a revert writes
 *  its hold FIRST (D-5206), so one cut short after its registry moved leaves the class held, its
 *  `previous` still on record, and its lane files to the hourly refresh's re-materialise; and the kernel drops the
 *  lane-files lock with the killed group. A spawn that never started → `spawn-failed`.
 *  The cap → `no-answer`, naming it. Exactly one JSON object on stdout, at exit 0, 1 or 2 → `ok`. Anything else →
 *  `no-answer` with the first stderr line (`firstStderrLine`: printable, cut to 200), which is where `ccrc` says why
 *  it printed no object — a missing `node` or `jq`, or a ccrc with no `models` verb at all. */
export function modelsAnswer(r: ModelsSpawnResult): ModelsAnswer {
  if (r.killed) return { ok: false, err: 'timeout', detail: `the ccrc child was stopped at the ${MODELS_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS} ms bound` };
  if (r.pid === null) return { ok: false, err: 'spawn-failed', detail: firstStderrLine(r.stderr) };
  if (r.capped) return { ok: false, err: 'no-answer', detail: `the child's answer passed the ${MODELS_ANSWER_MAX_BYTES}-byte cap` };
  const answer = r.stdout === null ? null : oneObject(r.stdout);
  if (answer === null) return { ok: false, err: 'no-answer', detail: firstStderrLine(r.stderr) };
  if (r.code !== 0 && r.code !== 1 && r.code !== 2) {
    return { ok: false, err: 'no-answer', detail: `ccrc exited ${r.code}, outside its 0/1/2 contract, after printing its answer` };
  }
  return { ok: true, exit: r.code as 0 | 1 | 2, answer };
}

/** Exactly one JSON object and one optional trailing newline, or null: two lines, an array, a bare value and an
 *  empty stdout are not an answer. */
function oneObject(stdout: string): Record<string, unknown> | null {
  const body = stdout.endsWith('\n') ? stdout.slice(0, -1) : stdout;
  if (body === '' || body.includes('\n')) return null;
  let v: unknown;
  try { v = JSON.parse(body); } catch { return null; }
  return typeof v === 'object' && v !== null && !Array.isArray(v) ? (v as Record<string, unknown>) : null;
}
```

```ts
/** `validateReq`'s answer for a well-shaped op whose ARGUMENT failed its guard
 *  (design 2026-09-20 §10). The message handler sends it as
 *  `fail(req.id, req.refuse)` before any case body runs. It covers the `update`
 *  op (`bad-tag`, `bad-kind`), the `token-sync` op (`bad-code`) and the `models`
 *  op (`bad-lane`, `bad-action`, `bad-class`, auto-advance W4). It is not
 *  `null`, because the handler answers `null` with `bad-request`, which from
 *  any of these ops must mean exactly one thing: this agent predates it. */
export interface ReqRefusal {
  refuse: Extract<UpdateOpError, 'bad-tag' | 'bad-kind'> | Extract<TokenSyncOpError, 'bad-code'>
    | Extract<ModelsOpError, 'bad-lane' | 'bad-action' | 'bad-class'>;
  id: number;
}
```

In `validateReq`, insert before `    default:` (the line followed by `      return null;` and the function's closing `}`):

```ts
    case 'models': {
      // The ONE lane guard (`isModelsLaneId`), the ONE action guard and the ONE class guard: never a pattern or a word
      // list here. A failed argument is a `ReqRefusal` carrying the op's own word, answered before any spawn;
      // `bad-request` from this op keeps meaning "this agent predates it".
      const { lane, action } = msg;
      if (!isModelsLaneId(lane)) return { refuse: 'bad-lane', id };
      if (!isModelsAction(action)) return { refuse: 'bad-action', id };
      if (action === 'show') {
        if (msg.class !== undefined) return { refuse: 'bad-class', id };
        return { t: 'req', id, op: 'models', lane, action } satisfies ModelsReq;
      }
      const cls = msg.class;
      if (!isModelsClass(cls)) return { refuse: 'bad-class', id };
      return { t: 'req', id, op: 'models', lane, action, class: cls } satisfies ModelsReq;
    }
```

- Modify: `server/src/server.ts` (one import; one key in `GET /api/accounts`' roster map)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Stage 0's `describe(account, registry, catalogue, reading)`/`orphanDescribe(id, registry, catalogue,
  reading)` (W1's call sites pass `win`) and W1's `advance` key on both (`{state: 'absent'} | {state: 'ok', classes}
  | {state: 'unreadable' | 'invalid', detail}`); `parseAdvance`, `AdvanceInvalid`, `ADVANCE_VERSION`, `HOLD_BY`,
  `HOWS`, `familyOf`, `lastMoveOf` and the types `ClassAdvance`, `HistoryEntry`, `Hold`, `Previous`
  (`shared/model-advance.mjs`, W1); `CLASSES`, `ModelClass`; Task 16's `MODELS_OP_ERRORS`.
- Produces:
  - every `describe` and `orphanDescribe` answer (so `show` and every mutation): `labels: Record<ModelClass, {id:
    string, label: string, efforts: string[]} | null>`.
  - `shared/api.ts` (appended): `export const LANE_KINDS = ['anthropic', 'codex', 'other'] as const`, `export type
    WireLaneKind`, and `RosterWire.laneKind?: WireLaneKind` on `GET /api/accounts`. Declared here, beside the wire
    field, because `shared/api.ts` may import nothing new (`peers-claims-l0.test.ts`, D-3021).
  - `shared/models-view.ts`: `LANE_KINDS` and `WireLaneKind` re-exported from `./api.js`; `LaneKind`,
    `laneKindOf(a)`, `readLaneKind(row)`; `ADVANCE_STATES`, `AdvanceState`; `ModelsClassView`, `ModelsLaneView`;
    `readModelsLaneView(lane, answer): ModelsLaneView | null` (the ONE reader of the child's answer);
    `asModelsLaneView(raw): ModelsLaneView | null` (the PWA's guard on the server's wire); `ModelsLaneAnswer`,
    `ModelsActAnswer`, `MODELS_ROUTE_ERRORS` (`MODELS_OP_ERRORS` spread, plus the route's own seven), `ModelsRouteError`,
    `ModelsRouteRefusal`.

The view's fields are the skeleton's §3.12, plus `advanceDetail` and a fifth `advanceState`, `unreported`.
**D-5228 (a departure beyond the skeleton, stated here):** a `show` answer from a
`ccrc` that predates the advance file carries no `advance` key at all, and the view says `unreported` rather than
folding it into `absent` ("no advance recorded yet"), because the remedy differs (update the fleet box, versus
nothing to do); `advanceDetail` carries the reason an `unreadable` or `invalid` file gave, which the panel shows.

Under ruling RC8 the view carries no sessions-behind facts: `show` computes none, and this wave adds no read of
`~/.cc-sessions` on the agent's path.

```ts
// Auto-advance plan W4 Task 18 (spec 2026-10-13 §2.6 and §2.7, D14, D17): the Models panel's view of one lane, read
// from the answer the REAL `deploy/models-op.mjs show` prints over a fixture HOME, and the roster's lane kind. Neutral
// lane and model ids only: this repository is public.
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { serializeAdvance } from '../../shared/model-advance.mjs';
import type { Registry } from '../../shared/models.js';
import {
  LANE_KINDS, asModelsLaneView, laneKindOf, readLaneKind, readModelsLaneView, type ModelsLaneView,
} from '../../shared/models-view.js';
import { ADVANCE_EXAMPLE, ADV_CATALOGUE, ADV_REGISTRY, cat } from './fixtures/advanceCases.js';
import { codexAuthDir } from './codexLaneFixture.js';
import { mkTmp } from './tmpHelpers.js';

const here = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const REPO = path.resolve(here, '..', '..');
const OP = path.join(REPO, 'deploy', 'models-op.mjs');

const ROSTER = {
  version: 1,
  accounts: [
    { id: 'lane-u', label: 'lane-u', configDirSuffix: '.claude', exec: { kind: 'upstream' }, homeAble: true,
      hue: 'cyan', telemetry: 'anthropic' },
    // Pure-parse ports: nothing in this file connects to either.
    { id: 'lane-b', label: 'lane-b', configDirSuffix: '.claude-lane-b',
      exec: { kind: 'codex', provider: 'openai', proxyPort: 45040, litellmPort: 45041, authDir: codexAuthDir('lane-b') },
      homeAble: false, hue: 'magenta', telemetry: 'codex' },
  ],
};
/** The lane as the advance example leaves it: opus advanced from model-5.6-gamma to model-6.1-gamma (its effort
 *  resolved down to xhigh, the newer row's highest), the other pins as ADV_REGISTRY has them. */
const REG: Registry = {
  ...ADV_REGISTRY, classes: { ...ADV_REGISTRY.classes, opus: 'model-6.1-gamma' },
  effort: { ...ADV_REGISTRY.effort, opus: 'xhigh' },
};
/** ADV_CATALOGUE with labels that are not the ids, so a label read off the id is caught. */
const LABELLED = cat(ADV_CATALOGUE.models.map((m) => ({ ...m, label: `${m.id} label` })));

/** Plant lane-b (registry, labelled catalogue, the advance example) and answer what `show <id>` prints. */
function show(id = 'lane-b'): Record<string, unknown> {
  const home = mkTmp('ccrc-models-view-');
  const dir = path.join(home, '.ccrc', 'models');
  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
  const roster = path.join(home, '.ccrc', 'accounts.json');
  fs.writeFileSync(roster, `${JSON.stringify(ROSTER, null, 2)}\n`);
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'lane-b.json'), JSON.stringify(LABELLED));
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'lane-b.classes.json'), `${JSON.stringify(REG, null, 2)}\n`, { mode: 0o600 });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'lane-b.advance.json'), serializeAdvance(ADVANCE_EXAMPLE));
  const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, [OP, 'show', '--file', roster, '--id', id],
    { env: { ...process.env, HOME: home }, encoding: 'utf8' });
  expect(r.status, `${r.stdout}${r.stderr}`).toBe(0);
  return JSON.parse(r.stdout) as Record<string, unknown>;
}
const byCls = (v: ModelsLaneView, cls: string) => v.classes.find((c) => c.cls === cls)!;
/** A copy of `answer` with `f` applied, read. */
const mutated = (answer: Record<string, unknown>, f: (a: any) => void): ModelsLaneView | null => { // eslint-disable-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
  const a = structuredClone(answer);
  f(a);
  return readModelsLaneView('lane-b', a);
};

describe('readModelsLaneView — the ONE reader of what `ccrc models <lane> show` prints', () => {
  it('reads the answer show really prints: pins, labels, families, holds, previous and history, all four classes', () => {
    const view = readModelsLaneView('lane-b', show());
    expect(view).not.toBeNull();
    expect(view!).toMatchObject({ lane: 'lane-b', anthropic: false, advanceState: 'ok', advanceDetail: null,
      catalogue: { fetchedAt: LABELLED.fetchedAt, stale: false } });
    expect(view!.classes.map((c) => c.cls)).toEqual(['haiku', 'sonnet', 'opus', 'fable']);
    const opus = byCls(view!, 'opus');
    expect(opus).toMatchObject({ model: 'model-6.1-gamma', label: 'model-6.1-gamma label', family: 'gamma', hold: null,
      previous: { model: 'model-5.6-gamma', effort: 'max' }, revertable: true, heldBack: null });
    expect(opus.lastMove).toMatchObject({ how: 'advance', from: 'model-5.6-gamma', to: 'model-6.1-gamma', ok: true });
    const sonnet = byCls(view!, 'sonnet');
    expect(sonnet).toMatchObject({ model: 'model-6-beta', label: 'model-6-beta label', family: 'beta', revertable: false,
      lastMove: null });
    expect(sonnet.heldBack).toMatchObject({ how: 'advance', to: 'model-6.1-beta', ok: false, canary: 'failed' });
    const fable = byCls(view!, 'fable');
    expect(fable).toMatchObject({ model: null, label: null, family: 'delta', hold: { by: 'revert' }, previous: null,
      revertable: false, heldBack: null });
    expect(fable.lastMove).toMatchObject({ how: 'revert', to: null, ok: true });
    expect(byCls(view!, 'haiku')).toMatchObject({ model: 'model-5.6-alpha', label: 'model-5.6-alpha label',
      family: 'alpha', lastMove: null, heldBack: null });
  });

  it('reads an Anthropic lane: no registry, so every class is empty, unlabelled and not revertable', () => {
    const view = readModelsLaneView('lane-u', show('lane-u'));
    expect(view).not.toBeNull();
    expect(view!.anthropic).toBe(true);
    expect(view!.classes.every((c) => c.model === null && c.label === null && !c.revertable)).toBe(true);
  });

  it.each([
    ['absent', (a: any) => { a.advance = { state: 'absent' }; }, 'absent', null],
    ['unreadable', (a: any) => { a.advance = { state: 'unreadable', detail: 'not a regular file' }; }, 'unreadable', 'not a regular file'],
    ['invalid', (a: any) => { a.advance = { state: 'invalid', detail: 'classes.opus.hold.by: …' }; }, 'invalid', 'classes.opus.hold.by: …'],
    ['unreported: an older ccrc sent no advance at all', (a: any) => { delete a.advance; }, 'unreported', null],
  ] as [string, (a: unknown) => void, string, string | null][])(
    'keeps %s apart: no hold, no previous, and each family derived from its pin (D-5228)',
    (_why, f, state, detail) => {
      const view = mutated(show(), f);
      expect(view).not.toBeNull();
      expect([view!.advanceState, view!.advanceDetail]).toEqual([state, detail]);
      expect(view!.classes.every((c) => c.hold === null && c.previous === null && !c.revertable && c.lastMove === null)).toBe(true);
      expect(view!.classes.map((c) => c.family)).toEqual(['alpha', 'beta', 'gamma', null]);
    });

  it.each([
    ['an id that is not the lane', (a: any) => { a.id = 'lane-a'; }],
    ['no anthropic flag', (a: any) => { delete a.anthropic; }],
    ['a registry missing a class', (a: any) => { delete a.registry.classes.opus; }],
    ['a pin that is not a string', (a: any) => { a.registry.classes.opus = 6; }],
    ['a catalogue whose time is a string', (a: any) => { a.catalogue.fetchedAt = 'today'; }],
    ['an advance state off the list', (a: any) => { a.advance = { state: 'maybe' }; }],
    ['an advance file the advance grammar refuses', (a: any) => { a.advance.classes.opus.hold = { at: '2026-10-22T08:00:00Z', by: 'pwa' }; }],
    ['an unreadable advance file with no detail', (a: any) => { a.advance = { state: 'unreadable' }; }],
    ['labels that are not an object', (a: any) => { a.labels = 'gamma'; }],
    ['a label for a model the class does not pin', (a: any) => { a.labels.opus.id = 'model-5.6-gamma'; }],
    ['labels missing a class', (a: any) => { delete a.labels.opus; }],
  ] as [string, (a: unknown) => void][])('refuses %s, whole: null, never a partial view', (_why, f) => {
    expect(mutated(show(), f)).toBeNull();
  });

  it('labels are null, never guessed, when the answer carries none (a ccrc from before them)', () => {
    const view = mutated(show(), (a) => { delete a.labels; });
    expect(view!.classes.map((c) => c.label)).toEqual([null, null, null, null]);
    expect(byCls(view!, 'opus').model).toBe('model-6.1-gamma');
  });

  it('revertable is true only with a previous, read from the advance file', () => {
    const view = mutated(show(), (a) => { a.advance.classes.haiku.previous = { model: 'model-5-alpha', effort: null }; });
    expect(view!.classes.map((c) => c.revertable)).toEqual([true, false, true, false]);
  });

  it('lastMove is the newest SUCCESSFUL entry, and heldBack the newest entry only when it is a failed advance', () => {
    const ok = { at: '2026-10-20T10:00:00Z', how: 'advance', from: 'model-6-beta', to: 'model-6.1-beta', ok: true, canary: 'passed' };
    const failed = { at: '2026-10-21T10:00:00Z', how: 'advance', from: 'model-6.1-beta', to: 'model-7-beta', ok: false, canary: 'failed', reason: 'http 500' };
    const hand = { at: '2026-10-22T10:00:00Z', how: 'hand', from: 'model-6.1-beta', to: 'model-6-beta', ok: true, canary: 'not-run' };
    const a = mutated(show(), (x) => { x.advance.classes.sonnet.history = [ok, failed]; });
    expect([byCls(a!, 'sonnet').lastMove, byCls(a!, 'sonnet').heldBack]).toEqual([ok, failed]);
    const b = mutated(show(), (x) => { x.advance.classes.sonnet.history = [failed, hand]; });
    expect([byCls(b!, 'sonnet').lastMove, byCls(b!, 'sonnet').heldBack]).toEqual([hand, null]);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 4: `shared/models-view.ts`**

```ts
// The Models panel's view of one lane, and the roster's lane kind (auto-advance spec 2026-10-13 §2.6 and §2.7, D14 and
// D17's Codex half; plan W4 Task 18). L0: it imports only its `shared/` siblings (`agent-protocol.ts`, `api.ts`,
// `models.ts`, `model-advance.mjs`, none of which imports this file back), and the PWA bundles it.
//
// TWO READERS, TWO INPUTS, each the only one of its kind:
//  - `readModelsLaneView(lane, answer)` reads the one JSON object `ccrc models <lane> show` prints — or a hold, release
//    or revert, which answer the same `describe` — as the server's route receives it through the agent's `models` op.
//    It is the only reader of that answer in TypeScript, and it re-uses the advance file's own validator
//    (`parseAdvance`) rather than restating its grammar.
//  - `asModelsLaneView(raw)` is the PWA's guard on the server's wire (`view` on `GET`/`POST /api/models/:lane`), the
//    `asStallWatchView` idiom: what arrived is checked, not cast.
// A view carries no sessions-behind facts (ruling RC8): `show` computes none, and doctor's `model-sessions-behind` is
// where they are named.
import { MODELS_OP_ERRORS } from './agent-protocol.js';
import { LANE_KINDS, type WireLaneKind } from './api.js';
import { CLASSES, type ModelClass } from './models.js';
import {
  ADVANCE_VERSION, AdvanceInvalid, HOLD_BY, HOWS, familyOf, lastMoveOf, parseAdvance,
  type ClassAdvance, type HistoryEntry, type Hold, type Previous,
} from './model-advance.mjs';

/** The kinds the server sends (`laneKindOf`), declared beside the wire field they type, at the end of
 *  `shared/api.ts` (which may import nothing new), and re-exported here beside their one reader. `unknown` is only
 *  ever a reader's answer. */
export { LANE_KINDS, type WireLaneKind };
export type LaneKind = WireLaneKind | 'unknown';

/** THE rule, stated once (D17: which label source applies is decided by the roster's lane kind, never by a wrapper
 *  name): an Anthropic-telemetry account is `anthropic`; an `exec.kind: 'codex'` account is `codex`, the one kind the
 *  automatic advance runs on (D-5198); every other account is `other`. */
export function laneKindOf(a: { readonly telemetry: string; readonly exec: { readonly kind: string } }): WireLaneKind {
  if (a.telemetry === 'anthropic') return 'anthropic';
  return a.exec.kind === 'codex' ? 'codex' : 'other';
}

/** THE ONE READER of a roster row's `laneKind` (additive on `RosterWire`): an absent field (an older server, an
 *  offline snapshot from before it), a non-string and a word off `LANE_KINDS` all read `unknown`, never a guessed
 *  kind. */
export function readLaneKind(row: unknown): LaneKind {
  if (typeof row !== 'object' || row === null) return 'unknown';
  const k = (row as { laneKind?: unknown }).laneKind;
  return typeof k === 'string' && (LANE_KINDS as readonly string[]).includes(k) ? (k as WireLaneKind) : 'unknown';
}

/** How the lane's advance file read, as `show` reported it — five values, never folded: `ok`; `absent` (none yet: a
 *  lane not backfilled, or set up by an older build); `unreadable` and `invalid` (present and not usable, each with
 *  `advanceDetail`); and `unreported`, a `show` answer that carried no `advance` key at all, which only a `ccrc` from
 *  before the advance file sends (D-5228). */
export const ADVANCE_STATES = ['ok', 'absent', 'unreadable', 'invalid', 'unreported'] as const;
export type AdvanceState = (typeof ADVANCE_STATES)[number];

/** One class, as the panel and the pickers read it. */
export interface ModelsClassView {
  readonly cls: ModelClass;
  /** The class's pin, or null for an empty class (or a lane with no registry). */
  readonly model: string | null;
  /** The catalogue's own label for `model`, or null: an empty class, a pin no catalogue row lists, or an answer from a
   *  `ccrc` that sends no `labels`. Never invented: a reader with none shows the id. */
  readonly label: string | null;
  /** The family the class follows: the advance file's when it was read, else derived from the pin (`familyOf`). The
   *  pickers read a class write back by it. */
  readonly family: string | null;
  readonly hold: Hold | null;
  readonly previous: Previous | null;
  /** True only when the advance file was read and holds a `previous`: a Revert has somewhere to go. */
  readonly revertable: boolean;
  /** The newest SUCCESSFUL move (`lastMoveOf`), or null. */
  readonly lastMove: HistoryEntry | null;
  /** The newest history entry when it is a failed advance, or null: the last attempt, which the panel names. Doctor's
   *  `model-advance-held-back` decides whether it still holds the class back (D-5191). */
  readonly heldBack: HistoryEntry | null;
}

/** One lane: all four classes, in `CLASSES` order, empty ones included. */
export interface ModelsLaneView {
  readonly lane: string;
  readonly anthropic: boolean;
  readonly advanceState: AdvanceState;
  readonly advanceDetail: string | null;
  readonly catalogue: { readonly fetchedAt: number; readonly stale: boolean } | null;
  readonly classes: readonly ModelsClassView[];
}

/** `GET /api/models/:lane`'s 200: the view and when it was measured (the server caches one per lane for 60 s). */
export interface ModelsLaneAnswer { readonly ok: true; readonly lane: string; readonly view: ModelsLaneView; readonly cachedAt: number }
/** `POST /api/models/:lane`'s 200: the view the action itself answered. */
export interface ModelsActAnswer { readonly ok: true; readonly lane: string; readonly view: ModelsLaneView }
/** The route's own refusal words. A 409 carries the child's own word instead (`lock-busy`, `no-previous`, …), so a
 *  refusal's `error` is a string, and these are the ones the route itself chooses: every word of the agent op's
 *  vocabulary, SPREAD from `MODELS_OP_ERRORS` and never typed again (a second list of those words is a second
 *  vocabulary, which `single-definition.test.ts` refuses), and the seven words only the route says. */
export const MODELS_ROUTE_ERRORS = [
  ...MODELS_OP_ERRORS,
  'bad-request', 'no-such-lane', 'not-configured', 'agent-predates-op', 'verb-missing', 'unreadable', 'link-down',
] as const;
export type ModelsRouteError = (typeof MODELS_ROUTE_ERRORS)[number];
export interface ModelsRouteRefusal { readonly ok: false; readonly error: string; readonly detail?: string }

const isObj = (v: unknown): v is Record<string, unknown> => typeof v === 'object' && v !== null && !Array.isArray(v);
const isStrOrNull = (v: unknown): v is string | null => v === null || typeof v === 'string';

/** The one reader of the child's answer: the view, or null for an answer it refuses WHOLE — never a partial view,
 *  because a panel that shows half a lane invites a tap on the half it got wrong. */
export function readModelsLaneView(lane: string, answer: unknown): ModelsLaneView | null {
  if (!isObj(answer) || answer['id'] !== lane) return null;
  const anthropic = answer['anthropic'];
  if (typeof anthropic !== 'boolean') return null;
  const pins = pinsOf(answer['registry']);
  if (pins === undefined) return null;
  const catalogue = catalogueOf(answer['catalogue']);
  if (catalogue === undefined) return null;
  const adv = advanceOf(answer['advance']);
  if (adv === null) return null;
  // `labels` is absent from a ccrc that predates it (every label then reads null), and refused when present and not
  // an object.
  const rawLabels = answer['labels'];
  let labels: Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
  if (rawLabels === undefined) labels = undefined;
  else if (isObj(rawLabels)) labels = rawLabels;
  else return null;
  const classes: ModelsClassView[] = [];
  for (const cls of CLASSES) {
    const model = pins === null ? null : pins[cls];
    const label = labelOf(labels, cls, model);
    if (label === undefined) return null;
    const a = adv.classes === null ? null : adv.classes[cls];
    const newest = a === null || a.history.length === 0 ? null : a.history[a.history.length - 1]!;
    classes.push({
      cls, model, label,
      family: a === null ? familyOf(model) : a.family,
      hold: a === null ? null : a.hold,
      previous: a === null ? null : a.previous,
      revertable: a !== null && a.previous !== null,
      lastMove: a === null ? null : lastMoveOf(a),
      heldBack: newest !== null && newest.how === 'advance' && newest.ok === false ? newest : null,
    });
  }
  return { lane, anthropic, advanceState: adv.state, advanceDetail: adv.detail, catalogue, classes };
}

/** The registry's four pins; `null` for no registry (an Anthropic lane, a lane nobody seeded); `undefined` for a
 *  shape this reader refuses. */
function pinsOf(registry: unknown): Record<ModelClass, string | null> | null | undefined {
  if (registry === null) return null;
  if (!isObj(registry)) return undefined;
  const classes = registry['classes'];
  if (!isObj(classes)) return undefined;
  const out = {} as Record<ModelClass, string | null>;
  for (const cls of CLASSES) {
    const v = classes[cls];
    if (!isStrOrNull(v)) return undefined;
    out[cls] = v;
  }
  return out;
}

/** `show`'s `{fetchedAt, stale, count}`, or null for a lane never probed; `undefined` for a shape refused. */
function catalogueOf(c: unknown): { fetchedAt: number; stale: boolean } | null | undefined {
  if (c === null) return null;
  if (!isObj(c)) return undefined;
  const fetchedAt = c['fetchedAt'];
  const stale = c['stale'];
  if (typeof fetchedAt !== 'number' || typeof stale !== 'boolean') return undefined;
  return { fetchedAt, stale };
}

/** `show`'s `advance`, kept in its five states; null for a shape refused. An `ok` file's classes go back through
 *  `parseAdvance`, the advance file's one grammar, so nothing here restates it. */
function advanceOf(adv: unknown): { state: AdvanceState; detail: string | null; classes: Record<ModelClass, ClassAdvance> | null } | null {
  if (adv === undefined) return { state: 'unreported', detail: null, classes: null };
  if (!isObj(adv)) return null;
  const state = adv['state'];
  if (state === 'absent') return { state, detail: null, classes: null };
  if (state === 'unreadable' || state === 'invalid') {
    const detail = adv['detail'];
    return typeof detail === 'string' ? { state, detail, classes: null } : null;
  }
  if (state !== 'ok') return null;
  try {
    return { state, detail: null, classes: parseAdvance({ v: ADVANCE_VERSION, classes: adv['classes'], pending: null }).classes };
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof AdvanceInvalid) return null;
    throw e;
  }
}

/** A class's label: its catalogue row's, null for none or for an answer with no `labels`, `undefined` for a row this
 *  reader refuses (a missing class key, or a row whose `id` is not the pin it labels). */
function labelOf(labels: Record<string, unknown> | undefined, cls: ModelClass, model: string | null): string | null | undefined {
  if (labels === undefined) return null;
  if (!(cls in labels)) return undefined;
  const row = labels[cls];
  if (row === null) return null;
  if (!isObj(row)) return undefined;
  const label = row['label'];
  if (typeof label !== 'string' || row['id'] !== model) return undefined;
  return label;
}

const isHoldOrNull = (h: unknown): h is Hold | null =>
  h === null || (isObj(h) && typeof h['at'] === 'string' && typeof h['by'] === 'string'
    && (HOLD_BY as readonly string[]).includes(h['by']));
const isPreviousOrNull = (p: unknown): p is Previous | null =>
  p === null || (isObj(p) && isStrOrNull(p['model']) && isStrOrNull(p['effort']));
const isEntryOrNull = (e: unknown): e is HistoryEntry | null =>
  e === null || (isObj(e) && typeof e['at'] === 'string' && typeof e['how'] === 'string'
    && (HOWS as readonly string[]).includes(e['how']) && isStrOrNull(e['from']) && isStrOrNull(e['to'])
    && typeof e['ok'] === 'boolean');

/** The PWA's guard on the server's wire: the view as the route sent it, or null. Checks every field the panel and the
 *  pickers read, and the four classes in `CLASSES` order. */
export function asModelsLaneView(raw: unknown): ModelsLaneView | null {
  if (!isObj(raw)) return null;
  const lane = raw['lane'];
  const anthropic = raw['anthropic'];
  const advanceState = raw['advanceState'];
  const advanceDetail = raw['advanceDetail'];
  if (typeof lane !== 'string' || typeof anthropic !== 'boolean' || !isStrOrNull(advanceDetail)) return null;
  if (typeof advanceState !== 'string' || !(ADVANCE_STATES as readonly string[]).includes(advanceState)) return null;
  const catalogue = catalogueOf(raw['catalogue']);
  if (catalogue === undefined) return null;
  const list = raw['classes'];
  if (!Array.isArray(list) || list.length !== CLASSES.length) return null;
  const classes: ModelsClassView[] = [];
  for (const [i, cls] of CLASSES.entries()) {
    const c: unknown = list[i];
    if (!isObj(c) || c['cls'] !== cls) return null;
    const { model, label, family, hold, previous, revertable, lastMove, heldBack } = c;
    if (!isStrOrNull(model) || !isStrOrNull(label) || !isStrOrNull(family) || typeof revertable !== 'boolean') return null;
    if (!isHoldOrNull(hold) || !isPreviousOrNull(previous) || !isEntryOrNull(lastMove) || !isEntryOrNull(heldBack)) return null;
    classes.push({ cls, model, label, family, hold, previous, revertable, lastMove, heldBack });
  }
  return { lane, anthropic, advanceState: advanceState as AdvanceState, advanceDetail, catalogue, classes };
}
```

The file names no class word but through `CLASSES` (the class-name enumeration scan reads comments too).

    (eight arms: `answer`, `refused`, `predates-op`, `foreign`, `malformed`, `unsent`, `lost`, `failed`); `export type
    Refused`, `export type Outcome`; `export function refused(status, error, detail): Refused`; `export function
    outcomeOf(lane: string, r: ModelsLinkResult): Outcome`; `export function parseActBody(body: unknown)`; `export
    const NOT_CONFIGURED: Refused`; `export function badLane(lane: string): Refused`.
  - `server/src/models/link.ts` (L3): `export interface ModelsLink { run(lane: string, call: ModelsCall):
    Promise<ModelsLinkResult> }` (never rejects); `export function modelsLinkOver(client: Pick<FleetClient,
    'request'>): ModelsLink`.
  - `server/src/models/routes.ts` (L4, decides nothing): `export const MODELS_CACHE_MS = 60_000`; `export function
    registerModelsRoutes(app, deps: Pick<Deps, 'modelsOp'>, sessionAuth: (req) => GateDecision, clock = Date.now):
    void`.
  - `GET /api/models/:lane` → `200 ModelsLaneAnswer`; `POST /api/models/:lane` with `{action, class}` → `200
    ModelsActAnswer`; refusals `{ok: false, error, detail?}` per the skeleton's §3.11 table.
  - `Deps.modelsOp?: ModelsLink`, set in remote mode only (`modelsLinkOver(fleet.client)`).

**D-5230 (a departure beyond the skeleton, stated here).** The skeleton's file map has two
server files for this surface, `link.ts` (L3) and `routes.ts` (L4). Which way the op ended and which status each way
earns is a DECISION, and CLAUDE.md's rings forbid L4 one ("L4 delivery owns fastify/sockets/timers but is NOT allowed
to DECIDE"); the token and docs surfaces each keep theirs in a `policy.ts` that imports `shared/` alone. So a third
file, `server/src/models/policy.ts` (L1), declares the link's result vocabulary (`ModelsCall`, `ModelsLinkResult`) and
every verdict (`outcomeOf`, `parseActBody`, `NOT_CONFIGURED`, `badLane`); `routes.ts` applies them and keeps only the
cache, its coalescing and the audit line; `link.ts` classifies. Step 1's ring case holds the import rule.

**D-5229 (a departure beyond the skeleton, stated here).** The skeleton's audit line ends
`by session <sid>`. A session's id is its cookie, a credential, and a log line is no place for one. The line names the
session by the device label the gate MEASURED with a live credential (`deviceActor(sessionAuth(req).device)`, the
form `pwaDec` already records): `device:<label>`, or `unmeasured` on a dark box. The handler hands that label to
`deviceActor` once and never branches on it (Step 1's audit describe, `auth-gate.test.ts`'s `pwaDec` rule).

**D-5226** (declared in Task 16) is applied here: an agent `no-answer` whose
detail is exactly `MODELS_VERB_MISSING_LINE` is `501 verb-missing`, beside the skeleton's `unknown-subcommand` arm.

```ts
/** What `ccrc models <lane> show` prints, cut to what the view reads: one class pinned, nothing else recorded. */
const SHOW = (pin = 'model-6.1-gamma', lane = 'lane-b') => ({
  ok: true, op: 'show', id: lane, anthropic: false,
  registry: { probe: 'codex', classes: { haiku: null, sonnet: null, opus: pin, fable: null }, subagent: 'sonnet',

});
const opusOf = (body: { view: { classes: { cls: string; model: string | null }[] } }) =>
  body.view.classes.find((c) => c.cls === 'opus')!.model;
/** Each lane's own pin, for the per-lane cases: lane-a's opus is model-6-gamma, every other lane's model-6.1-gamma. */
const pinOf = (lane: string): string => (lane === 'lane-a' ? 'model-6-gamma' : 'model-6.1-gamma');

const DEVICE: GateDecision = { allow: true, verdict: 'ok', reason: 'session', device: 'phone of lane-a' };

/** A link whose every call waits for the test to answer it. */
function scripted() {
  const calls: { lane: string; call: ModelsCall; answer: (r: ModelsLinkResult) => void }[] = [];
  const link: ModelsLink = { run: (lane, call) => new Promise((answer) => { calls.push({ lane, call, answer }); }) };
  return { link, calls };
}
/** A link that answers every call with `r`. */
function fixed(r: ModelsLinkResult) {
  const calls: { lane: string; call: ModelsCall }[] = [];
  const link: ModelsLink = { run: async (lane, call) => { calls.push({ lane, call }); return r; } };
  return { link, calls };
}
/** A link that answers each lane with that lane's own view (`pinOf`). */
function perLane() {
  const calls: { lane: string; call: ModelsCall }[] = [];
  const link: ModelsLink = {

  };

    ['the launcher could not start', { kind: 'refused', word: 'spawn-failed', detail: 'could not start the launcher (ENOENT)' }, 502, 'spawn-failed', 'could not start the launcher (ENOENT)'],
    ['the agent refused the lane', { kind: 'refused', word: 'bad-lane', detail: null }, 400, 'bad-lane', undefined],

describe('the cache: one view per lane for 60 s (plan §3.11)', () => {
  it('a GET inside 60 s sends no second op; one at 60 s does', async () => {
    const f = fixed(VIEW_OF());
    const app = await appWith(f.link);
    now = 2_000_000;
    expect((await get(app)).json().cachedAt).toBe(2_000_000);
    now += MODELS_CACHE_MS - 1;
    expect((await get(app)).json().cachedAt).toBe(2_000_000);
    expect(f.calls).toHaveLength(1);
    now += 1;
    expect((await get(app)).json().cachedAt).toBe(now);
    expect(f.calls).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(f.calls.every((c) => c.call.action === 'show')).toBe(true);
  });

  it('concurrent misses on one lane send one op, and both answer it', async () => {
    const s = scripted();
    const app = await appWith(s.link);
    const a = get(app);
    const b = get(app);
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(1));
    s.calls[0]!.answer(VIEW_OF());
    for (const res of [await a, await b]) expect(res.statusCode, res.body).toBe(200);
    expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("a POST replaces the lane's view with its own answer: the next GET answers it with no op", async () => {
    const s = scripted();
    const app = await appWith(s.link);
    const g = get(app);
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(1));
    s.calls[0]!.answer(VIEW_OF('model-6-gamma'));
    expect(opusOf((await g).json())).toBe('model-6-gamma');
    const p = post(app, { action: 'revert', class: 'opus' });
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(2));
    expect(s.calls[1]!.call).toEqual({ action: 'revert', cls: 'opus' });
    s.calls[1]!.answer(VIEW_OF('model-5.6-gamma'));
    expect((await p).statusCode).toBe(200);
    expect(opusOf((await get(app)).json())).toBe('model-5.6-gamma');
    expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it("a POST that answered no view drops the lane's view, because its effect on the box is unknown", async () => {
    const s = scripted();
    const app = await appWith(s.link);
    const g = get(app);
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(1));
    s.calls[0]!.answer(VIEW_OF());
    await g;
    const p = post(app, HOLD);
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(2));
    s.calls[1]!.answer({ kind: 'lost', why: 'timeout' });
    expect((await p).statusCode).toBe(504);
    const g2 = get(app);
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(3));
    s.calls[2]!.answer(VIEW_OF());
    expect((await g2).statusCode).toBe(200);
  });

  it("a read that began before a POST never lands over that POST's view", async () => {
    const s = scripted();
    const app = await appWith(s.link);
    const g = get(app);
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(1));
    const p = post(app, { action: 'revert', class: 'opus' });
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(2));
    s.calls[1]!.answer(VIEW_OF('model-5.6-gamma'));
    expect((await p).statusCode).toBe(200);
    s.calls[0]!.answer(VIEW_OF('model-6.1-gamma'));   // the stale read lands last
    expect(opusOf((await g).json())).toBe('model-6.1-gamma');   // it answers its own caller
    expect(opusOf((await get(app)).json())).toBe('model-5.6-gamma');   // and the cache keeps the POST's view
    expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it('the cache is per lane: a fresh view of one lane never answers a GET of another', async () => {
    const f = perLane();
    const app = await appWith(f.link);
    now = 2_500_000;
    expect(opusOf((await get(app, 'lane-b')).json())).toBe('model-6.1-gamma');
    const a = await get(app, 'lane-a');
    expect(a.statusCode, a.body).toBe(200);
    expect(a.json().lane).toBe('lane-a');
    expect(a.json().view.lane).toBe('lane-a');
    expect(opusOf(a.json())).toBe('model-6-gamma');
    expect(f.calls.map((c) => c.lane)).toEqual(['lane-b', 'lane-a']);
  });

  it('concurrent misses on two lanes send two ops, each answered with its own lane', async () => {
    const s = scripted();
    const app = await appWith(s.link);
    const b = get(app, 'lane-b');
    const a = get(app, 'lane-a');
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(2));
    expect(s.calls.map((c) => c.lane).sort()).toEqual(['lane-a', 'lane-b']);
    for (const c of s.calls) c.answer(VIEW_OF(pinOf(c.lane), c.lane));
    expect(opusOf((await a).json())).toBe('model-6-gamma');
    expect(opusOf((await b).json())).toBe('model-6.1-gamma');
  });

  it("a POST on one lane leaves another lane's cached view and its cachedAt alone, even when it fails", async () => {
    const s = scripted();
    const app = await appWith(s.link);
    now = 3_000_000;
    const g = get(app, 'lane-b');
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(1));
    s.calls[0]!.answer(VIEW_OF());
    expect((await g).json().cachedAt).toBe(3_000_000);
    now += 1_000;
    const p = post(app, HOLD, 'lane-a');
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(2));
    s.calls[1]!.answer({ kind: 'lost', why: 'timeout' });
    expect((await p).statusCode).toBe(504);
    expect((await get(app, 'lane-b')).json().cachedAt).toBe(3_000_000);
    expect(s.calls).toHaveLength(2);
  });
});

  });

  it("the POST hands the gate's device label to deviceActor once and never branches on it (auth-gate's pwaDec rule)", () => {
    const src = fs.readFileSync(join(REPO, 'server', 'src', 'models', 'routes.ts'), 'utf8');
    const at = src.indexOf("app.post('/api/models/:lane', async (req, reply) => {");

describe('modelsLinkOver — every way the request can end is its own arm, and nothing rejects', () => {
  /** A `request` that answers `outcome`, recording each call's arguments. */
  const clientOf = (outcome: () => Promise<unknown>) => {
    const seen: unknown[][] = [];
    const client = { request: (...args: unknown[]) => { seen.push(args); return outcome(); } };
    return { link: modelsLinkOver(client as unknown as Pick<FleetClient, 'request'>), seen };
  };
  const res = (extra: Record<string, unknown>) => async () => ({ t: 'res', id: 1, ok: true, ...extra });
  const rej = (e: unknown) => async () => { throw e; };

  it("sends the two frame shapes, each with the op's own 50 s deadline", async () => {
    const { link, seen } = clientOf(res({ exit: 0, answer: SHOW() }));
    await link.run('lane-b', { action: 'show' });
    await link.run('lane-b', { action: 'hold', cls: 'opus' });
    expect(seen).toEqual([
      [{ t: 'req', op: 'models', lane: 'lane-b', action: 'show' }, MODELS_OP_TIMEOUT_MS],
      [{ t: 'req', op: 'models', lane: 'lane-b', action: 'hold', class: 'opus' }, MODELS_OP_TIMEOUT_MS],
    ]);
  });

  it.each([
    ['an ok frame with exit and answer', res({ exit: 1, answer: { ok: false, error: 'lock-busy' } }),
      { kind: 'answer', exit: 1, answer: { ok: false, error: 'lock-busy' } }],
    ['an ok frame without them', res({}), { kind: 'malformed', detail: 'the agent answered ok without {exit, answer}' }],
    ['an exit outside 0/1/2', res({ exit: 3, answer: {} }), { kind: 'malformed', detail: 'the agent answered ok without {exit, answer}' }],
    ['an array as the answer', res({ exit: 0, answer: [] }), { kind: 'malformed', detail: 'the agent answered ok without {exit, answer}' }],
    ["the envelope's bad-request", rej(new AgentOpError('bad-request', null)), { kind: 'predates-op' }],
    ['one of the op words', rej(new AgentOpError('busy', 'x')), { kind: 'refused', word: 'busy', detail: 'x' }],
    ['a word off the op vocabulary', rej(new AgentOpError('not-implemented', null)), { kind: 'foreign', code: 'not-implemented', detail: null }],
    ['a frame that never left', rej(new LinkNotSentError('disconnected')), { kind: 'unsent', why: 'disconnected' }],
    ['the deadline', rej(new Error('timeout')), { kind: 'lost', why: 'timeout' }],
    ['a drop after the send', rej(new Error('disconnected')), { kind: 'lost', why: 'disconnected' }],
    ['an abort after the send', rej(new Error('aborted')), { kind: 'lost', why: 'aborted' }],
    ['an Error of no known kind', rej(new Error('boom')), { kind: 'failed', detail: 'boom' }],
    ['a thrown value that is not an Error', rej('boom'), { kind: 'failed', detail: 'boom' }],
  ] as [string, () => Promise<unknown>, ModelsLinkResult][])('%s is its own arm', async (_why, outcome, want) => {
    await expect(clientOf(outcome).link.run('lane-b', { action: 'show' })).resolves.toEqual(want);
  });
});

// ── the real thing: a POST hold racing the hourly commit (plan W4 Review Focus line 1) ──────────────────────────────
// A REAL agent (Task 17's port, under a fixture HOME), the REAL `ccd/ccrc` behind `_inst_shim`'s own launcher bytes,
// the real lane-files lock (W1), and a real `flock` holder standing in for the hourly refresh's commit. The agent's
// child sees exactly {HOME, PATH, LANG}, so `CCRC_MODELS_LOCK_S` cannot reach it: the wait is the default 20 s, which is
// why the bound order Task 16 pins matters, and why the second case takes about 20 s. That case is kept on purpose:
// Task 16's pin compares two numbers, and only this case measures that the real verb, behind the real launcher, under
// the agent's real environment, gives up on its own before the agent's bound.
const HAVE_FLOCK = spawnSync('bash', ['-c', 'command -v flock'], { encoding: 'utf8' }).status === 0;
const E2E_ROSTER = {
  version: 1,
  accounts: [
    { id: 'lane-u', label: 'lane-u', configDirSuffix: '.claude', exec: { kind: 'upstream' }, homeAble: true,
      hue: 'cyan', telemetry: 'anthropic' },
    // Pure-parse ports: nothing in this file connects to either.
    { id: 'lane-b', label: 'lane-b', configDirSuffix: '.claude-lane-b',
      exec: { kind: 'codex', provider: 'openai', proxyPort: 45060, litellmPort: 45061, authDir: codexAuthDir('lane-b') },
      homeAble: false, hue: 'magenta', telemetry: 'codex' },
  ],
};

describe('a POST hold racing the hourly commit — the real agent, the real ccrc, a real flock holder (Review Focus line 1)', () => {
  const holders: ChildProcess[] = [];
  const homes: string[] = [];
  let agent: RunningAgent | undefined;
  let fleet: ConnectedFleet | undefined;

  const release = (child: ChildProcess): Promise<void> => new Promise((resolve) => {
    if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) { resolve(); return; }
    child.once('exit', () => resolve());
    child.stdin!.end();
  });
  afterEach(async () => {
    for (const c of holders.splice(0)) await release(c);
    await fleet?.close();
    fleet = undefined;
    if (agent) await agent.close();
    agent = undefined;
    for (const h of homes.splice(0)) fs.rmSync(h, { recursive: true, force: true });
  });

  /** A fixture box: `ccrc` runs from `<home>/ccrc/ccd/ccrc` as on a deployed box, behind the real launcher. */
  function box(): { home: string; env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv } {
    const home = mkTmp('ccrc-models-route-');
    homes.push(home);
    const ccd = join(home, 'ccrc', 'ccd');
    fs.mkdirSync(ccd, { recursive: true });
    for (const f of ['ccrc', 'ccrc-wrapper-shape']) fs.symlinkSync(join(REPO, 'ccd', f), join(ccd, f));
    fs.symlinkSync(join(REPO, 'deploy'), join(home, 'ccrc', 'deploy'));
    fs.symlinkSync(join(REPO, 'shared'), join(home, 'ccrc', 'shared'));
    fs.mkdirSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'models'), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'accounts.json'), `${JSON.stringify(E2E_ROSTER, null, 2)}\n`);
    fs.writeFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'models', 'lane-b.classes.json'), ADV_REGISTRY_BYTES, { mode: 0o600 });
    fs.writeFileSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'models', 'lane-b.json'), JSON.stringify(ADV_CATALOGUE));
    const env = ghContainedEnv(home, { PATH: process.env.PATH ?? '', HOME: home, LANG: 'C' }, { systemd: true });
    const shim = join(home, '.local', 'bin', 'ccrc');
    const r = spawnSync('bash', ['-c', 'f=$1; out=$2; set --; . "$f"; _inst_shim > "$out"', 'shim',
      join(REPO, 'ccd', 'ccrc'), shim], { env, encoding: 'utf8' });
    expect(r.status, r.stderr).toBe(0);
    fs.chmodSync(shim, 0o755);
    return { home, env };
  }

  /** Another writer, outside the agent: a real `flock` on lane-b's lock, held until `release`. */
  async function holdLock(home: string): Promise<ChildProcess> {
    fs.mkdirSync(join(home, '.ccrc', 'locks'), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
    const child = spawn('flock', [join(home, '.ccrc', 'locks', 'models-lane-b.lock'), 'sh', '-c', 'echo held; read _'],
      { stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'ignore'] });
    holders.push(child);
    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      child.stdout!.once('data', () => resolve());
      child.once('error', reject);
      child.once('exit', (code) => reject(new Error(`the lock holder exited (${code}) before it held the lock`)));
    });
    return child;
  }

  async function serverOver(b: { home: string; env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv }): Promise<FastifyInstance> {
    const projects = mkTmp('ccrc-models-route-projects-');
    homes.push(projects);
    agent = await startAgent({ host: '127.0.0.1', port: 0, token: TOKEN, home: b.home, projectsRoot: projects,
      helloTimeoutMs: 300, spawnModels: makeModelsSpawn(modelsEnv(b.home, b.env)) });
    fleet = connectToAgent(agent.port);
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(fleet!.state.connected).toBe(true), { timeout: 3000 });
    const app = await buildServer({ ...testDeps(mkTmp('ccrc-models-route-server-')), modelsOp: modelsLinkOver(fleet.client) });
    apps.push(app);
    return app;
  }

  it.skipIf(!HAVE_FLOCK)('the hold waits out the commit and lands: 200, the class held by hand, never a timeout', async () => {
    const b = box();
    const app = await serverOver(b);
    const holder = await holdLock(b.home);
    let settled = false;
    const pending = post(app, HOLD).then((r) => { settled = true; return r; });
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1_500));
    expect(settled, 'the hold answered while the commit held the lane').toBe(false);
    expect(fs.existsSync(join(b.home, '.ccrc', 'models', 'lane-b.advance.json')), 'the hold wrote under a held lock').toBe(false);
    await release(holder);
    const res = await pending;
    expect(res.statusCode, res.body).toBe(200);
    const opus = res.json().view.classes.find((c: { cls: string }) => c.cls === 'opus');
    expect(opus.hold).toMatchObject({ by: 'hand' });
    expect(opus.hold.at).toMatch(/^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\dZ$/);
  }, 60_000);

  it.skipIf(!HAVE_FLOCK)('a commit that outlasts the lock wait is 409 lock-busy inside the spawn bound: the child is never killed holding the lock', async () => {
    const b = box();
    const app = await serverOver(b);
    await holdLock(b.home);
    const t0 = Date.now();
    const res = await post(app, HOLD);
    const took = Date.now() - t0;
    expect(res.statusCode, res.body).toBe(409);
    expect(res.json().error).toBe('lock-busy');
    expect(took, 'the verb gave up before its own lock wait').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(19_000);
    expect(took, 'the agent had to stop the child').toBeLessThan(MODELS_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS);
    expect(fs.existsSync(join(b.home, '.ccrc', 'models', 'lane-b.advance.json'))).toBe(false);
  }, 60_000);

  it('the word the verb-missing arm keys on is the word the real ccrc prints for a subcommand it lacks', () => {
    const b = box();
    const r = spawnSync('bash', [join(b.home, 'ccrc', 'ccd', 'ccrc'), 'models', 'lane-b', 'nosuch'],
      { env: b.env, encoding: 'utf8', input: '' });
    expect(r.status).toBe(2);
    const lines = (r.stdout ?? '').split('\n');
    expect(lines.length, r.stdout).toBe(2);
    expect(JSON.parse(lines[0]!)).toMatchObject({ ok: false, error: 'unknown-subcommand' });
  });
});
```
