- [ ] **Step 3: The verdicts, `server/src/models/policy.ts` (L1)**

```ts
// The Models panel's route verdicts, ring L1 (auto-advance spec 2026-10-13 §2.7, D14; plan W4 Task 19,
// D-5230): pure decisions over plain data, a typed answer out. It imports nothing but
// `shared/` (CLAUDE.md "Rings", the rule `token/policy.ts` and `docs/policy.ts` keep): no fastify, no reply, no clock,
// no timer, no console. The link (`link.ts`, L3) classifies how one op ended into a `ModelsLinkResult`, declared here
// because this file owns each arm's status; the routes (`routes.ts`, L4) APPLY these verdicts and own only the cache,
// its coalescing and the audit line. `models-routes.test.ts` holds the import rule and every status.
import {
  MODELS_OP_TIMEOUT_MS, MODELS_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS, isModelsAction, isModelsClass, isModelsVerbMissing,
  type ModelsAction, type ModelsOpError,
} from '../../../shared/agent-protocol.js';
import { CLASSES, type ModelClass } from '../../../shared/models.js';
import { readModelsLaneView, type ModelsLaneView, type ModelsRouteError } from '../../../shared/models-view.js';

/** One call: `show`, or a writing action with its class. */
export type ModelsCall =
  | { readonly action: 'show' }
  | { readonly action: Exclude<ModelsAction, 'show'>; readonly cls: ModelClass };

/** Every way one op can end, kept apart:
 *  - `answer`: the child printed one object, at exit 0, 1 or 2 — a view, or a refusal of the verb.
 *  - `refused`: the agent refused the op with one of its own words (`MODELS_OP_ERRORS`).
 *  - `predates-op`: the agent answered `bad-request`, its envelope's word for an op it does not know.
 *  - `foreign`: the agent refused with a word off the op's vocabulary (a thrown message from its envelope).
 *  - `malformed`: the agent said ok without `{exit, answer}`.
 *  - `unsent`: the frame never left (`LinkNotSentError`): nothing ran.
 *  - `lost`: the link failed after the send with one of its three known words (`timeout`, `disconnected`,
 *    `aborted`): the action may have run.
 *  - `failed`: the link failed after the send in a way none of those words names, its message kept: the action may
 *    have run. Never folded into `lost`, which would say "the link went down" about a failure nobody measured. */
export type ModelsLinkResult =
  | { readonly kind: 'answer'; readonly exit: 0 | 1 | 2; readonly answer: Record<string, unknown> }
  | { readonly kind: 'refused'; readonly word: ModelsOpError; readonly detail: string | null }
  | { readonly kind: 'predates-op' }
  | { readonly kind: 'foreign'; readonly code: string; readonly detail: string | null }
  | { readonly kind: 'malformed'; readonly detail: string }
  | { readonly kind: 'unsent'; readonly why: string }
  | { readonly kind: 'lost'; readonly why: 'timeout' | 'disconnected' | 'aborted' }
  | { readonly kind: 'failed'; readonly detail: string };

/** A refusal, as the route sends it: its status, its word, and its detail when it has one. */
export type Refused = { readonly ok: false; readonly status: number; readonly error: ModelsRouteError | string; readonly detail: string | null };
/** One op's verdict: the view, or a refusal. */
export type Outcome = { readonly ok: true; readonly view: ModelsLaneView } | Refused;

export const refused = (status: number, error: ModelsRouteError | string, detail: string | null): Refused =>
  ({ ok: false, status, error, detail });

/** Every way the op can end, one status each (plan §3.11). */
export function outcomeOf(lane: string, r: ModelsLinkResult): Outcome {
  switch (r.kind) {
    case 'answer': {
      const a = r.answer;
      if (a['ok'] === true) {
        if (r.exit !== 0) return refused(502, 'unreadable', `ccrc exited ${r.exit} with an answer that says ok`);
        const view = readModelsLaneView(lane, a);
        return view === null
          ? refused(502, 'unreadable', `the fleet box answered a view of ${lane} this server cannot read`)
          : { ok: true, view };
      }
      const error = a['error'];
      const detail = typeof a['detail'] === 'string' ? a['detail'] : null;
      if (a['ok'] !== false || typeof error !== 'string' || r.exit === 0) {
        return refused(502, 'unreadable', 'the fleet box answered neither a view nor a refusal');
      }
      // Two child words the route names, the rest passed through as the verb said them.
      if (error === 'no-such-account') return refused(404, 'no-such-lane', detail);
      if (error === 'unknown-subcommand') return refused(501, 'verb-missing', detail);
      return refused(409, error, detail);
    }
    case 'refused':
      switch (r.word) {
        case 'bad-lane': case 'bad-class': case 'bad-action': return refused(400, r.word, r.detail);
        case 'busy': return refused(429, 'busy', r.detail);
        case 'timeout':
          return refused(504, 'timeout', r.detail ?? `the ccrc child was stopped at the ${MODELS_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS} ms bound`);
        case 'spawn-failed': return refused(502, 'spawn-failed', r.detail);
        case 'no-answer':
          // D-5226: a ccrc with no `models` verb at all prints no object, and
          // its usage line is the whole story.
          return isModelsVerbMissing(r.detail) ? refused(501, 'verb-missing', r.detail) : refused(502, 'no-answer', r.detail);
        default: {
          const unhandled: never = r.word;
          return refused(502, 'no-answer', `the agent answered "${String(unhandled)}"`);
        }
      }
    case 'predates-op': return refused(501, 'agent-predates-op', "the fleet box's agent does not answer the models op: update it");
    case 'foreign':
      return refused(502, 'no-answer', `the agent answered "${r.code}"${r.detail === null ? '' : `: ${r.detail}`}`);
    case 'malformed': return refused(502, 'no-answer', r.detail);
    case 'unsent': return refused(503, 'link-down', `the request never reached the fleet agent (${r.why})`);
    case 'lost':
      return r.why === 'timeout'
        ? refused(504, 'timeout', `the fleet agent did not answer within ${MODELS_OP_TIMEOUT_MS} ms; the action may still have run`)
        : refused(503, 'link-down', `the link to the fleet agent went ${r.why === 'aborted' ? 'away' : 'down'} after the request was sent; the action may still have run`);
    case 'failed':
      return refused(502, 'no-answer', `the link to the fleet agent failed after the request was sent (${r.detail}); the action may still have run`);
    default: {
      const unhandled: never = r;
      return refused(502, 'no-answer', `an unknown link result ${JSON.stringify(unhandled)}`);
    }
  }
}

/** The POST body: exactly `{action, class}`, the action one of the three writing actions. Anything that is not an
 *  object — a `text/plain` body, which arrives as a string and is the shape a cross-site form can send — is
 *  `bad-request`, and is never parsed here. */
export function parseActBody(body: unknown):
  { ok: true; call: Exclude<ModelsCall, { action: 'show' }> } | { ok: false; refusal: Refused } {
  if (typeof body !== 'object' || body === null || Array.isArray(body)) {
    return { ok: false, refusal: refused(400, 'bad-request', 'the body must be {"action": "hold"|"release"|"revert", "class": <class>}') };
  }
  const b = body as Record<string, unknown>;
  const extra = Object.keys(b).filter((k) => k !== 'action' && k !== 'class');
  if (extra.length > 0) return { ok: false, refusal: refused(400, 'bad-request', `the body takes no field ${JSON.stringify(extra[0])}`) };
  const action = b['action'];
  if (!isModelsAction(action) || action === 'show') {
    return { ok: false, refusal: refused(400, 'bad-action', 'action must be hold, release or revert; the read is GET') };
  }
  const cls = b['class'];
  if (!isModelsClass(cls)) return { ok: false, refusal: refused(400, 'bad-class', `class must be one of ${CLASSES.join(', ')}`) };
  return { ok: true, call: { action, cls } };
}

/** Local mode, or no fleet client (D-5203). */
export const NOT_CONFIGURED: Refused = refused(501, 'not-configured',
  "this server reaches no fleet agent (it does not run with CCRC_FLEET=remote), so a lane's model classes cannot be read or changed from here");

/** A lane that fails `isModelsLaneId`, refused before any op. */
export function badLane(lane: string): Refused {
  return refused(400, 'bad-lane', `${JSON.stringify(lane)} is not a lane id the models op takes`);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: The link and the routes, `server/src/models/link.ts` (L3) and `server/src/models/routes.ts` (L4)**

`server/src/models/link.ts`:

```ts
// The `models` op over the one agent connection (auto-advance spec 2026-10-13 §2.7, D14; plan W4 Task 19), ring L3.
// It narrows nothing it received: every way the op can end is one `ModelsLinkResult` arm (declared in `policy.ts`,
// L1, which owns each arm's status), and the routes (L4) apply that status. The agent's answer is handed on as it
// came, the child's one object with its exit code, because reading it is `readModelsLaneView`'s job, in L0.
import { AgentOpError, LinkNotSentError, type FleetClient } from '../remote/client.js';
import { MODELS_OP, MODELS_OP_TIMEOUT_MS, isModelsOpError } from '../../../shared/agent-protocol.js';
import type { ModelsCall, ModelsLinkResult } from './policy.js';

/** The routes' port, declared beside its one adapter. `run` never rejects. */
export interface ModelsLink { run(lane: string, call: ModelsCall): Promise<ModelsLinkResult> }

const LOST_WORDS = ['timeout', 'disconnected', 'aborted'] as const;

/** `request` with the op's own 50 s deadline (`FleetClient`'s default is 15 s), so the agent's own answer — even
 *  "the child was stopped at the bound" — always arrives first. */
export function modelsLinkOver(client: Pick<FleetClient, 'request'>): ModelsLink {
  return {
    async run(lane, call) {
      try {
        const res = call.action === 'show'
          ? await client.request({ t: 'req', op: MODELS_OP, lane, action: 'show' }, MODELS_OP_TIMEOUT_MS)
          : await client.request({ t: 'req', op: MODELS_OP, lane, action: call.action, class: call.cls }, MODELS_OP_TIMEOUT_MS);
        const exit = (res as { exit?: unknown }).exit;
        const answer = (res as { answer?: unknown }).answer;
        if ((exit === 0 || exit === 1 || exit === 2) && typeof answer === 'object' && answer !== null && !Array.isArray(answer)) {
          return { kind: 'answer', exit, answer: answer as Record<string, unknown> };
        }
        return { kind: 'malformed', detail: 'the agent answered ok without {exit, answer}' };
      } catch (e) {
        if (e instanceof AgentOpError) {
          if (e.code === 'bad-request') return { kind: 'predates-op' };
          if (isModelsOpError(e.code)) return { kind: 'refused', word: e.code, detail: e.detail };
          return { kind: 'foreign', code: e.code, detail: e.detail };
        }
        if (e instanceof LinkNotSentError) return { kind: 'unsent', why: e.message };
        // After the send every rejection is a plain Error (`FleetClient.request`'s own note). Its three known words
        // are `lost`; any other failure is `failed`, its message kept, never folded into one of the three.
        const m = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
        if ((LOST_WORDS as readonly string[]).includes(m)) return { kind: 'lost', why: m as (typeof LOST_WORDS)[number] };
        return { kind: 'failed', detail: m };
      }
    },
  };
}
```

`server/src/models/routes.ts`:

```ts
import type { FastifyInstance, FastifyReply, FastifyRequest } from 'fastify';
import type { Deps } from '../server.js';
import type { GateDecision } from '../auth/gate.js';
import { deviceActor } from '../ccdargv.js';
import { NOT_CONFIGURED, badLane, outcomeOf, parseActBody, type Outcome, type Refused } from './policy.js';
import { isModelsLaneId } from '../../../shared/agent-protocol.js';
import type { ModelsActAnswer, ModelsLaneAnswer, ModelsLaneView } from '../../../shared/models-view.js';

/**
 * THE MODELS PANEL'S ROUTES (auto-advance spec 2026-10-13 §2.7, D14; plan W4 Task 19). L4: fastify, the clock and the
 * cache live here, and nothing is decided here. What the lane IS is `readModelsLaneView`'s (L0); how the op ended is
 * the link's `ModelsLinkResult` (L3); which status each ending earns, and every refusal of a lane or a body, is
 * `policy.ts`'s (L1, D-5230). These handlers apply those verdicts.
 *
 * THE CREDENTIALS. Both routes are session-gated and consult no fleet credential at all: neither is in
 * `auth/gate.ts`'s EXEMPT table, so armed they sit behind the passkey (and the POST, being non-GET, behind the origin
 * check), and dark they are open, as every route is. `box-token-census.test.ts` reads this file as a lane source of
 * its own (`MODELS_DOORS`) and counts any mention of the shared-secret check functions in a handler's slice, prose
 * included, which is why this file never names them.
 *
 * LOCAL MODE has no agent, so both routes answer `501 not-configured` there (D-5203). A local
 * spawn port is Later.
 *
 * THE CACHE. One view per lane for `MODELS_CACHE_MS`, so a phone that opens the panel twice, or a picker that mounts
 * on every session screen of a Codex lane, spends one spawn on the fleet box. Everything is keyed by the lane:
 * concurrent misses on one lane share ONE op, and two lanes never share one. A POST replaces its lane's view with the
 * view the action itself answered; a POST that answered no view drops that lane's view alone, because its effect on
 * the box is then unknown. A read that began before a POST never lands over that POST's view (`generation`).
 *
 * THE AUDIT. Every POST that reaches the op is logged first, through `console.warn` (the server runs `logger: false`,
 * so `req.log` is a no-op). The child's fixed argv and three-name environment carry no caller
 * (D-5190), so this line is where the act is attributed: to the device the gate MEASURED for the
 * session, handed to `deviceActor` and never branched on, never to the session cookie, which is a credential
 * (D-5229).
 */
export const MODELS_CACHE_MS = 60_000;

export function registerModelsRoutes(
  app: FastifyInstance,
  deps: Pick<Deps, 'modelsOp'>,
  /** `buildServer`'s `sessionAuth`, read by the audit line alone: the gate itself fronts both routes. */
  sessionAuth: (req: FastifyRequest) => GateDecision,
  clock: () => number = Date.now,
): void {
  const cache = new Map<string, { view: ModelsLaneView; cachedAt: number }>();
  const inflight = new Map<string, Promise<Outcome>>();
  const generation = new Map<string, number>();
  const genOf = (lane: string): number => generation.get(lane) ?? 0;

  const refuse = (reply: FastifyReply, o: Refused): FastifyReply =>
    reply.code(o.status).send({ ok: false, error: o.error, ...(o.detail === null ? {} : { detail: o.detail }) });

  /** The lane's view, from the cache while it is younger than `MODELS_CACHE_MS`. */
  app.get('/api/models/:lane', async (req, reply) => {
    const link = deps.modelsOp;
    if (link === undefined) return refuse(reply, NOT_CONFIGURED);
    const { lane } = req.params as { lane: string };
    if (!isModelsLaneId(lane)) return refuse(reply, badLane(lane));
    const hit = cache.get(lane);
    if (hit !== undefined && clock() - hit.cachedAt < MODELS_CACHE_MS) {
      return reply.send({ ok: true, lane, view: hit.view, cachedAt: hit.cachedAt } satisfies ModelsLaneAnswer);
    }
    let pending = inflight.get(lane);
    if (pending === undefined) {
      const gen = genOf(lane);
      pending = link.run(lane, { action: 'show' }).then((r) => {
        const o = outcomeOf(lane, r);
        if (o.ok && genOf(lane) === gen) cache.set(lane, { view: o.view, cachedAt: clock() });
        return o;
      }).finally(() => { inflight.delete(lane); });
      inflight.set(lane, pending);
    }
    const o = await pending;
    if (!o.ok) return refuse(reply, o);
    const c = cache.get(lane);
    const cachedAt = c !== undefined && c.view === o.view ? c.cachedAt : clock();
    return reply.send({ ok: true, lane, view: o.view, cachedAt } satisfies ModelsLaneAnswer);
  });

  /** Hold, release or Revert one class: the verb under the lane-files lock, on the fleet box, through the agent. */
  app.post('/api/models/:lane', async (req, reply) => {
    const link = deps.modelsOp;
    if (link === undefined) return refuse(reply, NOT_CONFIGURED);
    const { lane } = req.params as { lane: string };
    if (!isModelsLaneId(lane)) return refuse(reply, badLane(lane));
    const parsed = parseActBody(req.body);
    if (!parsed.ok) return refuse(reply, parsed.refusal);
    const { action, cls } = parsed.call;
    console.warn(`ccrc-server: models: ${action} ${lane} ${cls} by session ${deviceActor(sessionAuth(req).device)}`);
    generation.set(lane, genOf(lane) + 1);
    const o = outcomeOf(lane, await link.run(lane, parsed.call));
    if (!o.ok) {
      cache.delete(lane);
      return refuse(reply, o);
    }
    cache.set(lane, { view: o.view, cachedAt: clock() });
    return reply.send({ ok: true, lane, view: o.view } satisfies ModelsActAnswer);
  });
}
```

  opus: classView('opus', {
    model: 'model-6.1-gamma', label: 'Gamma 6.1', family: 'gamma',
    previous: { model: 'model-5.6-gamma', effort: 'max' }, revertable: true,
    lastMove: { at: '2026-10-21T14:05:11Z', how: 'advance', from: 'model-5.6-gamma', to: 'model-6.1-gamma', ok: true,
      canary: 'passed', effort: { from: 'max', to: 'xhigh' } },
  }),
  fable: classView('fable', {
    family: 'delta', hold: { at: '2026-10-22T08:00:00Z', by: 'revert' },
    lastMove: { at: '2026-10-22T08:00:00Z', how: 'revert', from: 'model-6-delta', to: null, ok: true, canary: 'not-run' },
  }),
};

/** The view: `ADVANCED`'s four classes with `classes` laid over them, and `over` over the lane's fields. */
export const laneView = (
  over: Partial<Omit<ModelsLaneView, 'classes'>> = {},
  classes: Partial<Record<ModelClass, Partial<ModelsClassView>>> = {},
): ModelsLaneView => ({
  lane: LANE, anthropic: false, advanceState: 'ok', advanceDetail: null,
  catalogue: { fetchedAt: 1789000000, stale: false },
  classes: CLASSES.map((c) => ({ ...ADVANCED[c], ...(classes[c] ?? {}) })),
  ...over,
});

/** `GET /api/models/:lane`'s 200 for `view`. */
export const laneAnswer = (view: ModelsLaneView = laneView()): ModelsLaneAnswer =>
  ({ ok: true, lane: view.lane, view, cachedAt: 1789000000000 });

describe('the models lane routes (auto-advance W4)', () => {
  it('modelsLane GETs /api/models/<lane>, the lane encoded', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn().mockImplementation(async () => jsonResponse(200, { ok: true, lane: 'lane-b', view: {}, cachedAt: 1 }));
    const api = createApi(fetchImpl as unknown as typeof fetch);
    await api.modelsLane('lane-b');

    expect(fetchImpl.mock.calls.map((c) => c[0])).toEqual(['/api/models/lane-b', '/api/models/a%2Fb']);
    expect((fetchImpl.mock.calls[0] as [string, RequestInit | undefined])[1]?.method ?? 'GET').toBe('GET');
  });

  it('modelsAct POSTs {action, class} as JSON and asks for JSON back', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(jsonResponse(200, { ok: true, lane: 'lane-b', view: {} }));
    const api = createApi(fetchImpl as unknown as typeof fetch);
    await api.modelsAct('lane-b', 'revert', 'opus');
    const [url, init] = fetchImpl.mock.calls[0] as [string, RequestInit];
    expect(url).toBe('/api/models/lane-b');
    expect(init.method).toBe('POST');
    expect(new Headers(init.headers).get('content-type')).toBe('application/json');
    expect(new Headers(init.headers).get('accept')).toBe('application/json');
    expect(JSON.parse(init.body as string)).toEqual({ action: 'revert', class: 'opus' });
  });

  it('modelsAct resolves unreadable on a 2xx whose body cannot be read — never a rejection (D-1150)', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(new Response('not json', { status: 200 }));
    const api = createApi(fetchImpl as unknown as typeof fetch);
    await expect(api.modelsAct('lane-b', 'hold', 'opus')).resolves.toBe('unreadable');
  });

  it('modelsAct rejects a refusal as ApiError, carrying its body', async () => {
    const body = { ok: false, error: 'lock-busy', detail: 'held' };
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(jsonResponse(409, body));
    const api = createApi(fetchImpl as unknown as typeof fetch);
    const err = await api.modelsAct('lane-b', 'hold', 'opus').catch((e: unknown) => e);
    expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(ApiError);
    expect([(err as ApiError).status, (err as ApiError).body]).toEqual([409, body]);
  });
});

Create `pwa/src/fleet/modelsWords.ts`:

```ts
// Every sentence the Models sheet says, written once (auto-advance plan W4 Task 20). A class arrives as data and is
// shown through `classTitle`; no class word is spelled here. No sentence claims a running session picks a re-pinned
// model up by itself: under D11's fallback a session may keep the model it has until it is relaunched (spec §2.4,
// ruling RC1).
import type { HistoryEntry, Hold } from '../../../shared/model-advance.mjs';
import type { ModelsClassView, ModelsLaneView, ModelsRouteError } from '../../../shared/models-view';
import { ApiError, apiErrorText } from '../lib/api';
import type { Unavailable } from './useLaneModels';

export const MODELS_BUTTON = 'Models';
export const MODELS_SHEET_TITLE = 'Model classes';
export const REVERT_CONFIRM = 'Revert and hold';

export const holdLabel = (held: boolean): string => (held ? 'release' : 'hold');
/** The Revert button names the model it reverts TO (`previous`), which after a hand `set-class` may not be the model
 *  the class had just before (spec D21: `previous` is the pin before the last ADVANCE). */
export const revertLabel = (to: string | null): string => `revert to ${to ?? 'none'}`;
export const revertTitle = (cls: string): string => `Revert the ${cls} class?`;
/** The revert's consequence. The verb reverts to whatever `previous` the fleet box holds at the tap, and the view this
 *  sheet read may be up to a minute old (the server's cache), so the target is said AS LAST READ, never promised; the
 *  sheet then settles on the box's own answer. */
export const revertConsequence = (lane: string, c: ModelsClassView): string[] => [
  `${lane}'s ${c.cls} class goes back to the model it had before its last automatic advance, and is held there, `
    + 'so no automatic advance moves it until you release it.',
  `As last read, that is ${c.previous?.model ?? 'none'}, replacing ${c.model ?? 'none'}; the sheet shows what the `
    + 'fleet box did once it answers.',
  'Sessions already running may keep their current model until they are relaunched.',
];

/** The pin as a person reads it: the catalogue's label beside the id when it has one, else the id; `empty` for none. */
export const modelLine = (model: string | null, label: string | null): string =>
  model === null ? 'empty' : label !== null && label !== model ? `${label} (${model})` : model;

/** `2026-10-21T14:05:11Z` read to the minute, UTC said. */
const minute = (at: string): string => `${at.slice(0, 10)} ${at.slice(11, 16)}Z`;

export const lastMoveLine = (m: HistoryEntry | null): string | null =>
  m === null ? null
    : `${m.how === 'advance' ? 'advanced' : m.how === 'revert' ? 'reverted' : 'set by hand'} ${minute(m.at)} from ${m.from ?? 'none'}`;
export const replacedLine = (c: ModelsClassView): string | null =>
  c.previous === null ? null : `replaced ${c.previous.model ?? 'none'}`;
export const holdLine = (h: Hold | null): string | null =>
  h === null ? null : `held ${h.by === 'revert' ? 'by a revert' : 'by hand'} since ${minute(h.at)}`;
export const heldBackLine = (e: HistoryEntry | null): string | null =>
  e === null ? null
    : `${e.to ?? 'none'} failed${e.canary === 'failed' ? ' its canary' : ''}`
      + `${typeof e.tries === 'number' && e.tries > 1 ? ` ${e.tries} times` : ''}`
      + `${typeof e.reason === 'string' ? `: ${e.reason}` : ''}`;
/** A class row's notes, in reading order, the empty ones left out. */
export const classNotes = (c: ModelsClassView): string[] =>
  [lastMoveLine(c.lastMove), replacedLine(c), holdLine(c.hold), heldBackLine(c.heldBack)]
    .filter((n): n is string => n !== null);

/** The advance file's state, said once above the rows; nothing when it read. */
export function advanceNote(v: ModelsLaneView): string | null {
  switch (v.advanceState) {
    case 'ok': return null;
    case 'absent': return 'No automatic advance is on record for this lane yet.';
    case 'unreadable': return `The advance file cannot be read: ${v.advanceDetail ?? 'no reason given'}`;
    case 'invalid': return `The advance file is not one this build reads: ${v.advanceDetail ?? 'no reason given'}`;
    case 'unreported': return "This fleet box's ccrc predates the advance record. Update it to hold or revert from here.";
    default: {
      const unhandled: never = v.advanceState;
      return String(unhandled);
    }
  }
}

export const STALE_CATALOGUE_TEXT = "The lane's catalogue is stale: its last probe failed, so no automatic advance runs on it.";
export const ANTHROPIC_LANE_TEXT = "An Anthropic lane: its classes are Claude Code's own, and nothing here moves them.";
export const NO_SUCH_LANE_TEXT = "The fleet box has no lane by this name: its roster and this server's disagree.";
export const UNREADABLE_TEXT = 'The fleet box answered, but not with a lane view this app can read.';
export const BUSY_TEXT = 'The fleet box is answering another models request. Try again in a moment.';
export const ACT_UNCONFIRMED_TEXT = 'The fleet box took the request, but its answer could not be read. Reading the lane again.';

/** Each way the read can be unavailable, with its own remedy. */
export const UNAVAILABLE_TEXT: Readonly<Record<Unavailable, string>> = {
  'not-configured': "This server reaches no fleet agent, so a lane's model classes cannot be read from here.",
  'agent-predates-op': "The fleet box's agent predates the Models panel. Update the fleet box, then open this again.",
  'verb-missing': "The fleet box's ccrc has no hold, release or revert yet. Update the fleet box, then open this again.",
  'server-predates-route': 'This server predates the Models panel. Update it, then open this again.',
};

/** The route's own words (`MODELS_ROUTE_ERRORS`), each said once. */
export const MODELS_ROUTE_TEXT: Readonly<Record<ModelsRouteError, string>> = {
  'bad-lane': 'That is not a lane id the fleet box takes.',
  'bad-class': 'That is not one of the four classes.',
  'bad-action': 'That action is not hold, release or revert.',
  'bad-request': 'The request was malformed.',
  'no-such-lane': NO_SUCH_LANE_TEXT,
  'busy': BUSY_TEXT,
  'not-configured': UNAVAILABLE_TEXT['not-configured'],
  'agent-predates-op': UNAVAILABLE_TEXT['agent-predates-op'],
  'verb-missing': UNAVAILABLE_TEXT['verb-missing'],
  'no-answer': 'The fleet box ran the verb but printed no answer.',
  'spawn-failed': "The fleet box's ccrc launcher could not start.",
  'unreadable': UNREADABLE_TEXT,
  'link-down': 'The link to the fleet box is down; the action may or may not have run.',
  'timeout': 'The fleet box did not answer in time; the action may still have run. Open the panel again to see.',
};

/** A refusal as one sentence. A 409 is the verb's own refusal, and its `detail` is the box's sentence; a route word is
 *  said in this file's words, with the box's detail beside the two that are the box's fault; anything else is
 *  `apiErrorText`'s. */
export function modelsRefusalText(err: unknown): string {
  if (err instanceof ApiError && typeof err.body === 'object' && err.body !== null) {
    const { error, detail } = err.body as { error?: unknown; detail?: unknown };
    if (err.status === 409 && typeof detail === 'string') return detail;
    if (typeof error === 'string' && Object.hasOwn(MODELS_ROUTE_TEXT, error)) {
      const text = MODELS_ROUTE_TEXT[error as ModelsRouteError];
      return typeof detail === 'string' && (error === 'no-answer' || error === 'spawn-failed') ? `${text} (${detail})` : text;
    }
  }
  return apiErrorText(err);
}
```

Create `pwa/src/fleet/useLaneModels.ts`:

```ts
// The Models sheet's read of one lane (auto-advance plan W4 Task 20): `GET /api/models/:lane`, read once per lane and
// on `reload`, never on a timer. Every way the read can end is its own state, so the sheet never says "loading" for an
// answer it got, or "no such lane" for a server that has no such route.
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { asModelsLaneView, type ModelsLaneAnswer, type ModelsLaneView } from '../../../shared/models-view';
import { ApiError, api } from '../lib/api';
import { modelsRefusalText } from './modelsWords';

/** The four ways the read is unavailable from here, each with its own remedy: no fleet agent, an agent from before
 *  the op, a fleet box `ccrc` from before the verbs, and a server from before the route (an older server's 404, which
 *  must never read as "no such lane"). */
export type Unavailable = 'not-configured' | 'agent-predates-op' | 'verb-missing' | 'server-predates-route';

export type LaneModels =
  | { readonly state: 'idle' }
  | { readonly state: 'loading' }
  | { readonly state: 'ready'; readonly view: ModelsLaneView }
  | { readonly state: 'unavailable'; readonly why: Unavailable }
  | { readonly state: 'no-such-lane' }
  | { readonly state: 'unreadable' }
  | { readonly state: 'failed'; readonly text: string };

export type GetLane = (lane: string) => Promise<ModelsLaneAnswer>;
/** Module scope, so its identity is stable; it reads `api.modelsLane` at call time, so a test's spy is the one used. */
const defaultGetLane: GetLane = (lane) => api.modelsLane(lane);

/** A 200's state: the view the guard accepts, or `unreadable` — never a partial view. */
export function laneModelsOf(answer: unknown): LaneModels {
  const raw = typeof answer === 'object' && answer !== null ? (answer as { view?: unknown }).view : undefined;
  const view = asModelsLaneView(raw);
  return view === null ? { state: 'unreadable' } : { state: 'ready', view };
}

const UNAVAILABLE_501: readonly Unavailable[] = ['not-configured', 'agent-predates-op', 'verb-missing'];

/** A refusal's state. A 404 is `no-such-lane` only when the route said so; any other 404 is a server without the route. */
export function laneModelsFailure(err: unknown): LaneModels {
  if (err instanceof ApiError) {
    const error = typeof err.body === 'object' && err.body !== null ? (err.body as { error?: unknown }).error : undefined;
    if (err.status === 501 && typeof error === 'string' && (UNAVAILABLE_501 as readonly string[]).includes(error)) {
      return { state: 'unavailable', why: error as Unavailable };
    }
    if (err.status === 404) return error === 'no-such-lane' ? { state: 'no-such-lane' } : { state: 'unavailable', why: 'server-predates-route' };
    if (err.status === 502 && error === 'unreadable') return { state: 'unreadable' };
  }
  return { state: 'failed', text: modelsRefusalText(err) };
}

/** One lane's models, read when `lane` is set (and again on `reload`); `idle` while it is null. `settle` puts a view
 *  the box answered a write with in place, with no second read. */
export function useLaneModels(lane: string | null, getLane: GetLane = defaultGetLane): {
  readonly models: LaneModels;
  readonly settle: (view: ModelsLaneView) => void;
  readonly reload: () => void;
} {
  const [models, setModels] = useState<LaneModels>(lane === null ? { state: 'idle' } : { state: 'loading' });
  const [nonce, setNonce] = useState(0);
  // The getter rides a ref, so a caller that passes a fresh function each render does not re-read the lane each render.
  const getter = useRef(getLane);
  useEffect(() => { getter.current = getLane; });
  useEffect(() => {
    if (lane === null) {
      setModels({ state: 'idle' });
      return undefined;
    }
    let live = true;
    setModels({ state: 'loading' });
    getter.current(lane).then(
      (answer) => { if (live) setModels(laneModelsOf(answer)); },
      (err: unknown) => { if (live) setModels(laneModelsFailure(err)); },
    );
    return () => { live = false; };
  }, [lane, nonce]);
  return {
    models,
    settle: (view) => setModels({ state: 'ready', view }),
    reload: () => setNonce((n) => n + 1),
  };
}
```

Create `pwa/src/fleet/LaneModelsSheet.tsx`:

```tsx
// The Models sheet (auto-advance spec 2026-10-13 §2.7; plan W4 Task 20). No per-lane page exists, so the panel is a
// sheet opened from each Codex lane's row on the Accounts screen (D-5202).
//
// Each class is one `ControlRow`: its model and label, its last move and what that replaced, a Hold that is NOT
// optimistic — its label is the hold the box answered, so it changes only when the box's answer lands — and a Revert
// that appears only when the box says the class can revert, and confirms first. One write at a time: while a tap is
// with the box, every control waits.
import { useState } from 'react';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { Button, ControlRow, QuickConfirm, Sheet, Skeleton, toast } from '@ccrc/ui';
import type { ModelsAction } from '../../../shared/agent-protocol';
import type { ModelClass } from '../../../shared/models';
import { asModelsLaneView, type ModelsActAnswer, type ModelsClassView } from '../../../shared/models-view';
import { api } from '../lib/api';
import { classTitle } from '../lib/models';
import { useLaneModels, type GetLane } from './useLaneModels';
import {
  ACT_UNCONFIRMED_TEXT, ANTHROPIC_LANE_TEXT, MODELS_SHEET_TITLE, NO_SUCH_LANE_TEXT, REVERT_CONFIRM, STALE_CATALOGUE_TEXT,
  UNAVAILABLE_TEXT, UNREADABLE_TEXT, advanceNote, classNotes, holdLabel, modelLine, modelsRefusalText, revertConsequence,
  revertLabel, revertTitle,
} from './modelsWords';
import './fleet.css';

export type ActLane = (lane: string, action: Exclude<ModelsAction, 'show'>, cls: ModelClass) => Promise<ModelsActAnswer | 'unreadable'>;
const defaultAct: ActLane = (lane, action, cls) => api.modelsAct(lane, action, cls);

export interface LaneModelsSheetProps {
  /** `null` while no lane's Models button has been tapped. */
  lane: string | null;
  open: boolean;
  onClose: () => void;
  /** Injectable for tests; default `api.modelsLane`. */
  getLane?: GetLane;
  /** Injectable for tests; default `api.modelsAct`. */
  act?: ActLane;
}

export function LaneModelsSheet({ lane, open, onClose, getLane, act = defaultAct }: LaneModelsSheetProps): ReactNode {
  const { models, settle, reload } = useLaneModels(open ? lane : null, getLane);
  const [pending, setPending] = useState<ModelClass | null>(null);
  const [confirm, setConfirm] = useState<ModelsClassView | null>(null);
  if (lane === null) return null;

  /** One write, settled on the box's own answer. An answer the app cannot read may still have changed the lane, so it
   *  is said, and the lane is read again rather than guessed. */
  const run = (action: Exclude<ModelsAction, 'show'>, cls: ModelClass): void => {
    if (pending !== null) return;
    setPending(cls);
    act(lane, action, cls).then(
      (answer) => {
        setPending(null);
        const view = answer === 'unreadable' ? null : asModelsLaneView(answer.view);
        if (view === null) {
          toast(ACT_UNCONFIRMED_TEXT, 'error');
          reload();
          return;
        }
        settle(view);
      },
      (err: unknown) => {
        setPending(null);
        toast(modelsRefusalText(err), 'error');
      },
    );
  };

  const body = (): ReactNode => {
    switch (models.state) {
      case 'idle': return null;
      case 'loading': return <Skeleton lines={4} />;
      case 'unavailable': return <p className="sheet-copy">{UNAVAILABLE_TEXT[models.why]}</p>;
      case 'no-such-lane': return <p className="sheet-copy">{NO_SUCH_LANE_TEXT}</p>;
      case 'unreadable': return <p className="sheet-copy">{UNREADABLE_TEXT}</p>;
      case 'failed': return <p className="sheet-copy">{models.text}</p>;
      case 'ready': {
        const v = models.view;
        if (v.anthropic) return <p className="sheet-copy">{ANTHROPIC_LANE_TEXT}</p>;
        // A hold is offered where the box can record one: a read advance file, or none yet (the hold creates it).
        const canHold = v.advanceState === 'ok' || v.advanceState === 'absent';
        const note = advanceNote(v);
        return (
          <>
            {note !== null && <p className="sheet-copy">{note}</p>}
            {v.catalogue?.stale === true && <p className="sheet-copy">{STALE_CATALOGUE_TEXT}</p>}
            {v.classes.map((c) => (
              <ControlRow key={c.cls} className="models-class-row" role="group" aria-label={classTitle(c.cls)}>
                <span className="models-class-name">{classTitle(c.cls)}</span>
                <span>{modelLine(c.model, c.label)}</span>
                {classNotes(c).map((n) => <span key={n}>{n}</span>)}
                {canHold && (
                  <Button
                    variant="quiet" size="fit" className="models-hold flex-none"
                    disabled={pending !== null} aria-busy={pending === c.cls}
                    onClick={() => run(c.hold === null ? 'hold' : 'release', c.cls)}
                  >
                    {holdLabel(c.hold !== null)}
                  </Button>
                )}
                {c.revertable && (
                  <Button
                    variant="quiet" size="fit" className="models-revert flex-none"
                    disabled={pending !== null} onClick={() => setConfirm(c)}
                  >
                    {revertLabel(c.previous?.model ?? null)}
                  </Button>
                )}
              </ControlRow>
            ))}
          </>
        );
      }
      default: {
        const unhandled: never = models;
        return String(unhandled);
      }
    }
  };

  return (
    <>
      <Sheet open={open} onClose={onClose} eyebrow={lane} title={MODELS_SHEET_TITLE}>
        {body()}
      </Sheet>
      {confirm !== null && (
        <QuickConfirm
          open
          onClose={() => setConfirm(null)}
          title={revertTitle(confirm.cls)}
          consequence={revertConsequence(lane, confirm)}
          confirmLabel={REVERT_CONFIRM}
          onConfirm={() => run('revert', confirm.cls)}
        />
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

// Auto-advance spec 2026-10-13 §2.6 (D17's Codex half; plan W4 Task 21): the pickers' labels come from DATA, chosen by

// and model ids only: this repository is public, and the roster ids this file checks for are read off the PWA's own

import path from 'node:path';

const ROUTE_OPUS = { fields: { class: 'opus' }, degraded: null, inert: [], unreadable: [] };

    expect(routeView(fleetSession({ model: 'model-6.1-gamma', route: ROUTE_OPUS }), codex()).wireQueuedField).toBeNull();

    const none = labelSourceFor('codex', null);
    const opts = modelOptions(none, 'model-6.1-gamma');
    expect(opts.map((o) => o.label)).toEqual([...CLASSES].reverse().map((c) => `${classTitle(c)} class`));
    expect(opts.every((o) => !o.active && o.readback === '' && o.sublabel === undefined)).toBe(true);
    expect(modelReadbackFor(none, 'opus')).toBeNull();
    expect(routeView(fleetSession({ model: 'model-6-beta', route: ROUTE_OPUS }), none).wireQueuedField).toBeNull();
  });

  it('an empty class has no row, and Ultracode is a Codex lane\'s unknown word only', () => {
    expect(modelOptions(codex(), null).map((o) => o.route.value)).not.toContain('fable');
    expect(effortIsKnown(codex(), 'ultracode')).toBe(false);
    expect(effortIsKnown(labelSourceFor('anthropic', null), 'ultracode')).toBe(true);
    expect(effortIsKnown(labelSourceFor('other', null), 'ultracode')).toBe(true);

// The session pickers' one pin (routing spec 2026-09-14 §5.3; auto-advance spec 2026-10-13 §2.6, D17). `modelOptions`
// takes a LABEL SOURCE chosen by the lane's kind: a Codex lane's rows come from its Models view, every other lane's
// are the alias rows. A row carries the routing record write a tap performs (`route: {field, value}`), which
// `SessionScreen`'s `pick` sends through `POST /api/sessions/:id/route`, never a slash command. Neutral lane and model
// ids only: this repository is public.
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { ROUTE_WRITABLE_FIELDS } from '../../shared/api';
import { EFFORT_LADDER } from '../../shared/routing-ladder';
import { effortOptions, modelOptions, type LabelSource, type PickOption } from '../src/lib/models';
import { laneView } from './modelsViewFixture';

const ANTHROPIC: LabelSource = { kind: 'anthropic' };
const OTHER: LabelSource = { kind: 'other' };
const CODEX: LabelSource = { kind: 'codex', view: laneView() };
const NO_VIEW: LabelSource = { kind: 'codex', view: null };
const routes = (s: LabelSource, cur: string | null = null): string[] =>
  modelOptions(s, cur).map((o: PickOption) => `${o.route.field}=${o.route.value}`);
const labelOf = (s: LabelSource, alias: string): string => modelOptions(s, null).find((o) => o.route.value === alias)!.label;

describe('modelOptions', () => {
  it("a Codex lane offers its pinned classes in capability order, each labelled by its catalogue row", () => {
    // The fixture's fourth class is empty, so it has no row.
    expect(routes(CODEX)).toEqual(['class=opus', 'class=sonnet', 'class=haiku']);
    expect(modelOptions(CODEX, null).map((o) => [o.label, o.sublabel]))
      .toEqual([['Gamma 6.1', 'Opus class'], ['Beta 6', 'Sonnet class'], ['Alpha 6.1', 'Haiku class']]);
  });

  it('never offers a bare "Default" on a Codex lane, with a view or without', () => {
    // Routing to `class=default` resolves through what the lane's launcher sets, which this console cannot state.
    expect(routes(CODEX)).not.toContain('class=default');
    expect(routes(NO_VIEW)).not.toContain('class=default');
  });

  it('an Anthropic lane keeps its alias rows, ending in class=default, and an other lane gets the same rows', () => {
    expect(routes(ANTHROPIC)).toEqual(['class=opus', 'class=sonnet', 'class=fable', 'class=haiku', 'class=default']);
    expect(modelOptions(OTHER, null)).toEqual(modelOptions(ANTHROPIC, null));
    expect(modelOptions(ANTHROPIC, null).map((o) => o.label)).not.toContain('Gamma 6.1');
  });

  it('carries the readback key the read-back effect matches the live model string against', () => {
    // A Codex row's readback is its class's FAMILY; an alias row's is the family word. The Default row's is the empty
    // string, which `pick` never consults: `class=default` clears `queued` on the 2xx (absence is not readable).
    expect(modelOptions(CODEX, null).map((o) => o.readback)).toEqual(['gamma', 'beta', 'alpha']);
    expect(modelOptions(ANTHROPIC, null).map((o) => o.readback)).toEqual(['opus', 'sonnet', 'fable', 'haiku', '']);
  });

  it('every row writes a field ROUTE_WRITABLE_FIELDS knows, and never carries a command key', () => {
    for (const s of [CODEX, NO_VIEW, ANTHROPIC, OTHER]) {
      for (const o of modelOptions(s, null)) {
        expect(ROUTE_WRITABLE_FIELDS as readonly string[], o.label).toContain(o.route.field);
        expect('command' in o, o.label).toBe(false);
      }
    }
  });

  it('highlights the live row from the statusline display name, case-insensitively, and only that one', () => {
    const active = (s: LabelSource, cur: string): string[] => modelOptions(s, cur).filter((o) => o.active).map((o) => o.route.value);
    expect(active(CODEX, 'model-6.1-gamma')).toEqual(['opus']);
    expect(active(CODEX, 'MODEL-6-BETA')).toEqual(['sonnet']);
    // A context-size suffix must not defeat the match.
    expect(active(ANTHROPIC, 'Opus x (1M context)')).toEqual(['opus']);
  });

  // Whole-branch review M1: `route.degraded` — the class ccd IS serving when no lane could serve the intended one
  // (spec §5.4). `degradedTo` carries a LABEL off THIS lane's own list, never the bare alias.
  describe('the degraded-class note (whole-branch review M1)', () => {
    const noted = (s: LabelSource, intended: string, degraded: string | null): (string | undefined)[] =>
      modelOptions(s, null, { intended, inert: false, degraded }).filter((o) => o.active).map((o) => o.degradedTo);

    it('names the served class by its label on this lane, on the intended row alone', () => {
      expect(noted(CODEX, 'opus', 'haiku')).toEqual(['Alpha 6.1']);
      expect(noted(ANTHROPIC, 'opus', 'haiku')).toEqual([labelOf(ANTHROPIC, 'haiku')]);
    });

    it('sets nothing when the stamp names the intended class itself, or is absent', () => {
      expect(noted(ANTHROPIC, 'opus', 'opus')).toEqual([undefined]);
      expect(noted(CODEX, 'opus', null)).toEqual([undefined]);
      expect(modelOptions(ANTHROPIC, null, { intended: 'opus', inert: false }).filter((o) => o.active).map((o) => o.degradedTo))
        .toEqual([undefined]);
    });

    it('falls back to the raw stamped word for a class no row here carries — a degradation it cannot name is still one', () => {
      expect(noted(ANTHROPIC, 'opus', 'ludicrous')).toEqual(['ludicrous']);
      expect(noted(CODEX, 'opus', 'fable')).toEqual(['fable']);   // the fixture's empty class has no row to name it
    });

    it('attaches to no row at all when the class read was unreadable — no active row to sit beside', () => {
      expect(modelOptions(ANTHROPIC, 'haiku x', { intended: null, inert: false, unreadable: true, degraded: 'haiku' })
        .filter((o) => o.degradedTo !== undefined)).toEqual([]);
    });
  });
});

describe('effortOptions', () => {
  it('withholds Ultracode from a Codex lane, with a view or without, and offers it on every other kind', () => {
    for (const s of [CODEX, NO_VIEW]) expect(effortOptions(s, 'high', false).map((o) => o.label)).not.toContain('Ultracode');
    for (const s of [ANTHROPIC, OTHER]) expect(effortOptions(s, 'high', false).map((o) => o.label)).toContain('Ultracode');
  });

  it('every row writes the effort field, ultracode included, and Auto writes effort=auto', () => {
    for (const s of [CODEX, ANTHROPIC]) {
      for (const o of effortOptions(s, null, false)) {
        expect(o.route.field, o.label).toBe('effort');
        expect('command' in o, o.label).toBe(false);
      }
    }
    expect(effortOptions(ANTHROPIC, null, false).find((o) => o.label === 'Auto')?.route).toEqual({ field: 'effort', value: 'auto' });
    expect(effortOptions(ANTHROPIC, null, false).find((o) => o.label === 'Ultracode')?.route).toEqual({ field: 'effort', value: 'ultracode' });
  });

  // The five slider stops come from EFFORT_LADDER rather than five hand-built rows — Auto and Ultracode are the
  // picker's own labelled superset on top of the ladder, never part of it.
  const levelRows = (opts: PickOption[]): PickOption[] => opts.filter((o) => o.label !== 'Auto' && o.label !== 'Ultracode');

  it('the five level rows equal EFFORT_LADDER in order, capitalised', () => {
    const rows = levelRows(effortOptions(ANTHROPIC, null, false));
    expect(rows.map((o) => o.route.value)).toEqual([...EFFORT_LADDER]);
    expect(rows.map((o) => o.label)).toEqual(EFFORT_LADDER.map((v) => v[0]!.toUpperCase() + v.slice(1)));
  });

  it("control: the five stops match the spec's own hand-written list, so a reordered or shortened ladder reds this", () => {
    expect(levelRows(effortOptions(CODEX, null, false)).map((o) => o.route.value)).toEqual(['low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', 'max']);
  });

  it('pins the full row order — Auto last, Ultracode spliced before Max on a non-Codex lane only — against a hand-written literal', () => {
    expect(effortOptions(ANTHROPIC, null, false).map((o) => o.label)).toEqual(['Low', 'Medium', 'High', 'Xhigh', 'Ultracode', 'Max', 'Auto']);
    expect(effortOptions(CODEX, null, false).map((o) => o.label)).toEqual(['Low', 'Medium', 'High', 'Xhigh', 'Max', 'Auto']);
  });
});

import type { RouteField } from '../../../shared/api';
import { CLASSES, type ModelClass } from '../../../shared/models';
import type { LaneKind, ModelsLaneView } from '../../../shared/models-view';
import { EFFORT_LADDER, type EffortRung } from '../../../shared/routing-ladder';

/** Where a lane's labels come from, chosen by its kind (`labelSourceFor`). */
export type LabelSource =
  | { readonly kind: 'anthropic' }
  | { readonly kind: 'codex'; readonly view: ModelsLaneView | null }
  | { readonly kind: 'other' };

/** THE choice (D17): a `codex` lane reads its view; an `anthropic` lane its alias rows; an `other` lane, and one whose
 *  kind is `unknown` (an older server, or a roster not read yet), the same alias rows every non-Codex lane has always
 *  had. Never a wrapper name. */
export function labelSourceFor(kind: LaneKind, view: ModelsLaneView | null): LabelSource {
  if (kind === 'codex') return { kind: 'codex', view };
  return kind === 'anthropic' ? { kind: 'anthropic' } : { kind: 'other' };

/** A Codex lane's rows, in capability order (the reverse of `CLASSES`), from its view (D17's Codex half): the label is
 *  the catalogue's for the pin (the id when the catalogue has none), the sublabel the class, the readback the class's
 *  family. With no view yet every class reads "<Class> class" with an empty readback, which lights no row and which
 *  `modelReadbackFor` reports as unmeasurable. An empty class has no row. No `Default` row: what it routes to is set
 *  by the lane's launcher, and this console cannot state it. */
function codexRows(view: ModelsLaneView | null): { label: string; alias: ModelClass; key: string; sublabel?: string }[] {
  return [...CLASSES].reverse().flatMap((cls) => {
    if (view === null) return [{ label: `${classTitle(cls)} class`, alias: cls, key: '' }];
    const c = view.classes.find((x) => x.cls === cls);
    if (c === undefined || c.model === null) return [];
    return [{ label: c.label ?? c.model, alias: cls, key: c.family ?? '', sublabel: `${classTitle(cls)} class` }];
  });
}

 *  which survives the family's version moving. A Codex row's readback is its class's family from the view — the last
 *  part of a `<vendor>-<version>-<family>` id — so a write still reads back after an advance moved the pin to a newer
 *  version of the same family; its label is the catalogue's own and moves with the pin. */

/** The model row's own `readback` for a routing `class` alias on this lane's option list — `null` for an alias no row
 *  carries (an out-of-vocabulary value ccd wrote from a build ahead of this one), AND for a row whose readback is
 *  empty (a Codex class before its view has landed, or `default`): nothing on the pane can read either back, so
 *  `routeView` treats both as unmeasurable, never as agreeing. */
export function modelReadbackFor(source: LabelSource, alias: string): string | null {

The skeleton's seventeen deviations, and the slugs W1 and W2 added, stand as written (ruling RB1). This wave writes
the skeleton's `D-5203`, `D-5202`, `D-5190`,
`D-5191` and `D-5198` where they apply, and adds five, each by its slug
until the allocator issues a number; each is stated in the task where it first appears.

| Slug | Where | Deviation, and why |
|---|---|---|
| D-5226 | Tasks 16, 19 | A `no-answer` whose detail is exactly `ccrc: unknown argument: models` (`_ccrc_usage_die`'s line from a `ccrc` with no `models` verb at all) is `501 verb-missing`, beside the skeleton's `unknown-subcommand` arm. Without it an older fleet box reads as a `502` fault rather than the named hold Review Focus line 5 asks for. Exact equality, so `models-x` is never read as it |
| D-5227 | Task 17 | The child's environment keeps exactly `{HOME, PATH, LANG}`, with the directory of the `node` running the agent first on `PATH`. `ccrc models` runs `deploy/models-op.mjs` under `node`, and a user unit's `PATH` may name none, which would make every Models tap a `no-answer` on a box whose agent is itself a working `node` |
| D-5228 | Task 18 | The view's `advanceState` has a fifth value, `unreported` (a `show` answer with no `advance` key, which only a `ccrc` from before the advance file sends), and the view carries `advanceDetail`. Folding the first into `absent` would tell the operator "nothing recorded yet" when the remedy is "update the fleet box" |
| D-5229 | Task 19 | The audit line names the session by the device label the gate measured (`deviceActor`, `device:<label>` or `unmeasured`), not by a session id: a session's id is its cookie, a credential, and the skeleton's `by session <sid>` would write one into the server's log |
| D-5230 | Task 19 | A third server file beyond the skeleton's two: `server/src/models/policy.ts` (L1, imports `shared/` only) declares the link's result vocabulary and every route verdict (`outcomeOf`, `parseActBody`, `NOT_CONFIGURED`, `badLane`), so `routes.ts` (L4) applies verdicts and decides nothing, as CLAUDE.md's rings require and as the token and docs surfaces' own `policy.ts` files already do |

How W4 applies two of the skeleton's slugs, recorded here so their text is complete when the allocator issues them:
- **D-5203, its known limit.** `ccrc install` writes `CCRC_FLEET=local` by default, and there both
  routes answer `501 not-configured`. So on such a box the Models sheet says no fleet agent is reachable, and a
  codex-kind lane's pickers read `<Class> class` with no model name, light no row, and never show a class write as
  `queued` (its readback is unmeasurable), where today they show hard-coded names. This holds until a local spawn port
  exists (Later).
- **D-5198, in the PWA.** The pickers and the Models button follow the same rule as the advance:
  a Codex lane still rostered `exec.kind: 'external'` reads `other` and gets the alias rows, Ultracode and no Models
  button. The wave contract makes every Codex lane codex-kind a precondition of the rollout.

## Known limits and Later

**Known limits (accepted for this plan):**
- **Running sessions.** A running session on a class that moved keeps the old model until it picks the new one up by
  itself or is relaunched (D11 did not hold; Task 1). `model-sessions-behind` names one still on it a day after the
  move, and its remedy says how to relaunch it.
- **A slow canary waits silently.** A model that never produces text within the canary's deadline is not-ready every
  hour, and nothing WARNs about it (spec §2.3 step 3 and D22; ruling 6). Its reason in the refresh row tells it apart
  from a silent lane.
- **No feed record, no rate cap.** The models push and the Models sheet's taps get no feed record and no
  per-(lane, class) rate cap (ruling 7). The durable record is the advance file's `hold` and `history`, plus the
  server's audit line.
- **Stale labels.**
  - The PWA's labels can be up to 60 s stale after an advance (the route's cache).
  - If W2 reaches the fleet before W4, a moved Codex class shows its old hard-coded label in the pickers until W4
    lands. `ccrc models <id> show` is authoritative.
- **Local mode.** `CCRC_FLEET=local` has no Models sheet: the route answers 501 there.

**Later:**
- the typed `/model` at an idle tick on a Codex lane, if runbook step 6 shows it works, with the ccd routing-record
  change of spec §2.5 item 5;
- the Anthropic arm (spec §2.5, D18, D19, and the Anthropic halves of §2.6 to §2.8);
- a feed record and a rate cap for models pushes and taps;
- naming a class whose canary has been not-ready for more than a day, which would need a spec change to D22's "waits
  silently";
- the PWA showing sessions behind a move, which needs its own probe of the session registry on the agent's path.

## Operator runbook: rollout and live acceptance (not tasks)

1. **Before W2 merges, the coordinator measures the update control plane.** It reads `GET /api/updates`. If any fleet
   node's desired tag would follow a new prerelease, W2 does not merge until R-O9 has run, or until the operator has
   pinned that node. **No wave reaches the fleet before R-O9.**
2. **Roll W1 out first,** after R-O9, with `ccrc rollout --to <tag>`. Then, for any Codex-lane class meant to stay
   empty, run `ccrc models <id> hold <class>`: W2's backfill seeds every empty class's family, and the next hour would
   fill it. Measured on 2026-10-15, no class is empty on either Codex lane, so no hold is expected.
3. **Roll W2 out.**
   - Expect each Codex lane to gain `<id>.advance.json` on the first hourly run, and no moves, because of the
     2026-10-13 stopgap.
   - W2 may reach the fleet before W4. Until W4 lands, the pickers' labels for a moved class are stale (Known
     limits).
   - W2's README names `model-sessions-behind` before W3 ships it, so W2's PR body says so.
4. **Before W3 reaches the fleet,** any running soak gate records its acceptance of the check names
   `model-advance-held-back`, `model-held-behind`, `model-sessions-behind` and `model-advance-blocked`, by name.
5. **Live acceptance (spec §5)** is the stopgap's procedure, run by the code, for the next new model:
   - the hourly refresh canaries the model and moves the class (check `ccrc models <id> show` and the push);
   - a throwaway session on that lane, started only with the operator's go and using `--model <class>`, replies on
     the new id (check its transcript metadata only);
   - `ccrc doctor` shows `model-advance-held-back`, `model-held-behind` and `model-advance-blocked` PASS.
     `model-sessions-behind` may WARN a day after the move for sessions not yet relaunched, and it clears as they
     are relaunched.
6. **The typed-`/model` measurement (D11's fallback), only with the operator's explicit go.**
   - **The test.** Start a throwaway session on the lane before the move, then let the move happen while it is in a
     long turn. Read its transcript metadata at its next turn. If it is still on the old model, type `/model <class>`
     into that throwaway session alone, and read its next turn again.
   - **Timing.** The natural moment is step 5's next new model. A deliberate short re-pin of one class is the other
     choice; it moves that class twice for every session on that lane.
   - **Then.** If the typed step moves the session, it lands with the ccd routing-record change (Later). If it does
     not, sessions move only on relaunch, and that choice goes back to the operator.
7. **Before W4 reaches the fleet,** every Codex lane is `exec.kind: codex` in the server box's roster too. Check it
   from `GET /api/accounts`' `laneKind` after rollout, as W4's whole-branch Step 3 says. A lane read as `other` gets
   no Models button and falls back to alias labels.

## Deviations found

Each entry was issued its number by the ledger allocator. A code comment that cites one of these numbers points here.
"Where" names the tasks that carry it.

### D-5187 — the lane-files lock lives in `~/.ccrc/locks`, not beside the lane's files

Where: Task 4. The lock is `~/.ccrc/locks/models-<id>.lock`, not `~/.ccrc/models/<id>.lock`. Account removal's `<id>.*` glob would list it as a leftover forever. `rm` cannot unlink a lock file safely. The models-dir listings are pinned by tests.

### D-5188 — a pending intent closes the crash gap, for an advance and for a hand `set-class`

Where: Tasks 3, 5, 9, 11 and 14. A `pending` intent is written under the lane-files lock before the registry rename and reconciled by the next locked writer. It closes the crash gap that D21's order leaves, and `previous` and `history` are still written only after materialise succeeds. A hand `set-class` writes one too, `{how: 'hand', class, from, to, emptied, at}`, before its own rename, and records its move by settling that intent through the same reconcile: when the class's pin equals `to`, the move is recorded as `how: hand`, one entry for the named class and one for each class that one-model-one-class emptied and that is still empty, each family rewritten from its pin and cleared when the pin is none or breaks the id grammar (D-5195), `previous` untouched and no `recovered` mark; otherwise the intent is dropped. So a `set-class` cut short between its rename and its history entry never leaves an emptied class with a family the next hour refills it from. A caller that reports recovered moves reads the intent's `how` first and reports a landed hand move as hand, never as an advance (ruling 4).

### D-5189 — `previous` carries the effort level as well as the model

Where: Tasks 3, 6 and 9. `previous` is `{model, effort}`, so a Revert restores an effort level the advance resolved down, instead of leaving the class at a level it never had.

### D-5190 — a hold records the act that set it, hand or revert

Where: Tasks 3, 6 and 19. A hold's "who" is the act that set it (`hand` or `revert`). The agent child's fixed argv and three-name environment carry no caller, so the server's audit line names who tapped, by the device label its gate measured (D-5229).

### D-5191 — held-back also clears when its candidate is no longer the class's candidate

Where: Tasks 3, 14, 15 and 18. `model-advance-held-back` also clears when its candidate is no longer the class's candidate. Otherwise a candidate that left the catalogue would WARN forever.

### D-5192 — a repeated failure updates one history entry

Where: Tasks 3 and 9. A repeated failure of the same move updates one history entry (`tries`, `lastAt`). This is what makes it "one push, not one an hour", and it keeps real moves from being evicted by the cap.

### D-5193 — `model-advance-blocked` names more causes than the spec lists

Where: Tasks 2, 8, 9, 14 and 15. `model-advance-blocked` also names `shared-family`, `lane-not-codex-kind` and `windows-unreadable`, so none of these goes quiet It also names `lock-unwritable` (ruling 8): `advance-health` reports a lane whose lock path is a symlink or anything but a regular file this account can write, or whose lock directory is a symlink, not a directory, another account's, or not writable, measured with `lstat` and `access(W_OK)` only; an absent directory or file is no finding. This closes the gap D-5209 left to W3.

### D-5194 — `model-sessions-behind` names the evidence, not ccd's reason

Where: Tasks 14 and 15. `model-sessions-behind` names the evidence (the last render's model and time, the last turn's start), not "ccd's reason". Under D11's fallback ccd types nothing on a Codex lane, so it records no reason.

### D-5195 — a hand act that empties a class clears its family

Where: Tasks 3, 5 and 15. A hand action that empties a class, or pins an unparseable id, clears its family. Without this the next hour would refill a class the operator emptied. Only `init` and the one-time backfill seed empty classes.

### D-5196 — a stale LiteLLM list waits silently

Where: Task 11. Readiness also requires the on-disk LiteLLM list to be current, so a stale list waits silently instead of failing the canary (§2.3 step 4). It is a lane state, and a failure would push and WARN about a model that is fine.

### D-5197 — a foreign tier, or a tier that cannot be asked, waits silently

Where: Task 11. A foreign tier (2) and a cannot-ask answer (3) from `_codex_tier_ours` wait silently, like down or starting. Doctor's `codex` check already names both.

### D-5198 — only codex-kind lanes advance

Where: Tasks 5, 6, 8, 9, 14 and 18. Only `exec.kind: codex` rows advance. An external-kind row has no tier, port or key known to ccrc.

### D-5199 — no advance, and no retired fallback, on a stale catalogue

Where: Tasks 2 and 8. No advance, and no retired fallback, on a catalogue marked stale. This matches `deriveModels`' rule.

### D-5200 — effort is ranked by the old pin's catalogue row

Where: Tasks 2 and 8. "Below it in the catalogue's own order" is ranked by the old pin's row. With no old row, the new model's lowest level is taken.

### D-5201 — the advance commit refuses without `flock`

Where: Tasks 4 and 11. The advance commit refuses without `flock`. Hand verbs keep today's unserialised behaviour on such a box.

### D-5202 — the Models panel is a sheet on the Accounts screen

Where: Task 20. No per-lane page exists, so the Models panel is a sheet opened from each Codex lane's row on the Accounts screen.

### D-5203 — the models route answers 501 in local mode

Where: Task 19. The models route answers 501 in `CCRC_FLEET=local`, where there is no agent. A local spawn port is Later.

### D-5204 — the lane-files lock has three refusal words, not one

Where: Task 4. The design's §3.4 gave the lane-files lock one refusal word, `lock-busy`. It has three, because the three cases have three remedies and are never folded into one: `lock-busy` (still held when the wait ends), `lock-unwritable` (the lock cannot be used: the file cannot be opened, the directory cannot be made 0700, or the path is a symlink, a FIFO, a directory or anything but a regular file, which is refused before any open so it can never hang one) and `install-incomplete` (the wrapper-shape contract the id check needs is missing). The lock prints nothing itself; each of its two callers prints the one refusal in its own shape.

### D-5205 — no lock where its directory is absent and `mkdir` is not on PATH

Where: Task 4. The design's §3.4 has `_models_lock` degrade to unserialised (rc 0, FD empty) only where `flock` is missing. It also degrades where `~/.ccrc/locks` does not exist yet and `mkdir` is not on PATH. Without this, `ccrc doctor --fix` could not re-render `lane.json` on a PATH that has lost coreutils, the box doctor most needs to work on, and two of `ccrc-doctor.test.ts`'s real-run cases would go red. Once the directory exists, the lock is always taken; W2's advance step checks for this as it checks for `flock`.

### D-5206 — a revert writes its hold before the registry moves

Where: Tasks 6 and 17. The design lists revert's hold last. The revert writes its `{by: 'revert'}` hold to the advance file BEFORE the registry rename, so a revert stopped anywhere, including on a failed materialise that restores the old registry, leaves the class held and never free for the next hour to advance. `previous` and `history` are still written only after materialise succeeds.

### D-5207 — a moved registry that fails validation is a failed advance

Where: Task 9. A moved registry that `parseRegistry` or `modelEnvBlock` refuses is recorded as a failed advance (`canary: passed`, `restored: true`) rather than answered as a refusal, so doctor's held-back check names it instead of the hour failing silently.

### D-5208 — the commit's answer says whether the old pin was restored

Where: Tasks 9 and 11. `advance-commit`'s answer and the refresh event carry `restored` on a failed move after a passed canary; `restored: false` makes the row `ok: false`. Skeleton §3.3 and §3.7 name no such field, and without it a lane whose files no longer match its registry would read `ok: true`

### D-5209 — a commit that never ran its re-check is an abandoned event

Where: Task 11. A commit that never ran its re-check (`lock-busy`, `lock-unwritable`, `install-incomplete`, a node refusal, or no answer) is an `abandoned` event whose `why` is that word; §3.7 lists `why` only for the six re-check reasons. A persistent `lock-unwritable` is not silent: it is on every hourly row and refuses every hand verb on that lane (W1's `_models_answer_locked`), and W3's `model-advance-blocked` reports such a lane with cause `lock-unwritable`, measured read-only (ruling RC7). `no-answer` also covers a commit whose node W1's 10 s `MODELS_NODE_BOUND_S` ended.

### D-5210 — readiness also proves the listener is this lane's shim

Where: Tasks 10 and 11. Readiness also requires `_codex_tier_ours <id> shim` to answer 0, and the canary asks `GET /ccgpt/lane` with no key and sends the keyed request only when the listener answers as this lane, else `unavailable`. Skeleton §3.6 and §3.7 ask only the LiteLLM tier, which would hand the lane key to whatever listens on the shim's port (`ccd/ccgpt-proxy.py`: "a port is only a number")

### D-5211 — `/api/notify` pushes only a well-shaped models line

Where: Task 12. `/api/notify` honours `push: true` only for a line `modelsPushOf` reads (L0, `shared/models.mjs`, at most 300 characters) whose lane is a roster row of `exec.kind: "codex"`; anything else gets the banner and a warning. A box token proves only "a process on the fleet box". Residual, accepted for this plan (ruling RC6) and stated in the code: a box-token holder can still send a well-shaped models line (attribution, not authentication), and a models push gets no feed record and no per-(lane, class) rate cap.

### D-5212 — the push tag names the lane and the class

Where: Task 12. The push tag is `models-advance:<lane>:<class>`, not §3.8's constant `models-advance`: a phone replaces a notification of the same tag (`pwa/public/push-sw.js`), so one tag would let a second move or failure in a run erase the first.

### D-5213 — the advance step runs after every lane's refresh

Where: Task 11. The advance step runs as a second pass after every lane's probe, materialise and LiteLLM render, from the deadline taken once at the arm's start, so a late SIGTERM can only cut an advance short (which `pending` covers) and never a LiteLLM stop and start. Skeleton §3.7 ran it inside each lane's iteration.

### D-5214 — a canary is sent only when the budget still covers it and its commit

Where: Task 11. A canary is sent only when `SECONDS` plus its deadline + 15 (outer bound) + 8 (kill grace ceiling) + the lock wait + the commit's bounded node run (W1's `MODELS_NODE_BOUND_S`, 10, plus its kill grace ceiling, 8) + 5 (the push's `curl -m 5`) is within the deadline: 156 s by default, replacing §3.7's `+ 20`, which let the last commit and push run past the budget. `_models_lock`'s wait clamp moves into `_models_lock_secs`, read by both.

### D-5215 — `advance-backfill` also settles a pending intent, every hour

Where: Tasks 9 and 11. `advance-backfill`, the hourly step's first locked writer, also settles a pending intent in a file that exists (W1's op only created). Without it, after a crash gap the moved class has no candidate, no commit runs, and the move never gets a history entry or a `previous`, so Revert cannot undo it.

### D-5216 — a recovered advance is reported and pushed once

Where: Tasks 9 and 11. `advance-backfill`'s and `advance-commit`'s answers carry `recoveredMove: {class, from, to, how}` when a settled intent had landed. An automatic advance's (`how: 'advance'`) is reported by the step as a `moved` event marked `recovered`, with that move's one push (§2.3 step 5). A hand set-class's (`how: 'hand'`, W1's intent under D-5188) is reported as hand, never as an advance (ruling RC3): no event and no push, and the commit's `recovered` stays false, matching the history entry, which carries no `recovered` mark.

### D-5217 — a move whose old registry cannot be put back keeps its intent

Where: Task 9. When the previous registry cannot be written back after a failed materialise, the failure is recorded and the intent KEPT (§3.3 step 9 clears it): the registry does pin the new model, so the next locked writer records the move as landed once the next refresh has re-materialised the lane.

### D-5218 — the canary's own `bad-argv` reads as unavailable

Where: Task 11. `_models_canary` reads the canary's own `bad-argv` as `unavailable` (silent), not as §3.6's "no answer → failed", so a value the canary cannot carry never records a failed advance or pushes about a model that is fine.

### D-5219 — `advance-health` takes the session-registry and lock paths from bash

Where: Tasks 14 and 15. `advance-health` takes `--reg` (the session registry) and `--lock-template` (the lane-files lock path with `{id}` in place of the lane) from its bash caller, both required; skeleton §3.5 gives it `--file` only. `ccd/ccrc` spells the session registry once (`_SVC_REG`) and the lock path once (`_models_lock_path`, pinned by `single-definition.test.ts`), so node takes both rather than spelling a second copy.

### D-5220 — `advance-health`'s answer carries fields the design does not show

Where: Tasks 14 and 15. The answer carries fields §3.9 does not show: `canary` on each `heldBack` entry, so the WARN says whether the canary or the move failed, as §3.8's two push messages do; `reason` on each `heldBehind` entry (`chooseCandidate`'s `newer`, `retired` or `empty`), so a held class whose pin left the catalogue is not called "behind a newer model" when its fallback may be older; a top-level `sessions` word (`read`, `absent`, `unreadable`), so a session registry that cannot be listed is a SKIP of `model-sessions-behind`, never a PASS that measured nothing; and `sessionsUnmeasured`, at the top level for a session whose `.wrapper` cannot be read (`wrapper-unreadable`) and on each lane for a session of it that could not be judged (`advance-file-unreadable`, `marker-absent`, `marker-unreadable`, `sidecar-absent`, `sidecar-unreadable`), which `model-sessions-behind` counts by why on its PASS line and every WARN line, so no verdict stands over sessions nobody read (D-4052's rule for the `codex` check). Under ruling RC1 this check is the only backstop, and a lane whose homes write no sidecar would otherwise PASS without one session measured.

### D-5221 — a held class is never held-back

Where: Tasks 14 and 15. A held class is never `model-advance-held-back`; with a newer model it is `model-held-behind`. Spec §2.8 clears held-back only when an advance succeeds, but a hold stops the hourly retries (§3.9's own remedy says so), so held-back's "the next hourly refresh retries it" would be false and the class would WARN twice.

### D-5222 — sessions-behind judges every model a move replaced

Where: Task 14. `sessionBehind` judges, per class, the newest SUCCESSFUL history entry whose `from` is the session's model, not only the class's newest move (§3.9's "the lane's newest ok move M"). With only the newest move, a session two moves behind would never be reported once a second move followed within a day: the backstop would go quiet.

### D-5223 — the relaunch remedy is `ccd stop`, then `ccd start`

Where: Task 15. `model-sessions-behind`'s remedy names `ccd stop <id>` then `ccd start <id>`, the relaunch ccd has, to run once the session is idle (`cmd_stop` kills the pane, and a turn in flight with it), and says a running session does not always pick up a re-pin by itself (ruling RC1). It promises no pins: the one-argument `start` resumes the conversation, but a respawn carries `--model <class>` only when the routing record holds a class, so a session with none may come back on its old model (spec §2.5 item 5), and the remedy says so. §3.9's `'ccd restart <id>'` names a verb ccd does not have, and its "should move at its next turn" is the D11 claim Task 1 measured false. The PWA's "Restart session" adopts a running pane and relaunches nothing, so the remedy names the shell pair alone.

### D-5224 — each check bounds `advance-health` by doctor's existing timeout

Where: Task 15. Each check bounds its one `advance-health` run by `CCRC_DOCTOR_GH_TIMEOUT` (15 s by default), the knob `_check_history` already reuses for its own node read, and spells the command as node's own. §3.9's `_plat_timeout 20 _models_node …` cannot run: `_plat_timeout` runs a program, never a shell function. A new knob would also have to join every suite's knob-deletion array.

### D-5225 — `model-advance-blocked`'s remedy has one clause per cause

Where: Task 15. `model-advance-blocked`'s remedy has one clause per cause the lane's findings name (eight clauses, two of them shared by two words), not §3.9's one sentence. That sentence sends an unreadable advance file to `ccrc models <id> rm` then `init codex`, which reaps the registry too and resets every pin; the advance-file clause says to repair that file alone, and that removing it instead loses its holds and history and lets the next hourly refresh seed and fill every empty class again (a fresh file comes from the backfill), so each class that must stay put is held at once (Review Focus line 3, D-5195). The lock clause names every shape `lock-unwritable` reports, the RC7-letter one included.

### D-5226 — a ccrc with no `models` verb is a named 501

Where: Tasks 16 and 19. A `no-answer` whose detail is exactly `ccrc: unknown argument: models` (`_ccrc_usage_die`'s line from a `ccrc` with no `models` verb at all) is `501 verb-missing`, beside the skeleton's `unknown-subcommand` arm. Without it an older fleet box reads as a `502` fault rather than the named hold Review Focus line 5 asks for. Exact equality, so `models-x` is never read as it.

### D-5227 — the op's child PATH starts with the agent's own node

Where: Task 17. The child's environment keeps exactly `{HOME, PATH, LANG}`, with the directory of the `node` running the agent first on `PATH`. `ccrc models` runs `deploy/models-op.mjs` under `node`, and a user unit's `PATH` may name none, which would make every Models tap a `no-answer` on a box whose agent is itself a working `node`

### D-5228 — the view tells an older ccrc's silence from an empty advance file

Where: Task 18. The view's `advanceState` has a fifth value, `unreported` (a `show` answer with no `advance` key, which only a `ccrc` from before the advance file sends), and the view carries `advanceDetail`. Folding the first into `absent` would tell the operator "nothing recorded yet" when the remedy is "update the fleet box".

### D-5229 — the audit line names the device, never a session id

Where: Task 19. The audit line names the session by the device label the gate measured (`deviceActor`, `device:<label>` or `unmeasured`), not by a session id: a session's id is its cookie, a credential, and the skeleton's `by session <sid>` would write one into the server's log.

### D-5230 — the route's decisions live in an L1 policy file

Where: Task 19. A third server file beyond the skeleton's two: `server/src/models/policy.ts` (L1, imports `shared/` only) declares the link's result vocabulary and every route verdict (`outcomeOf`, `parseActBody`, `NOT_CONFIGURED`, `badLane`), so `routes.ts` (L4) applies verdicts and decides nothing, as CLAUDE.md's rings require and as the token and docs surfaces' own `policy.ts` files already do.
